# Identifiability API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

The module `commol.identifiability`: the identifiability methods, the report they return, and its parts. Guide: [Identifiability](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/identifiability/index.md).

## StructuralRank

Bases: `IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]`, `RangeChecked`

Structural identifiability, local and numerical: the rank of the scaled sensitivities at random points inside the bounds.

The sensitivities come from finite differences, with a step and an error set by the accuracy of the engine; a singular value counts when it is above the norm of that error. The engine must be deterministic. The points come from the seed of the calibrator, `Calibrator.seed`.

Attributes:

| Name     | Type  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `points` | `int` | How many rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds, at least 1.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `design` | `str` | "observations": the positions and outputs of the observations, their values ignored (can this design determine the parameters?). "dense": every observed series at every unit position up to the last observation (can denser data of these series?). |

Source code in `commol/identifiability/methods.py`

```python
class StructuralRank(IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport], RangeChecked):
    """
    Structural identifiability, local and numerical: the rank of the scaled
    sensitivities at random points inside the bounds.

    The sensitivities come from finite differences, with a step and an error
    set by the accuracy of the engine; a singular value counts when it is
    above the norm of that error. The engine must be deterministic. The
    points come from the seed of the calibrator, ``Calibrator.seed``.

    Attributes
    ----------
    points : int
        How many rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds, at least 1.
    design : str
        ``"observations"``: the positions and outputs of the observations,
        their values ignored (can this design determine the parameters?).
        ``"dense"``: every observed series at every unit position up to the
        last observation (can denser data of these series?).
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_structural_rank)

    points: int = Field()
    design: StructuralDesign
```

## Collinearity

Bases: `IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]`, `RangeChecked`

Collinearity analysis after Brun et al. (2001): the sensitivity measure of each parameter and the collinearity index of each subset.

The index of a subset is 1 when its sensitivities are orthogonal and grows without bound as they approach linear dependence. The literature puts the threshold between 5 and 20. The engine must be deterministic.

Attributes:

| Name              | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `at`              | \`CalibrationResult | ParameterSample\`                                                                                                                                         |
| `max_subset_size` | `int`               | The largest subset, at least 2 and at most the number of parameters. Every subset up to 6 parameters is evaluated; a greedy search adds parameters above. |
| `threshold`       | `float`             | The index below which a subset can be fitted together. No default: it is a modelling judgment.                                                            |

Source code in `commol/identifiability/methods.py`

```python
class Collinearity(IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport], RangeChecked):
    """
    Collinearity analysis after Brun et al. (2001): the sensitivity measure
    of each parameter and the collinearity index of each subset.

    The index of a subset is 1 when its sensitivities are orthogonal and grows
    without bound as they approach linear dependence. The literature puts the
    threshold between 5 and 20. The engine must be deterministic.

    Attributes
    ----------
    at : CalibrationResult | ParameterSample
        Where to evaluate: the best point of a fit, or each draw of a sample,
        summarized by the weighted median.
    max_subset_size : int
        The largest subset, at least 2 and at most the number of parameters.
        Every subset up to 6 parameters is evaluated; a greedy search adds
        parameters above.
    threshold : float
        The index below which a subset can be fitted together. No default:
        it is a modelling judgment.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_collinearity)

    _engine_handles: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("at",)

    at: CalibrationResult | ParameterSample
    max_subset_size: int
    threshold: float = Field()
```

## SampleIdentifiability

Bases: `IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]`, `RangeChecked`

Practical identifiability from any parameter sample: how much it contracts each parameter, which parameters move together, and which marginals have several modes.

Attributes:

| Name                    | Type              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sample`                | `ParameterSample` | The sample, such as the draws of an uncertainty method.                                                                                                                                            |
| `reference`             | `{bounds, prior}` | The distribution the contraction compares with: "bounds", the uniform distribution on the bounds, or "prior", the prior of each parameter in priors, such as the priors the sample was drawn with. |
| `correlation_threshold` | `float`           | The absolute correlation above which a pair is listed and its parameters are poorly determined, strictly between 0 and 1. No default: it is a modelling judgment.                                  |
| `priors`                | \`Priors          | dict[str, distribution]                                                                                                                                                                            |

Source code in `commol/identifiability/methods.py`

```python
class SampleIdentifiability(IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport], RangeChecked):
    """
    Practical identifiability from any parameter sample: how much it contracts
    each parameter, which parameters move together, and which marginals have
    several modes.

    Attributes
    ----------
    sample : ParameterSample
        The sample, such as the draws of an uncertainty method.
    reference : {"bounds", "prior"}
        The distribution the contraction compares with: ``"bounds"``, the
        uniform distribution on the bounds, or ``"prior"``, the prior of each
        parameter in `priors`, such as the priors the sample was drawn with.
    correlation_threshold : float
        The absolute correlation above which a pair is listed and its
        parameters are poorly determined, strictly between 0 and 1. No
        default: it is a modelling judgment.
    priors : Priors | dict[str, distribution] | None
        The prior of each parameter, with ``reference="prior"`` only.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_sample_identifiability)

    _engine_handles: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("sample",)

    sample: ParameterSample
    reference: SampleReference
    correlation_threshold: float
    priors: Priors | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _read_priors(cls, data: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
        """Read a mapping of parameter to distribution as `Priors`."""
        if isinstance(data, Mapping) and data.get("priors") is not None:
            return {**data, "priors": coerce_priors(data["priors"])}
        return data

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_priors(self) -> Self:
        """The priors go with ``reference="prior"``, and only with it."""
        if self.reference == "prior" and self.priors is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "reference='prior' needs priors: the prior of each parameter."
            )
        if self.reference == "bounds" and self.priors is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "priors are read only with reference='prior'; with "
                "reference='bounds' leave them out."
            )
        return self
```

## ProfileIdentifiability

Bases: `IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]`

Identifiability from the profiles of a `ProfileLikelihood`: the verdict of the shape of each profile, with a `profile` section.

`identifiable` gives the practical verdict `determined` and `practically_non_identifiable` the practical verdict `poorly_determined`. `structurally_non_identifiable` gives the structural verdict of its `structure`, `in_combination` or `non_identifiable`, with no combination: the reason names the compensating parameters. A flat profile with no structural verdict gives the practical verdict `poorly_determined`. Every reason says that the verdict holds with the other parameters at their fitted values. A parameter with no profile, or no verdict, gets neither.

Attributes:

| Name     | Type            | Description                                                 |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `result` | `ProfileResult` | The profiles of the parameters of this calibration problem. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                                    |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If the result holds prediction profiles, which have no verdict on a parameter. |

Source code in `commol/identifiability/methods.py`

```python
class ProfileIdentifiability(IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]):
    """
    Identifiability from the profiles of a `ProfileLikelihood`: the verdict
    of the shape of each profile, with a ``profile`` section.

    ``identifiable`` gives the practical verdict ``determined`` and
    ``practically_non_identifiable`` the practical verdict
    ``poorly_determined``. ``structurally_non_identifiable`` gives the
    structural verdict of its `structure`, ``in_combination`` or
    ``non_identifiable``, with no combination: the reason names the
    compensating parameters. A flat profile with no structural verdict gives
    the practical verdict ``poorly_determined``. Every reason says that the
    verdict holds with the other parameters at their fitted values. A
    parameter with no profile, or no verdict, gets neither.

    Attributes
    ----------
    result : ProfileResult
        The profiles of the parameters of this calibration problem.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the result holds prediction profiles, which have no verdict on a
        parameter.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_profile_identifiability)

    result: ProfileResult

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _parameter_profiles(self) -> Self:
        if self.result.quantity != "parameter":
            raise ValueError(
                "This result holds the profiles of predictions, and predictions "
                "have no verdict on a parameter; profile the parameters "
                "(ProfileLikelihood) for their identifiability."
            )
        return self
```

## IdentifiabilityReport

Bases: `_FrozenResult`

Which parameters the model and the data determine: one structural and one practical verdict per parameter, and the evidence of each method.

The structural verdict comes from `StructuralRank` on the design of the observations, and from a flat profile; a dense design answers what denser data would determine, so its verdicts stay in its section. The practical verdict comes from `Collinearity`, `SampleIdentifiability`, `StartsIdentifiability` and the other profiles.

Attributes:

| Name                                                | Type                           | Description                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `parameters`                                        | `list[str]`                    | The parameters, in problem order.                  |
| `verdicts`                                          | `dict[str, ParameterVerdicts]` | The verdicts of each parameter.                    |
| `structural, collinearity, sample, starts, profile` | `list`                         | The sections of the methods that ran, one per run. |

Source code in `commol/identifiability/results.py`

```python
class IdentifiabilityReport(_FrozenResult):
    """
    Which parameters the model and the data determine: one structural and one
    practical verdict per parameter, and the evidence of each method.

    The structural verdict comes from `StructuralRank` on the design of the
    observations, and from a flat profile; a dense design answers what
    denser data would determine, so its verdicts stay in its section. The
    practical verdict comes from `Collinearity`, `SampleIdentifiability`,
    `StartsIdentifiability` and the other profiles.

    Attributes
    ----------
    parameters : list[str]
        The parameters, in problem order.
    verdicts : dict[str, ParameterVerdicts]
        The verdicts of each parameter.
    structural, collinearity, sample, starts, profile : list
        The sections of the methods that ran, one per run.
    """

    parameters: list[str]
    verdicts: dict[str, ParameterVerdicts]
    structural: list[StructuralSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    collinearity: list[CollinearitySection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    sample: list[SampleSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    starts: list[StartsSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    profile: list[ProfileSection] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_parameters(self) -> Self:
        """Check that the verdicts hold the parameters, in order."""
        if list(self.verdicts) != self.parameters:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The verdicts must hold the parameters {self.parameters} in "
                f"order, got {list(self.verdicts)}."
            )
        return self

    def report(self) -> IdentifiabilityReportData:
        """
        Report the identifiability of each parameter as plain data.

        Returns
        -------
        IdentifiabilityReportData
            ``parameters``: each parameter, in problem order, with its
            structural and practical verdicts; ``sections``: the evidence of
            each method that ran.
        """
        return identifiability_report(self)

    def merge(self, *others: "IdentifiabilityReport") -> "IdentifiabilityReport":
        """
        Join this report with others of the same parameters.

        The sections are kept side by side. A verdict that the reports agree
        on stays, with the reasons of each; one they disagree on is
        ``conflicting``, with every reason.

        Parameters
        ----------
        *others : IdentifiabilityReport
            The reports to join.

        Returns
        -------
        IdentifiabilityReport
            The joined report.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a report has other parameters.
        """
        reports = [self, *others]
        for other in others:
            if other.parameters != self.parameters:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Reports of different parameters cannot merge: "
                    f"{self.parameters} and {other.parameters}."
                )
        verdicts = {
            name: ParameterVerdicts(
                structural=_merge_structural(
                    [
                        v
                        for r in reports
                        if (v := r.verdicts[name].structural) is not None
                    ]
                ),
                practical=_merge_practical(
                    [
                        v
                        for r in reports
                        if (v := r.verdicts[name].practical) is not None
                    ]
                ),
            )
            for name in self.parameters
        }
        return IdentifiabilityReport(
            parameters=self.parameters,
            verdicts=verdicts,
            structural=[s for r in reports for s in r.structural],
            collinearity=[s for r in reports for s in r.collinearity],
            sample=[s for r in reports for s in r.sample],
            starts=[s for r in reports for s in r.starts],
            profile=[s for r in reports for s in r.profile],
        )
```

# Local Approximations API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

The module `commol.local`: the Laplace approximation, the sandwich, the Laplace mixture, and their results. Guide: [Local Approximations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/local/index.md).

## Laplace

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[LaplaceResult]`, `RangeChecked`

The Laplace approximation of the problem's observation models: the normal `N(θ̂, H⁻¹)` on the unbounded scale of the parameters, centred on the fit, with `H` the curvature of `−log L` there.

It needs `observation_models`: a loss has no noise scale, so its curvature is no inverse variance (use `Sandwich`). A fit on a bound of its parameter is refused: on the unbounded scale its variance is infinite there.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type                      | Description                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `draws`     | `int`                     | Number of draws of the normal, at least 1.                                                        |
| `curvature` | `{gauss_newton, hessian}` | The curvature (default "gauss_newton").                                                           |
| `starts`    | `int`                     | Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds. |

Source code in `commol/local/methods.py`

```python
class Laplace(UncertaintyMethod[LaplaceResult], RangeChecked):
    """
    The Laplace approximation of the problem's observation models: the normal
    ``N(θ̂, H⁻¹)`` on the unbounded scale of the parameters, centred on the
    fit, with ``H`` the curvature of ``−log L`` there.

    It needs ``observation_models``: a loss has no noise scale, so its
    curvature is no inverse variance (use `Sandwich`). A fit on a bound of
    its parameter is refused: on the unbounded scale its variance is
    infinite there.

    Attributes
    ----------
    draws : int
        Number of draws of the normal, at least 1.
    curvature : {"gauss_newton", "hessian"}
        The curvature (default ``"gauss_newton"``).
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin
        hypercube over the bounds.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_laplace)

    draws: int = Field(description="Number of draws.")
    curvature: Literal["gauss_newton", "hessian"] = Field(
        default="gauss_newton", description="The curvature."
    )
    starts: int = Field(default=1, description="Starts of the fit.")
```

## Sandwich

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[SandwichResult]`, `RangeChecked`

The sandwich covariance `H⁻¹ B H⁻¹` at the fit, with the meat `B` summed over blocks of positions (the clustered estimator CR1): `B = G/(G − 1) · Σ_b s_b s_bᵀ`, with `s_b` the sum of the gradients of the terms of the observations of block `b`.

It needs no noise model: with a loss, `H` is the curvature of the loss; with observation models, of `−log L`. It holds when the noise depends on its neighbours inside a block, when its size changes, and when the noise model is wrong but the mean is right. Intervals and draws read a Student t with `G − 1` degrees of freedom; with `G` blocks not above the parameters it is refused, since `B` would have rank below them. `loss_function="mae"` is refused: its sandwich needs a density of the residuals at 0 and a bandwidth (use a bootstrap).

Attributes:

| Name           | Type                      | Description                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `block_length` | \`int                     | auto\`                                                                                                      |
| `draws`        | `int`                     | Number of draws of the Student t, at least 1.                                                               |
| `curvature`    | `{gauss_newton, hessian}` | The curvature H (default "gauss_newton"). With the Hessian, the sandwich also holds when the mean is wrong. |
| `starts`       | `int`                     | Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds.           |

Source code in `commol/local/methods.py`

```python
class Sandwich(UncertaintyMethod[SandwichResult], RangeChecked):
    """
    The sandwich covariance ``H⁻¹ B H⁻¹`` at the fit, with the meat ``B``
    summed over blocks of positions (the clustered estimator CR1):
    ``B = G/(G − 1) · Σ_b s_b s_bᵀ``, with ``s_b`` the sum of the gradients
    of the terms of the observations of block ``b``.

    It needs no noise model: with a loss, ``H`` is the curvature of the loss;
    with observation models, of ``−log L``. It holds when the noise depends
    on its neighbours inside a block, when its size changes, and when the
    noise model is wrong but the mean is right. Intervals and draws read a
    Student t with ``G − 1`` degrees of freedom; with ``G`` blocks not above
    the parameters it is refused, since ``B`` would have rank below them.
    ``loss_function="mae"`` is refused: its sandwich needs a density of the
    residuals at 0 and a bandwidth (use a bootstrap).

    Attributes
    ----------
    block_length : int | "auto"
        Positions per block; ``"auto"`` is the rule of Politis and White
        (2004) for non-overlapping blocks on the residuals of the fit.
    draws : int
        Number of draws of the Student t, at least 1.
    curvature : {"gauss_newton", "hessian"}
        The curvature ``H`` (default ``"gauss_newton"``). With the Hessian,
        the sandwich also holds when the mean is wrong.
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin
        hypercube over the bounds.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_sandwich)

    block_length: int | Literal["auto"] = Field(description="Positions per block.")
    draws: int = Field(description="Number of draws.")
    curvature: Literal["gauss_newton", "hessian"] = Field(
        default="gauss_newton", description="The curvature."
    )
    starts: int = Field(default=1, description="Starts of the fit.")
```

## LaplaceMixture

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[ImportanceResult]`, `RangeChecked`

The Laplace mixture: a Laplace approximation at each distinct optimum of a multi-start fit, weighted by its Laplace evidence, as the proposal of importance sampling of a posterior, with the largest weights smoothed (Pareto-smoothed importance sampling, Vehtari et al. 2024).

The ends of the starts merge into a component when they are closer than one Mahalanobis unit to it. Every draw is weighted by the target over the mixture, on the unbounded scale. `k_hat` says whether the mixture covers the target: above 0.7 the sample is marked unreliable.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type                      | Description                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `starts`    | `int`                     | Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds. |
| `draws`     | `int`                     | Number of draws of the mixture, at least 25, so that the tail of the weights has 5.               |
| `target`    | \`LikelihoodTarget        | GibbsTarget\`                                                                                     |
| `curvature` | `{gauss_newton, hessian}` | The curvature of each component (default "gauss_newton").                                         |

Source code in `commol/local/methods.py`

```python
class LaplaceMixture(UncertaintyMethod[ImportanceResult], RangeChecked):
    """
    The Laplace mixture: a Laplace approximation at each distinct optimum of
    a multi-start fit, weighted by its Laplace evidence, as the proposal of
    importance sampling of a posterior, with the largest weights smoothed
    (Pareto-smoothed importance sampling, Vehtari et al. 2024).

    The ends of the starts merge into a component when they are closer than
    one Mahalanobis unit to it. Every draw is weighted by the target over
    the mixture, on the unbounded scale. ``k_hat`` says whether the mixture
    covers the target: above 0.7 the sample is marked unreliable.

    Attributes
    ----------
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1): the initial guess, then rows of a Latin
        hypercube over the bounds.
    draws : int
        Number of draws of the mixture, at least 25, so that the tail of the
        weights has 5.
    target : LikelihoodTarget | GibbsTarget
        The posterior of the observation models with priors, or the Gibbs
        posterior of the loss with priors and ``eta``.
    curvature : {"gauss_newton", "hessian"}
        The curvature of each component (default ``"gauss_newton"``).
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_laplace_mixture)

    starts: int = Field(default=1, description="Starts of the fit.")
    draws: int = Field(description="Number of draws.")
    target: _MixtureTarget = Field(description="The posterior to sample.")
    curvature: Literal["gauss_newton", "hessian"] = Field(
        default="gauss_newton", description="The curvature."
    )
```

## LocalResult

Bases: `ResultModel`

What every local approximation returns: a distribution on the unbounded scale of the parameters, centred on the fit.

Attributes:

| Name         | Type                | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fit`        | `CalibrationResult` | The fit the approximation is centred on: Calibrator.run(starts).                                                       |
| `covariance` | `list[list[float]]` | The covariance of the distribution on the unbounded scale of the parameters, in the order of the problem's parameters. |
| `sample`     | `ParameterSample`   | Draws of the distribution, mapped back to the parameters, with equal weights.                                          |
| `notes`      | `list[str]`         | The entries of the curvature whose estimated error is not small against their scale; each is also logged as a warning. |

Source code in `commol/local/results.py`

```python
class LocalResult(ResultModel):
    """
    What every local approximation returns: a distribution on the unbounded
    scale of the parameters, centred on the fit.

    Attributes
    ----------
    fit : CalibrationResult
        The fit the approximation is centred on: ``Calibrator.run(starts)``.
    covariance : list[list[float]]
        The covariance of the distribution on the unbounded scale of the
        parameters, in the order of the problem's parameters.
    sample : ParameterSample
        Draws of the distribution, mapped back to the parameters, with equal
        weights.
    notes : list[str]
        The entries of the curvature whose estimated error is not small
        against their scale; each is also logged as a warning.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    fit: CalibrationResult
    covariance: list[list[float]]
    sample: ParameterSample
    notes: list[str]

    def degrees_of_freedom(self) -> float | None:
        """
        The degrees of freedom of the distribution.

        Returns
        -------
        float | None
            Those of a Student t, or None for a normal.
        """
        return None

    def delta_band(
        self,
        calibrator: CalibrationPort,
        positions: Sequence[float],
        confidence_level: float,
    ) -> DeltaBand:
        """
        The band of every output of this approximation by the delta method.

        The model is linearized at the fit: the variance of an output is
        ``J Σ Jᵀ``, with ``J`` its derivatives on the unbounded scale and
        ``Σ`` the covariance of this result. The band is the prediction at
        the fit plus and minus the quantile of a normal, or of the Student t
        of a `SandwichResult`, times its standard deviation. It runs the
        model a few times per parameter, not once per draw, and reads only
        the fields of this result, so a result read back from JSON works.

        Parameters
        ----------
        calibrator : Calibrator
            The calibrator of the problem this approximation is of.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions to report at.
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        DeltaBand
            The prediction at the fit and the ends of the interval of each
            output at each position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the parameters of this result are not those of the problem,
            the level is not strictly between 0 and 1, the engine is
            stochastic, or the engine rejects a position.
        RuntimeError
            If the derivatives fail at the fit.
        """
        names = calibrator.parameter_names
        if self.sample.names != names:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The result has the parameters {self.sample.names}; the problem "
                f"has {names}."
            )
        points = [float(position) for position in positions]
        outputs, center, lower, upper = commol_rs.inference.delta_band(
            calibrator._engine_problem,
            [self.fit.best_parameters[name] for name in names],
            self.covariance,
            self.degrees_of_freedom(),
            points,
            confidence_level,
        )
        return DeltaBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=points,
            center=by_output(outputs, center),
            lower=by_output(outputs, lower),
            upper=by_output(outputs, upper),
        )
```

```python
    positions: Sequence[float],

    ``J Σ Jᵀ``, with ``J`` its derivatives on the unbounded scale and

    the fit plus and minus the quantile of a normal, or of the Student t

    Returns
    -------

        The prediction at the fit and the ends of the interval of each
        output at each position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the parameters of this result are not those of the problem,
        the level is not strictly between 0 and 1, the engine is
        stochastic, or the engine rejects a position.
    RuntimeError
        If the derivatives fail at the fit.
    """
    names = calibrator.parameter_names
    if self.sample.names != names:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The result has the parameters {self.sample.names}; the problem "
            f"has {names}."
        )
    points = [float(position) for position in positions]
    outputs, center, lower, upper = commol_rs.inference.delta_band(
        calibrator._engine_problem,
        [self.fit.best_parameters[name] for name in names],
        self.covariance,
        self.degrees_of_freedom(),
        points,
        confidence_level,
    )
    return DeltaBand(
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        positions=points,
        center=by_output(outputs, center),
        lower=by_output(outputs, lower),
        upper=by_output(outputs, upper),
    )
```

## SandwichResult

Bases: `LocalResult`

The result of a sandwich: a Student t on the unbounded scale of the parameters, centred on the fit, of covariance `H⁻¹ B H⁻¹` and `blocks − 1` degrees of freedom.

Attributes:

| Name                     | Type                | Description                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `fit`                    | `CalibrationResult` | The fit the sandwich is centred on: Calibrator.run(starts).                          |
| `covariance`             | `list[list[float]]` | H⁻¹ B H⁻¹ on the unbounded scale of the parameters.                                  |
| `sample`                 | `ParameterSample`   | Draws of the Student t, mapped back to the parameters, with equal weights.           |
| `notes`                  | `list[str]`         | The entries of the curvature whose estimated error is not small against their scale. |
| `blocks`                 | `int`               | The number of blocks G; intervals read a Student t with G − 1 degrees of freedom.    |
| `block_length`           | `int`               | The positions per block.                                                             |
| `block_length_estimates` | \`dict[str, float]  | None\`                                                                               |

Source code in `commol/local/results.py`

```python
class SandwichResult(LocalResult):
    """
    The result of a sandwich: a Student t on the unbounded scale of the
    parameters, centred on the fit, of covariance ``H⁻¹ B H⁻¹`` and
    ``blocks − 1`` degrees of freedom.

    Attributes
    ----------
    fit : CalibrationResult
        The fit the sandwich is centred on: ``Calibrator.run(starts)``.
    covariance : list[list[float]]
        ``H⁻¹ B H⁻¹`` on the unbounded scale of the parameters.
    sample : ParameterSample
        Draws of the Student t, mapped back to the parameters, with equal
        weights.
    notes : list[str]
        The entries of the curvature whose estimated error is not small
        against their scale.
    blocks : int
        The number of blocks ``G``; intervals read a Student t with
        ``G − 1`` degrees of freedom.
    block_length : int
        The positions per block.
    block_length_estimates : dict[str, float] | None
        With ``block_length="auto"``, the estimate of each series, by label;
        otherwise None.
    """

    blocks: int
    block_length: int
    block_length_estimates: dict[str, float] | None

    def degrees_of_freedom(self) -> float | None:
        """
        The degrees of freedom of the Student t.

        Returns
        -------
        float | None
            ``blocks − 1``.
        """
        return float(self.blocks - 1)
```

## ImportanceResult

Bases: `ResultModel`

The result of a Laplace mixture: draws of the mixture weighted by the target over the mixture, smoothed by Pareto-smoothed importance sampling.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                     | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fit`            | `CalibrationResult`      | The multi-start fit whose ends made the components: Calibrator.run(starts).                                                      |

| `components`     | `list[MixtureComponent]` | The components, in order of their objective.                                                                                     |
| `k_hat`          | `float`                  | The Pareto shape of the tail of the weights. Up to 0.5 the weights have a finite variance; above 0.7 the estimate is unreliable. |
| `effective_size` | `float`                  | Kish's effective size of the smoothed weights.                                                                                   |
| `reliable`       | `bool`                   | Whether k_hat is at most 0.7. An unreliable sample is also logged as a warning.                                                  |
| `notes`          | `list[str]`              | Ends that gave no component, and an unreliable sample, in words.                                                                 |

Source code in `commol/local/results.py`

# ModelBuilder API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

Builds a `Model`. A `StratificationCondition` selects the compartments of a category, and a `StratifiedRate` gives a transition its rate in the compartments that match its conditions. Guide: [Building Models](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/building-models/index.md), [Transitions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/transitions/index.md).

## ModelBuilder

A fluent interface that writes the process of a model, once.

The builder adds bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions and parameters: the process, which is the same for every kind of model. `build` joins it with a structure, which lays the process out (such as `Aggregate`, amounts per compartment), and an engine, which runs it. Each method that adds returns the builder, so the calls chain.

Source code in `commol/_model/builder.py`

```python
class ModelBuilder:
    """
    A fluent interface that writes the process of a model, once.

    The builder adds bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions and
    parameters: the process, which is the same for every kind of model.
    `build` joins it with a structure, which lays the process out (such as
    `Aggregate`, amounts per compartment), and an engine, which runs it.
    Each method that adds returns the builder, so the calls chain.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str | None = None,
        version: str | None = None,
        bin_unit: str | None = None,
        step_unit: str | None = None,
        origin: date | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the ModelBuilder.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name : str
            The unique name that identifies the model.
        description : str | None, default=None
            A human-readable description of the model's purpose and function.
        version : str | None, default=None
            The version number of the model.
        bin_unit : str | None, default=None
            The default unit for all bins.
            Individual bins can override this with their own unit parameter.
            Units are optional but required for model.check_unit_consistency().
        step_unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of one step on the axis, of any single dimension (for example
            ``"day"`` or ``"meter"``). The unit check requires every flow to be
            ``<bin unit>/<step_unit>``, and ``Model.axis_units()`` converts
            values to steps of it. None means ``step``, the default increment
            of any axis.
        origin : date | None, default=None
            Calendar moment of position 0: a `datetime.datetime` with no time
            zone, or a `datetime.date`, read as its midnight. With it,
            ``Model.axis_units()`` converts between dates and positions, and
            ``results.plot.series()`` labels its ticks with dates. It
            needs a ``step_unit`` of time whose length is a whole number of
            days or a whole fraction of a day, such as ``"hour"`` or
            ``"day"``; `build` raises ``ValueError`` otherwise, or for a
            moment with a time zone.
        """
        self._name: str = name
        self._description: str | None = description
        self._version: str | None = version
        self._bin_unit: str | None = bin_unit
        self._step_unit: str | None = step_unit
        self._origin: date | None = origin

        self._bins: list[Bin] = []
        self._accumulators: list[Accumulator] = []
        self._stratifications: list[Stratification] = []
        self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
        self._parameters: list[Parameter] = []
        self._series_counter: int = 0

        logger.info(
            (
                f"Initialized ModelBuilder: name='{self._name}', "
                f"version='{self._version or 'N/A'}'"
            )
        )

    def add_bin(self, id: str, name: str, unit: str | None = None) -> Self:
        """
        Add a bin to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the bin.
        name : str
            Human-readable name for the bin.
        unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of measurement for this bin. If None, uses the model-level bin_unit.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.
        """
        # Use bin-specific unit, or fall back to model-level bin_unit
        final_unit = unit if unit is not None else self._bin_unit
        self._bins.append(Bin(id=id, name=name, unit=final_unit))
        logger.info(f"Added bin: id='{id}', name='{name}', unit='{final_unit}'")
        return self

    def add_accumulator(self, id: str, name: str) -> Self:
        """
        Add an accumulator: a cumulative event counter in the model outputs.

        A transition adds its flow to the accumulators it names
        (``add_transition(accumulators=...)``). An accumulator is an output,
        not a part of the state, so ``total`` leaves it out.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the accumulator. It names its output, which
            stratifications expand as they expand a bin (``acc_g1``,
            ``acc_g2``).
        name : str
            Human-readable name for the accumulator.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.
        """
        self._accumulators.append(Accumulator(id=id, name=name))
        logger.info(f"Added accumulator: id='{id}', name='{name}'")
        return self

    def add_stratification(
        self,
        id: str,
        categories: list[str],
        description: str | None = None,
        conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a stratification to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the stratification.
        categories : list[str]
            list of category identifiers within this stratification.
        description : str | None, default=None
            Human-readable description of the stratification.
        conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None, default=None
            When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
            already-applied categories satisfy ALL conditions. Each condition
            names a stratification declared before this one and its category.

            Example: only apply the `sub` stratification to `group1`::

                conditions = [
                    StratificationCondition(stratification="group", category="group1")
                ]

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any condition references a stratification not yet declared.
        """
        if conditions:
            declared_ids = {s.id for s in self._stratifications}
            for cond in conditions:
                if cond.stratification not in declared_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Stratification '{id}': condition references "
                        f"'{cond.stratification}' which has not been declared yet. "
                        "Conditions may only reference stratifications declared before "
                        "this one."
                    )

        self._stratifications.append(
            Stratification(
                id=id,
                categories=categories,
                description=description,
                conditions=list(conditions) if conditions else None,
            )
        )
        logger.info(f"Added stratification: id='{id}', categories={categories}")
        return self

    def add_parameter(
        self,
        id: str,
        value: float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None,
        description: str | None = None,
        unit: str | None = None,
        mode: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a global parameter to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the parameter.
        value : float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None
            Value of the parameter. Can be:
            - float: A numerical constant value
            - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
                   special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e),
                   or contain mathematical expressions (e.g., "k1 * 2",
                   "total_g1 / total")
            - list[tuple[float, float]]: Empirical series as (position, value)
                   points; requires ``mode`` to be set.
            - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use

        description : str | None, default=None
            Human-readable description of the parameter.
        unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "item").
            Used for unit consistency checking in equations.
        mode : str | None, default=None
            Required when ``value`` is a list of (position, value) points.
            Selects how the series is read: ``"pulse"`` (the value on the step
            of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only),
            ``"step_function"`` (the value of the last point at or before
            ``t``), or ``"linear"`` (linear interpolation in ``t``).

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``value`` is a list but ``mode`` is not provided, if
            ``mode`` is provided without a list ``value``, or if the parser
            of the engine rejects a formula ``value``, with its message.
        """
        if isinstance(value, list):
            if mode is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is required when 'value' is a "
                    "series list. Use mode='pulse', 'step_function', or 'linear'."
                )
            param_value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = SeriesValue(
                data=value, mode=mode
            )
        else:
            if mode is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is only valid when 'value' is a "
                    "series list."
                )
            param_value = value
        self._ensure_parameter_id_available(id)
        self._parameters.append(
            Parameter(id=id, value=param_value, description=description, unit=unit)
        )
        logger.info(f"Added parameter: id='{id}', value={value}, unit='{unit}'")
        return self

    def _ensure_parameter_id_available(self, id: str) -> None:
        if any(parameter.id == id for parameter in self._parameters):
            raise ValueError(f"Parameter id '{id}' already exists")

    def _register_series_pattern(
        self,
        pattern: AxisPattern,
        *,
        transition_id: str,
        source_bin: str,
        target_bin: str,
    ) -> AxisPattern:
        """Auto-register a series parameter for pulse-type patterns.

        If ``pattern`` has numeric pulse data, registers a ``"pulse"`` series
        parameter and returns a ``_ComputedAxisPattern`` whose formula is the
        generated parameter name. Otherwise returns ``pattern`` unchanged.
        """
        data = pattern._as_series_data()
        if data is None:
            return pattern
        conditions = pattern.conditions
        if transition_id and conditions:
            src_cats = "_".join(c.category for c in conditions if c.category)
            tgt_cats = "_".join(
                target for c in conditions if (target := c.to or c.category)
            )
            src = f"{source_bin}_{src_cats}" if source_bin else src_cats
            tgt = f"{target_bin}_{tgt_cats}" if target_bin else tgt_cats
            param_name = f"{transition_id}_{src}_to_{tgt}"
        else:
            param_name = f"_series_{self._series_counter}"
            self._series_counter += 1
        self._ensure_parameter_id_available(param_name)
        self._parameters.append(
            Parameter(
                id=param_name,
                value=SeriesValue(data=data, mode="pulse"),
            )
        )
        return _ComputedAxisPattern(
            computed_formula=param_name,
            conditions=conditions,
            source_compartment=pattern.source_compartment,
        )

    def add_transition(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
        rate: "str | float | AxisPattern | None" = None,
        stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None = None,
        per_compartment: bool | None = None,
        accumulators: list[str] | None = None,
        impulse_at: list[float] | None = None,
        impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a transition between states to the model.

        This method supports two distinct behaviors:

        When you specify multiple sources without the $compartment placeholder,
        a single transition is created that affects all sources simultaneously.
        The rate is evaluated once, at each position the engine reads it, and
        that value applies to all source compartments at once. What the value
        means (an amount moved in one step or an instantaneous rate) is the
        engine's; see "What a rate means" in the Core Concepts guide.

        When you use the $compartment placeholder in the rate formula with multiple
        sources, the system automatically expands this into multiple independent
        transitions - one for each source compartment. Each transition has its own
        rate calculation where $compartment is replaced with the actual compartment
        name.

        Each transition's rate is evaluated independently, giving per-compartment
        dynamics. This suits an outflow such as ``k1 * $compartment``, where the
        flow of each compartment is proportional to its own amount.

        **$compartment Usage Rules**:
        - Only valid with several sources (and one or no target) or several
          targets (and one or no source)
        - Can be used with stratified_rates - the placeholder will be expanded in
          both the base rate and all stratified rate expressions
        - The placeholder $compartment will be replaced with each source compartment
          name

        **$compartment Restrictions**:
        - Using $compartment with a single source will raise an error (use the
          compartment name directly instead)
        - Using $compartment with multiple targets will raise an error (ambiguous
          which target corresponds to which source)

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the transition. When using $compartment expansion,
            the system will append "__<compartment_name>" to create unique IDs for
            each expanded transition (e.g., "out__A", "out__B").
        source : list[str]
            List of source state/category identifiers. When using $compartment in
            the rate, each source will generate a separate transition.
        target : list[str]
            List of target state/category identifiers. When using $compartment
            with several targets, each target generates a separate transition.
        rate : str | float | AxisPattern | None, default=None
            Default mathematical formula, parameter reference, or constant value for
            the transition rate. Used when no stratified rate matches.
            Can be:
            - A parameter reference
            - A constant value
            - A mathematical formula
            - A formula with $compartment placeholder

            Special variables available in formulas:
            - total: The sum of every compartment, accumulators excluded
            - total_<category>…: The sum of the compartments with these
              categories, in the declaration order of the stratifications
            - t: The current position on the axis
            - step: The step that holds it, ``floor(t)``; in a
              DifferenceEquations model ``t`` and ``step`` are equal
            - pi, e: Mathematical constants
            - $compartment: Expands to each source compartment name (only with
              multiple sources)

        stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None, default=None
            The rates of the compartments that match some categories. A
            compartment that no stratified rate matches takes ``rate``.

        per_compartment : bool | None, default=None
            When True, each id of a source or target bin in a rate reads the
            compartment of the flow (``A_g1``) instead of the total of the bin.
            Any other bin keeps its total: in a transition from ``A`` to ``B``,
            ``k * A * (C + D) / total`` reads ``A_g1`` and the totals of ``C``
            and ``D``. It applies to the fallback rate, to every stratified
            rate, and to every transition that ``$compartment`` expands to,
            where ``$compartment`` reads the compartment that flows. A
            transition between categories ignores it.

        accumulators : list[str] | None, default=None
            Ids of accumulators that add up the flow of this transition.

        impulse_at : list[float] | None, default=None
            Make the transition an impulse at these positions on the axis. At
            each one, ``rate`` is the fraction of the source (proportional) or the
            amount (absolute) moved at once, before the flows of that step. A
            DifferenceEquations or StochasticSteps model needs integer
            positions.

        impulse_every : tuple[float, float] | None, default=None
            ``(period, offset)``: make the transition an impulse at ``offset``,
            ``offset + period``, ``offset + 2 * period``, ...

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            - If $compartment is used with only one source compartment
            - If $compartment is used with multiple targets
            - If rate is None when using $compartment
        """
        # If `rate` is a AxisPattern, extract its rate string and stratified
        # rates and route them into the existing pipeline. A AxisPattern fully
        # specifies how the rate changes along the axis, so passing `stratified_rates=`
        # alongside it is a conflict.
        if isinstance(rate, AxisPattern):
            if impulse_at is not None or impulse_every is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{id}': an impulse moves its rate at once; pass "
                    "a fraction or an amount as `rate=`, not a AxisPattern."
                )
            if stratified_rates is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{id}': pass either a AxisPattern as `rate=` "
                    "or `stratified_rates=`, not both."
                )
            src_bin = source[0] if source else ""
            tgt_bin = target[0] if target else ""
            if isinstance(rate, _ScheduleAxisPattern):
                resolved = rate.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "patterns": [
                            _GroupEntry(
                                pattern=self._register_series_pattern(
                                    entry.pattern,
                                    transition_id=id,
                                    source_bin=src_bin,
                                    target_bin=tgt_bin,
                                ),
                                absolute=entry.absolute,
                            )
                            for entry in rate.patterns
                        ]
                    }
                )
                rate = resolved
            else:
                rate = self._register_series_pattern(
                    rate, transition_id=id, source_bin=src_bin, target_bin=tgt_bin
                )
            stratified_rates = rate._builder_stratified_rates()
            rate = rate._builder_rate()

        # Convert rate to string if numeric
        if isinstance(rate, int) or isinstance(rate, float):
            rate = str(rate)

        # Check for $compartment placeholder and handle expansion
        if rate and "$compartment" in rate:
            self._validate_compartment_placeholder(id, source, target)
            self._expand_compartment_transition(
                id,
                source,
                target,
                rate,
                stratified_rates,
                per_compartment,
                accumulators,
                impulse_at,
                impulse_every,
            )
            return self

        stratified_rates_objects = _stratified_rate_objects(stratified_rates)
        self._transitions.append(
            Transition(
                id=id,
                source=source,
                target=target,
                accumulators=accumulators or [],
                rate=rate,
                stratified_rates=stratified_rates_objects,
                per_compartment=per_compartment,
                impulse_at=impulse_at,
                impulse_every=impulse_every,
            )
        )
        logger.info(
            (
                f"Added transition: id='{id}', source={source}, target={target}, "
                f"rate='{rate}', stratified_rates={
                    len(stratified_rates_objects) if stratified_rates_objects else 0
                }"
            )
        )
        return self

    def _validate_compartment_placeholder(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Validate that $compartment placeholder is used correctly.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Transition identifier (for error messages)
        source : list[str]
            Source compartments
        target : list[str]
            Target compartments
        rate : str
            Rate formula
        stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None
            Stratified rates

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If $compartment usage violates any rules
        """
        # Check that we have either multiple sources OR multiple targets, but not both
        has_multiple_sources = len(source) > 1
        has_multiple_targets = len(target) > 1

        if not has_multiple_sources and not has_multiple_targets:
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Transition '{id}': $compartment placeholder requires either "
                    f"multiple source compartments or multiple target compartments "
                    f"(found {len(source)} source(s) and {len(target)} target(s)). "
                    f"If you have a single source/target, use the compartment name "
                    f"directly in the rate formula instead of $compartment."
                )
            )

        if has_multiple_sources and has_multiple_targets:
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Transition '{id}': $compartment placeholder cannot be used "
                    f"with both multiple sources and multiple targets "
                    f"(found {len(source)} sources and {len(target)} targets). "
                    f"This would create ambiguous mappings. Use either multiple "
                    f"sources with single/empty target, or single/empty source with "
                    f"multiple targets."
                )
            )

    def _expand_compartment_transition(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
        rate: str,
        stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None,
        per_compartment: bool | None,
        accumulators: list[str] | None,
        impulse_at: list[float] | None,
        impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Expand a transition with $compartment placeholder into multiple transitions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Base transition identifier
        source : list[str]
            Source compartments
            (will create one transition per source if multiple sources)
        target : list[str]
            Target compartments
            (will create one transition per target if multiple targets)
        rate : str
            Rate formula containing $compartment
        stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None
            Stratified rates (can contain $compartment which will be expanded)
        per_compartment, accumulators, impulse_at, impulse_every : optional
            The arguments of `add_transition` that every expanded transition
            keeps
        """
        # Determine if we're expanding over sources or targets
        has_multiple_sources = len(source) > 1

        if has_multiple_sources:
            compartments = source
            expand_type = "source"
        else:
            compartments = target
            expand_type = "target"

        logger.info(
            (
                f"Expanding transition '{id}' with $compartment placeholder: "
                f"{len(compartments)} {expand_type} compartments will create "
                f"{len(compartments)} separate transitions"
            )
        )

        for compartment in compartments:
            # Replace $compartment with actual compartment name in base rate
            expanded_rate = rate.replace("$compartment", compartment)

            expanded_stratified_rates = _stratified_rate_objects(
                stratified_rates, compartment
            )

            # Generate unique ID for this expanded transition
            expanded_id = f"{id}__{compartment}"

            # add_transition accepts several sources or several targets.
            if has_multiple_sources:
                expanded_source = [compartment]
                expanded_target = target
            else:
                expanded_source = source
                expanded_target = [compartment]

            self._transitions.append(
                Transition(
                    id=expanded_id,
                    source=expanded_source,
                    target=expanded_target,
                    accumulators=accumulators or [],
                    rate=expanded_rate,
                    stratified_rates=expanded_stratified_rates,
                    per_compartment=per_compartment,
                    impulse_at=impulse_at,
                    impulse_every=impulse_every,
                )
            )

            strat_info = (
                f", {len(expanded_stratified_rates)} stratified rates"
                if expanded_stratified_rates
                else ""
            )
            logger.info(
                (
                    f"  Created expanded transition: id='{expanded_id}', "
                    f"source=['{compartment}'], target={target}, "
                    f"rate='{expanded_rate}'{strat_info}"
                )
            )

        logger.info(
            f"Successfully expanded transition '{id}' into {len(compartments)} "
            "transitions"
        )

    def get_summary(self) -> dict[str, str | int | list[str] | None]:
        """
        Get a summary of the current model builder state.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, dict[str, str | int | list[str] | None]]
            Dictionary containing summary information about the model being built.
        """
        return {
            "name": self._name,
            "description": self._description,
            "version": self._version,
            "bins_count": len(self._bins),
            "bin_ids": [state.id for state in self._bins],
            "stratifications_count": len(self._stratifications),
            "stratification_ids": [strat.id for strat in self._stratifications],
            "transitions_count": len(self._transitions),
            "transition_ids": [trans.id for trans in self._transitions],
            "parameters_count": len(self._parameters),
            "parameter_ids": [param.id for param in self._parameters],
        }

    def clone(self) -> Self:
        """
        Create a deep copy of this ModelBuilder.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            A new ModelBuilder instance with the same configuration: every
            bin, accumulator, stratification, transition and parameter.
            Changes to one builder do not affect the other.
        """
        return copy.deepcopy(self)

    def reset(self) -> Self:
        """
        Reset the builder to empty state.

        The name, description, version, ``bin_unit``, ``step_unit`` and
        ``origin`` are kept. Every bin,
        accumulator, stratification, transition and parameter is removed.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.
        """
        self._bins.clear()
        self._accumulators.clear()
        self._stratifications.clear()
        self._transitions.clear()
        self._parameters.clear()
        self._series_counter = 0
        return self

    def process(self) -> Process:
        """
        The process the builder has written so far.

        Returns
        -------
        Process
            The bins, accumulators, stratifications and transitions.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ids repeat, or a transition or a stratified rate names an id
            the process does not have.
        """
        return Process(
            bins=self._bins,
            accumulators=self._accumulators,
            stratifications=self._stratifications,
            transitions=self._transitions,
        )

    def build(
        self,
        structure: StructureT,
        engine: EngineName,
        settings: EngineSettings | None = None,
    ) -> Model[StructureT]:
        """
        Join the process with a structure and an engine into a model.

        The process is written once; the structure lays it out and sets the
        kind of the model, so one builder builds every kind its process fits:

        ``builder.build(Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}),
        engine="DifferentialEquations")``

        Parameters
        ----------
        structure : ModelStructure
            How the process is laid out, such as `Aggregate` (amounts per
            compartment). The model is a ``Model`` of its class.
        engine : EngineName
            The engine that runs the model, which must run the kind of the
            structure: ``"DifferenceEquations"`` (discrete time),
            ``"DifferentialEquations"`` (continuous time), ``"StochasticEvents"``
            or ``"StochasticSteps"`` (at random).
        settings : EngineSettings | None, default=None
            Settings of that engine; None uses its defaults: `ODESolver` for
            ``"DifferentialEquations"``, `StochasticEventsSettings` and
            `StochasticStepsSettings` for the stochastic engines.

        Returns
        -------
        Model[StructureT]
            The model, of the class of ``structure``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If validation fails, the structure does not fit the process (for
            example a fraction names no bin, or a rate reads ``neighbors_<bin>``
            and the structure has no ``neighbors``), the engine is unknown or
            does not run the kind of the structure, the settings are not
            settings of that engine, a series point or an impulse position is
            one the engine cannot run (a position between two steps for an
            engine that steps only at integers, or a ``"pulse"`` point between
            two steps), a per-compartment override names an unknown
            compartment, a stochastic engine gets an amount that is not whole,
            or the origin has a time zone or a step unit that is not of fixed
            calendar length.
        """
        model: Model[StructureT] = Model(
            name=self._name,
            description=self._description,
            version=self._version,
            parameters=self._parameters,
            engine=ModelEngine(type=engine, settings=settings),
            process=self.process(),
            structure=structure,
            step_unit=self._step_unit,
            origin=self._origin,
        )

        logger.info(f"Model '{self._name}' successfully built for the {engine} engine.")

        return model
```

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    name: str,
    description: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    bin_unit: str | None = None,
    step_unit: str | None = None,
    origin: date | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Initialize the ModelBuilder.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The unique name that identifies the model.
    description : str | None, default=None
        A human-readable description of the model's purpose and function.
    version : str | None, default=None
        The version number of the model.
    bin_unit : str | None, default=None
        The default unit for all bins.
        Individual bins can override this with their own unit parameter.
        Units are optional but required for model.check_unit_consistency().
    step_unit : str | None, default=None
        Unit of one step on the axis, of any single dimension (for example
        ``"day"`` or ``"meter"``). The unit check requires every flow to be
        ``<bin unit>/<step_unit>``, and ``Model.axis_units()`` converts
        values to steps of it. None means ``step``, the default increment
        of any axis.
    origin : date | None, default=None
        Calendar moment of position 0: a `datetime.datetime` with no time
        zone, or a `datetime.date`, read as its midnight. With it,
        ``Model.axis_units()`` converts between dates and positions, and
        ``results.plot.series()`` labels its ticks with dates. It
        needs a ``step_unit`` of time whose length is a whole number of
        days or a whole fraction of a day, such as ``"hour"`` or
        ``"day"``; `build` raises ``ValueError`` otherwise, or for a
        moment with a time zone.
    """
    self._name: str = name
    self._description: str | None = description
    self._version: str | None = version
    self._bin_unit: str | None = bin_unit
    self._step_unit: str | None = step_unit
    self._origin: date | None = origin

    self._bins: list[Bin] = []
    self._accumulators: list[Accumulator] = []
    self._stratifications: list[Stratification] = []
    self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
    self._parameters: list[Parameter] = []
    self._series_counter: int = 0

    logger.info(
        (
            f"Initialized ModelBuilder: name='{self._name}', "
            f"version='{self._version or 'N/A'}'"
        )
    )
```

```python
def add_bin(self, id: str, name: str, unit: str | None = None) -> Self:
    """
    Add a bin to the model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for the bin.
    name : str
```

```python
def add_stratification(
    self,
    id: str,
    categories: list[str],
    description: str | None = None,
    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a stratification to the model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        list of category identifiers within this stratification.
    description : str | None, default=None
        Human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None, default=None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied categories satisfy ALL conditions. Each condition
        names a stratification declared before this one and its category.

        Example: only apply the `sub` stratification to `group1`::

            conditions = [
                StratificationCondition(stratification="group", category="group1")
            ]

    Returns
    -------
    ModelBuilder
        Self for method chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any condition references a stratification not yet declared.
    """
    if conditions:
        declared_ids = {s.id for s in self._stratifications}
        for cond in conditions:
            if cond.stratification not in declared_ids:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Stratification '{id}': condition references "
                    f"'{cond.stratification}' which has not been declared yet. "
                    "Conditions may only reference stratifications declared before "
                    "this one."
                )

    self._stratifications.append(
        Stratification(
            id=id,
            categories=categories,
            description=description,
            conditions=list(conditions) if conditions else None,
        )
    )
    logger.info(f"Added stratification: id='{id}', categories={categories}")
    return self
```
