```python
    core and every level in parallel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        The number of threads, at least 1.
    levels : {"all", "outer"} | None
        Which levels run in parallel when a method nests them; `None` keeps
        the current levels.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `n` is below 1 or `levels` is neither name.
    """
    commol_rs.parallelism.setting().set(_choice(n, levels))
```

#### threads

```python
threads(n: int | None = None, levels: Levels | None = None) -> Generator[None]
```

Limit the threads of every parallel method within a block.

The previous setting comes back when the block ends, also on an error.

Parameters:

| Name     | Type           | Description                                                                           | Default                                                           |
| -------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `n`      | \`int          | None\`                                                                                | The number of threads, at least 1; None keeps the current number. |
| `levels` | `(all, outer)` | Which levels run in parallel when a method nests them; None keeps the current levels. | `"all"`                                                           |

Yields:

| Type   | Description                      |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| `None` | The block runs with the setting. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If n is below 1 or levels is neither name. |

Source code in `commol/parallelism/threads.py`

```python
@contextmanager
def threads(n: int | None = None, levels: Levels | None = None) -> Generator[None]:
    """
    Limit the threads of every parallel method within a block.

    The previous setting comes back when the block ends, also on an error.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int | None
        The number of threads, at least 1; `None` keeps the current number.
    levels : {"all", "outer"} | None
        Which levels run in parallel when a method nests them; `None` keeps
        the current levels.

    Yields
    ------
    None
        The block runs with the setting.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `n` is below 1 or `levels` is neither name.
    """
    variable = commol_rs.parallelism.setting()
    token = variable.set(_choice(n, levels))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        variable.reset(token)
```

```python
def get_threads() -> int:
    """
    The number of threads of the parallel methods in this context.

    Returns
```

# Plotting API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

The module `commol.plotting`: `plot_compared` and the style of a figure, `PlotConfig`. The figures are read from the results they draw, and return a matplotlib `Figure`. `results.plot`, `replicates.plot` and `predictive.plot` give the figures of a run, of replicates and of a predictive: `plot.series()`, `plot.cumulative()` and `plot.observations()`; each accessor is on the page of the object that gives it: [Simulation](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/simulation/index.md) and [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/uncertainty/index.md). The results of PRCC, Morris, Sobol and polynomial chaos, and the result of a profile likelihood, draw their figure with `plot()`. `plot_compared` draws several runs, replicates or predictives on the same panels. The figures need the optional extra `commol[plot]`. Guide: [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#plotting).

## plot_compared

```python
plot_compared(results: Mapping[str, Plotted], series: list[str] | None = None, window: float | None = None, observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] | None = None, panels: Literal['series', 'observations'] = 'series', axes: Figure | None = None, output_file: str | None = None, config: PlotConfig | None = None, show_legend: bool = True, position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None, tick_every: float | None = None, x_label: str = 'Step', confidence_level: float = 0.95, **kwargs: str | int | float | bool | None) -> Figure
```

Draw several results of the same model on the same panels, one panel per series or one per observed series.

Each panel has one line per result, labelled with its key and in the same color in every panel (`C0` for the first key, `C1` for the second, …). Replicates show their mean and the band of the replicates, and a predictive the weighted median of its draws and their band, in the color of their key. The observations are drawn once.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `results`          | \`Mapping\[str, SimulationResults   | SimulationReplicates                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Predictive\]\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `series`           | \`list[str]                         | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | What to draw, one panel each, as in ResultsPlot.series. If None, every output. Only with panels="series".                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `window`           | \`float                             | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The length of a window on the axis. Each line is then the gain of the series over each complete window, as Simulation.windowed_totals reads it, at the end of the window; a band is the band of these gains. If None, each line is the line of the plot.series of its result with observed_data. Only with panels="series". |
| `observed_data`    | \`list[ObservedDataPoint]           | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Observations, each drawn once as a point on the panel of its label. Without window, they also set how each line is read, as in ResultsPlot.series.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `panels`           | `Literal['series', 'observations']` | "series": one panel per entry of series. "observations": one panel per label of observed_data, with each result read only at the observations, through the observation operator of each one, as ResultsPlot.observations reads one result. | `'series'`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `axes`             | \`Figure                            | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A figure of commol to draw on: each series is drawn on its panel, the Axes whose label is the id of the series (or the label of the observed series). If None, a new figure.                                                                                                                                                |
| `output_file`      | \`str                               | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Path to save the figure to. If None, the figure is only returned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `config`           | \`PlotConfig                        | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Layout and style. If None, the defaults.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `show_legend`      | `bool`                              | Whether each panel shows its legend.                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `True`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `position_label`   | \`Callable\[[float], str\]          | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Turns a position into a tick label, as in ResultsPlot.series.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tick_every`       | \`float                             | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The distance between labelled positions, as in ResultsPlot.series.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `x_label`          | `str`                               | The label of the x axis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `'Step'`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `confidence_level` | `float`                             | The level of the bands of replicates and predictives, strictly between 0 and 1.                                                                                                                                                            | `0.95`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `**kwargs`         | \`str                               | int                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | float                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Returns:

| Type     | Description            |
| -------- | ---------------------- |
| `Figure` | The matplotlib figure. |

Raises:

| Type          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError`  | If there are no results; a result does not have the outputs of the first (the message names its key and the outputs that differ); window is not positive; the confidence level is out of range; axes has no panel of a series; panels is neither "series" nor "observations"; or, with panels="observations", series or window is given, there are no observations, or a result has no value at the position of an observation or at the start of its window. |
| `KeyError`    | If an entry of series is neither an output nor a bin or accumulator id of the model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ImportError` | If matplotlib is not installed (pip install 'commol[plot]').                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Examples:

```pycon
>>> figure = plot_compared({"k1 = 0.3": results, "k1 = 0.5": faster})
>>> checked = plot_compared(
...     {"k1 = 0.3": results, "k1 = 0.5": faster},
...     observed_data=observed,
...     panels="observations",
... )
```

Source code in `commol/plotting/compared.py`

```python
def plot_compared(
    results: "Mapping[str, Plotted]",
    series: list[str] | None = None,
    window: float | None = None,
    observed_data: "list[ObservedDataPoint] | None" = None,
    panels: Literal["series", "observations"] = "series",
    axes: "Figure | None" = None,
    output_file: str | None = None,
    config: "PlotConfig | None" = None,
    show_legend: bool = True,
    position_label: Callable[[float], str] | None = None,
    tick_every: float | None = None,
    x_label: str = "Step",
    confidence_level: float = 0.95,
    **kwargs: str | int | float | bool | None,
) -> "Figure":
    """
    Draw several results of the same model on the same panels, one panel per
    series or one per observed series.

    Each panel has one line per result, labelled with its key and in the
    same color in every panel (``C0`` for the first key, ``C1`` for the
    second, …). Replicates show their mean and the band of the replicates,
    and a predictive the weighted median of its draws and their band, in the
    color of their key. The observations are drawn once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results : Mapping[str, SimulationResults | SimulationReplicates | Predictive]
        The results, by the label of their lines. Each has the outputs of
        the first; the model of the first names the series.
    series : list[str] | None
        What to draw, one panel each, as in ``ResultsPlot.series``. If None,
        every output. Only with ``panels="series"``.
    window : float | None
        The length of a window on the axis. Each line is then the gain of
        the series over each complete window, as `Simulation.windowed_totals`
        reads it, at the end of the window; a band is the band of these
        gains. If None, each line is the line of the ``plot.series`` of its
        result with `observed_data`. Only with ``panels="series"``.
    observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint] | None
        Observations, each drawn once as a point on the panel of its label.
        Without `window`, they also set how each line is read, as in
        ``ResultsPlot.series``.
    panels : Literal["series", "observations"]
        ``"series"``: one panel per entry of `series`. ``"observations"``:
        one panel per label of `observed_data`, with each result read only
        at the observations, through the observation operator of each one,
        as ``ResultsPlot.observations`` reads one result.
    axes : Figure | None
        A figure of commol to draw on: each series is drawn on its panel,
        the `Axes` whose label is the id of the series (or the label of the
        observed series). If None, a new figure.
    output_file : str | None
        Path to save the figure to. If None, the figure is only returned.
    config : PlotConfig | None
        Layout and style. If None, the defaults.
    show_legend : bool
        Whether each panel shows its legend.
    position_label : Callable[[float], str] | None
        Turns a position into a tick label, as in ``ResultsPlot.series``.
    tick_every : float | None
        The distance between labelled positions, as in
        ``ResultsPlot.series``.
    x_label : str
        The label of the x axis.
    confidence_level : float
        The level of the bands of replicates and predictives, strictly
        between 0 and 1.
    **kwargs : str | int | float | bool | None
        Passed to ``Axes.plot`` for the line of each result, such as
        ``linewidth``.

    Returns
    -------
    Figure
        The matplotlib figure.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If there are no results; a result does not have the outputs of the
        first (the message names its key and the outputs that differ);
        `window` is not positive; the confidence level is out of range;
        ``axes`` has no panel of a series; `panels` is neither ``"series"``
        nor ``"observations"``; or, with ``panels="observations"``, `series`
        or `window` is given, there are no observations, or a result has no
        value at the position of an observation or at the start of its
        window.
    KeyError
        If an entry of ``series`` is neither an output nor a bin or
        accumulator id of the model.
    ImportError
        If matplotlib is not installed (``pip install 'commol[plot]'``).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> figure = plot_compared({"k1 = 0.3": results, "k1 = 0.5": faster})
    >>> checked = plot_compared(
    ...     {"k1 = 0.3": results, "k1 = 0.5": faster},
    ...     observed_data=observed,
    ...     panels="observations",
    ... )
    """
    from commol.plotting.figures import _compared_series

    return _compared_series(
        results,
        series=series,
        window=window,
        observed_data=observed_data,
        panels=panels,
        axes=axes,
        output_file=output_file,
        config=config,
        show_legend=show_legend,
        position_label=position_label,
        tick_every=tick_every,
        x_label=x_label,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        **kwargs,
    )
```

Draw each profile: one panel per parameter or prediction, with the statistic of each point, the threshold, and the ends of the interval.

```python
    self,
    output_file: str | None = None,
    config: "PlotConfig | None" = None,
    axes: "Figure | None" = None,
) -> "Figure":
    """
    Draw each profile: one panel per parameter or prediction, with the
    statistic of each point, the threshold, and the ends of the interval.

    A profile that stays under the threshold up to a bound is open on that
    side; a flat one stays near 0 over its whole range.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output_file : str | None
        Path to save the figure to. If None, the figure is only returned.
    config : PlotConfig | None
        Layout and style. If None, the defaults.
    axes : Figure | None
        A figure of commol to draw on: each panel is the `Axes` whose
        label is the name of its profile. If None, a new figure.

    Returns
    -------
    Figure
        The matplotlib figure.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``axes`` has no panel of a profile.
    ImportError
        If matplotlib is not installed (``pip install 'commol[plot]'``).
    """
    from commol.profiles.plots import profiles_figure

    return profiles_figure(self, output_file=output_file, config=config, axes=axes)
```

## PlotConfig

Bases: `BaseModel`

Configuration for plot layout and styling.

Attributes:

| Name      | Type                  | Description                                                                                                                |
| --------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `figsize` | `tuple[float, float]` | Figure size in inches (width, height), of a figure of running totals; the other figures take their size from their panels. |
| `dpi`     | `int`                 | Dots per inch for figure resolution.                                                                                       |
| `layout`  | \`tuple[int, int]     | None\`                                                                                                                     |
| `style`   | \`str                 | list[str]                                                                                                                  |

Notes

The style applies to the figure of one call only: after the call, `matplotlib.rcParams` is as it was before it, so the figures that you draw with matplotlib keep your style. Given `axes=`, a figure draws on the panels of an earlier figure, and `figsize`, `dpi` and `layout` are those of that figure.

Examples:

```pycon
>>> # Direct configuration
>>> config = PlotConfig(style=["seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid", "seaborn-v0_8-talk"])
```

```pycon
>>> # Using presets
>>> config = PlotConfig.presentation()
>>> config = PlotConfig.publication()
```

Source code in `commol/plotting/config.py`

```python
class PlotConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    Configuration for plot layout and styling.

    Attributes
    ----------
    figsize : tuple[float, float]
        Figure size in inches (width, height), of a figure of running totals;
        the other figures take their size from their panels.
    dpi : int
        Dots per inch for figure resolution.
    layout : tuple[int, int] | None
        Panel layout as (rows, cols). If None, computed from the number of
        panels.
    style : str | list[str] | None
        A matplotlib style, or a list of styles applied in order: a name of
        ``matplotlib.style.available`` (such as ``"ggplot"`` or
        ``"seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid"``) or the path of a style file.
        See: https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/customizing.html

    Notes
    -----
    The style applies to the figure of one call only: after the call,
    ``matplotlib.rcParams`` is as it was before it, so the figures that you
    draw with matplotlib keep your style. Given ``axes=``, a figure draws on
    the panels of an earlier figure, and `figsize`, `dpi` and `layout` are
    those of that figure.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # Direct configuration
    >>> config = PlotConfig(style=["seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid", "seaborn-v0_8-talk"])

    >>> # Using presets
    >>> config = PlotConfig.presentation()
    >>> config = PlotConfig.publication()
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    figsize: tuple[float, float] = Field(
        default=(12, 8),
        description="Figure size in inches (width, height)",
    )
    dpi: int = Field(
        default=100,
        description="Dots per inch for figure resolution",
    )
    layout: tuple[int, int] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Panel layout as (rows, cols). If None, computed.",
    )
    style: str | list[str] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="A matplotlib style, or styles applied in order",
    )

    @classmethod
    def presentation(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for presentations.

        Large figure size, high DPI, a white grid, the large text of the
        "talk" style and a palette for colour-blind readers.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with presentation-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(16, 10),
            dpi=150,
            style=[
                "seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid",
                "seaborn-v0_8-talk",
                "seaborn-v0_8-colorblind",
            ],
        )

    @classmethod
    def publication(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for academic publications.

        Smaller figure size suitable for journal columns, high DPI for print
        quality, ticks and the small text of the "paper" style.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with publication-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(8, 6),
            dpi=300,
            style=["seaborn-v0_8-ticks", "seaborn-v0_8-paper"],
        )

    @classmethod
    def notebook(cls) -> Self:
        """
        Create a configuration optimized for Jupyter notebooks.

        Balanced defaults for interactive exploration.

        Returns
        -------
        PlotConfig
            Configuration with notebook-friendly settings.
        """
        return cls(
            figsize=(12, 8),
            dpi=100,
            style=["seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid", "seaborn-v0_8-notebook"],
        )
```

# Profiles API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

The module `commol.profiles`: the profile likelihood of parameters and predictions, and its result. Guide: [Profile Likelihood](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/profiles/index.md).

## ProfileLikelihood

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[ProfileResult]`, `RangeChecked`

The profile likelihood of parameters (Raue et al. 2009).

Each parameter is held at values that step away from the fit, in both directions, and the others are fitted again with the problem's own optimizer. The step grows while the profile rises slowly and shrinks when it jumps, and each point starts from a line through the two points before it. A side ends past the threshold, at a bound, or after `max_steps` points. Parameters run in parallel.

Attributes:

| Name         | Type        | Description                                                                             |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parameters` | `list[str]` | The parameters to profile, at least one.                                                |
| `threshold`  | `Threshold` | The threshold of the statistic.                                                         |
| `max_steps`  | `int`       | The most points on each side of a profile (default 100).                                |
| `starts`     | `int`       | Starts of the fit (default 1): the fit, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds. |

Source code in `commol/profiles/methods.py`

```python
class ProfileLikelihood(UncertaintyMethod[ProfileResult], RangeChecked):
    """
    The profile likelihood of parameters (Raue et al. 2009).

    Each parameter is held at values that step away from the fit, in both
    directions, and the others are fitted again with the problem's own
    optimizer. The step grows while the profile rises slowly and shrinks
    when it jumps, and each point starts from a line through the two points
    before it. A side ends past the threshold, at a bound, or after
    `max_steps` points. Parameters run in parallel.

    Attributes
    ----------
    parameters : list[str]
        The parameters to profile, at least one.
    threshold : Threshold
        The threshold of the statistic.
    max_steps : int
        The most points on each side of a profile (default 100).
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1): the fit, then rows of a Latin
        hypercube over the bounds.
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_profile_likelihood)

    parameters: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    threshold: Threshold
    max_steps: int = Field(
        default=100,
    )
    starts: int = Field(
        default=1,
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_unique(self) -> Self:
        """Each parameter is profiled once."""
        if len(set(self.parameters)) != len(self.parameters):
            raise ValueError(f"A parameter is listed twice: {self.parameters}.")
        return self
```

## PredictionProfile

Bases: `UncertaintyMethod[ProfileResult]`, `RangeChecked`

The profile likelihood of predictions (Kreutz et al. 2012).

Each prediction is held at values that step away from its value at the fit, as an equality constraint met by an augmented Lagrangian whose inner solver is the problem's own optimizer, and the parameters are fitted again. The interval of a prediction is the set of values the data do not reject; several specs at several positions give a band.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type                   | Description                                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `specs`     | `list[PredictionSpec]` | The predictions, at least one, with distinct labels.     |
| `threshold` | `Threshold`            | The threshold of the statistic.                          |
| `max_steps` | `int`                  | The most points on each side of a profile (default 100). |
| `starts`    | `int`                  | Starts of the fit (default 1).                           |

Source code in `commol/profiles/methods.py`

```python
class PredictionProfile(UncertaintyMethod[ProfileResult], RangeChecked):
    """
    The profile likelihood of predictions (Kreutz et al. 2012).

    Each prediction is held at values that step away from its value at the
    fit, as an equality constraint met by an augmented Lagrangian whose
    inner solver is the problem's own optimizer, and the parameters are
    fitted again. The interval of a prediction is the set of values the data
    do not reject; several specs at several positions give a band.

    Attributes
    ----------
    specs : list[PredictionSpec]
        The predictions, at least one, with distinct labels.
    threshold : Threshold
        The threshold of the statistic.
    max_steps : int
        The most points on each side of a profile (default 100).
    starts : int
        Starts of the fit (default 1).
    """

    _runner = staticmethod(run_prediction_profile)

    specs: list[PredictionSpec] = Field(min_length=1)
    threshold: Threshold
    max_steps: int = Field(
        default=100,
    )
    starts: int = Field(
        default=1,
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_labels(self) -> Self:
        """Each prediction has a label of its own."""
        labels = [spec.as_observation().label for spec in self.specs]
        if len(set(labels)) != len(labels):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Each prediction needs a label of its own, got {labels}; set label."
            )
        return self
```

## PredictionSpec

Bases: `RangeChecked`

A prediction to profile: an output, or a sum of outputs, at a position, read as an observation is.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type        | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `at`        | `float`     | The position.                                                 |
| `output`    | \`str       | None\`                                                        |
| `outputs`   | \`list[str] | None\`                                                        |
| `label`     | `str`       | The name of the prediction in the result; defaults to output. |
| `window`    | \`float     | None\`                                                        |
| `factor_id` | \`str       | None\`                                                        |

Source code in `commol/profiles/methods.py`

```python
class PredictionSpec(RangeChecked):
    """
    A prediction to profile: an output, or a sum of outputs, at a position,
    read as an observation is.

    Attributes
    ----------
    at : float
        The position.
    output : str | None
        The output. Give either `output` or `outputs`.
    outputs : list[str] | None
        Outputs summed. Needs a `label`.
    label : str
        The name of the prediction in the result; defaults to `output`.
    window : float | None
        A window length: the prediction is the output at `at` less the
        output at ``at - window``.
    factor_id : str | None
        A factor parameter that multiplies the prediction.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    at: float = Field()
    output: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1)
    outputs: list[str] | None = None
    label: str = ""
    window: float | None = Field(
        default=None,
    )
    factor_id: str | None = None

    def as_observation(self) -> ObservedDataPoint:
        """
        The observation that reads this prediction; its value is not read.

        Returns
        -------
        ObservedDataPoint
            The observation.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the outputs or the label are not valid.
        """
        return ObservedDataPoint(
            at=self.at,
            output=self.output,
            outputs=self.outputs,
            label=self.label,
            value=0.0,
            window=self.window,
            factor_id=self.factor_id,
        )
```

## Threshold

Bases: `RangeChecked`

How far the statistic of a profile may rise above the fit inside an interval of `confidence_level`.

Build one with `chi_square`, `beale` or `bootstrap_calibrated`.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type                                        | Description                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`             | `{chi_square, beale, bootstrap_calibrated}` | The rule.                                                       |
| `confidence_level` | `float`                                     | The level of each pointwise interval, strictly between 0 and 1. |
| `bootstrap`        | \`BayesianBootstrap                         | ParametricBootstrap                                             |

Source code in `commol/profiles/results.py`

```python
class Threshold(RangeChecked):
    """
    How far the statistic of a profile may rise above the fit inside an
    interval of `confidence_level`.

    Build one with `chi_square`, `beale` or `bootstrap_calibrated`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    kind : {"chi_square", "beale", "bootstrap_calibrated"}
        The rule.
    confidence_level : float
        The level of each pointwise interval, strictly between 0 and 1.
    bootstrap : BayesianBootstrap | ParametricBootstrap | ResidualBootstrap | WildBootstrap | None
        The bootstrap of ``"bootstrap_calibrated"``; None otherwise.
    """  # noqa: E501

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    kind: Literal["chi_square", "beale", "bootstrap_calibrated"]
    confidence_level: float
    bootstrap: _ProfileBootstrap | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_bootstrap(self) -> Self:
        """A bootstrap goes with ``"bootstrap_calibrated"``, and only with it."""
        if (self.kind == "bootstrap_calibrated") != (self.bootstrap is not None):
            raise ValueError(
                "A bootstrap calibrates the threshold 'bootstrap_calibrated' and no "
                "other; build thresholds with Threshold.chi_square, Threshold.beale "
                "or Threshold.bootstrap_calibrated."
            )
        return self

    @classmethod
    def chi_square(cls, confidence_level: float) -> Self:
        """
        ``½ χ²₁(confidence_level)`` on ``−log L`` (Wilks): the threshold of a
        problem with observation models.

        It assumes that the models hold and that the statistic is near its
        large-sample distribution.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            The level of each interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        Threshold
            The threshold.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        return cls(kind="chi_square", confidence_level=confidence_level)

    @classmethod
    def beale(cls, confidence_level: float) -> Self:
        """
        Beale's threshold of a sum of squares:
        ``S(θ̂) · F(1, n − p; confidence_level) / (n − p)``, with ``n``
        observations of positive weight and ``p`` parameters.

        It assumes independent Gaussian errors of one variance, and is exact
        for a model linear in its parameters. It needs the loss ``"sse"``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            The level of each interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        Threshold
            The threshold.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        return cls(kind="beale", confidence_level=confidence_level)

    @classmethod
    def bootstrap_calibrated(
        cls, bootstrap: _ProfileBootstrap, confidence_level: float
    ) -> Self:
        """
        The threshold of each quantity calibrated by `bootstrap`
        (prepivoting, Beran 1988), for any loss.

        Each replicate of the bootstrap, rebuilt from the problem's seed as
        ``Calibrator.uncertainty(bootstrap)`` builds it, is fitted
        (``θ̂_b``) and then fitted again with the quantity held at its value
        at the fit of the original data: the rise of the replicate is
        ``PL_b(θ̂ⱼ) − L_b(θ̂_b)``. The threshold is the quantile
        `confidence_level` of the rises. It costs one fit and one refit per
        quantity for each replicate.

        Parameters
        ----------
        bootstrap : BayesianBootstrap | ParametricBootstrap | ResidualBootstrap | WildBootstrap
            The bootstrap, with its replicates and starts.
        confidence_level : float
            The level of each interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        Threshold
            The threshold.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """  # noqa: E501
        return cls(
            kind="bootstrap_calibrated",
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            bootstrap=bootstrap,
        )
```

## ProfileResult

Bases: `_FrozenResult`

The result of a profile likelihood.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type                            | Description                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fit`              | `CalibrationResult`             | The fit every profile starts from.                                                                                                                      |
| `quantity`         | `{parameter, prediction}`       | What the profiles hold fixed: parameters (ProfileLikelihood) or predictions (PredictionProfile).                                                        |
| `threshold`        | `Threshold`                     | The threshold the profiles ran with.                                                                                                                    |
| `profiles`         | `dict[str, Profile]`            | The profile of each parameter or prediction, by name.                                                                                                   |
| `intervals`        | `dict[str, ProfileInterval]`    | The interval of each.                                                                                                                                   |
| `verdicts`         | \`dict\[str, ProfileVerdictName | None\]\`                                                                                                                                                |
| `structure`        | `dict[str, ProfileStructure]`   | For each profile of a parameter that does not cross on both sides, what resetting the other parameters says.                                            |
| `tolerance`        | `float`                         | The numerical tolerance of the statistic: max(τ, ν), the tolerance of the optimizer and the noise floor of the objective at the fit.                    |
| `evaluation_floor` | \`float                         | None\`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `notes`            | `list[str]`                     | What a reader should know, such as a threshold below the tolerance or a refit below the fit.                                                            |
| `failed`           | `list[str]`                     | With a bootstrap threshold, each replicate that failed: "Replicate <index> failed: <reason>", also logged as a warning. Empty with any other threshold. |
| `not_converged`    | `int`                           | With a bootstrap threshold, the replicates kept although their optimizer did not converge; 0 with any other threshold.                                  |

Source code in `commol/profiles/results.py`

```python
class ProfileResult(_FrozenResult):
    """
    The result of a profile likelihood.

    Attributes
    ----------
    fit : CalibrationResult
        The fit every profile starts from.
    quantity : {"parameter", "prediction"}
        What the profiles hold fixed: parameters (`ProfileLikelihood`) or
        predictions (`PredictionProfile`).
    threshold : Threshold
        The threshold the profiles ran with.
    profiles : dict[str, Profile]
        The profile of each parameter or prediction, by name.
    intervals : dict[str, ProfileInterval]
        The interval of each.
    verdicts : dict[str, ProfileVerdictName | None]
        What the shape of each profile says: ``identifiable`` (it crosses the
        threshold on both sides), ``practically_non_identifiable`` (it stays
        below on a side, up to a bound or `max_steps`) or
        ``structurally_non_identifiable`` (flat within `tolerance` over the
        whole range). None when the threshold is below `tolerance`: the
        profile cannot tell a rise from numerical error.
    structure : dict[str, ProfileStructure]
        For each profile of a parameter that does not cross on both sides,
        what resetting the other parameters says.
    tolerance : float
        The numerical tolerance of the statistic: ``max(τ, ν)``, the
        tolerance of the optimizer and the noise floor of the objective at
        the fit.
    evaluation_floor : float | None
        The floor of a comparison of two evaluations of the objective; None
        when it cannot be computed.
    notes : list[str]
        What a reader should know, such as a threshold below the tolerance or
        a refit below the fit.
    failed : list[str]
        With a bootstrap threshold, each replicate that failed:
        ``"Replicate <index> failed: <reason>"``, also logged as a warning.
        Empty with any other threshold.
    not_converged : int
        With a bootstrap threshold, the replicates kept although their
        optimizer did not converge; 0 with any other threshold.
    """

    fit: CalibrationResult
    quantity: Literal["parameter", "prediction"]
    threshold: Threshold
    profiles: dict[str, Profile]
    intervals: dict[str, ProfileInterval]
    verdicts: dict[str, ProfileVerdictName | None]
    tolerance: float
    evaluation_floor: float | None = None
    structure: dict[str, ProfileStructure] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    notes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    failed: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    not_converged: int = 0

    def plot(
        self,
        output_file: str | None = None,
        config: "PlotConfig | None" = None,
        axes: "Figure | None" = None,
    ) -> "Figure":
        """
        Draw each profile: one panel per parameter or prediction, with the
        statistic of each point, the threshold, and the ends of the interval.

        A profile that stays under the threshold up to a bound is open on that
        side; a flat one stays near 0 over its whole range.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output_file : str | None
            Path to save the figure to. If None, the figure is only returned.
        config : PlotConfig | None
            Layout and style. If None, the defaults.
        axes : Figure | None
            A figure of commol to draw on: each panel is the `Axes` whose
            label is the name of its profile. If None, a new figure.

        Returns
        -------
        Figure
            The matplotlib figure.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``axes`` has no panel of a profile.
        ImportError
            If matplotlib is not installed (``pip install 'commol[plot]'``).
        """
        from commol.profiles.plots import profiles_figure

        return profiles_figure(self, output_file=output_file, config=config, axes=axes)
```

## Profile

| `multipliers`     | \`list\[float                           | None\]\`                                                                      |
| `converged`       | `list[bool]`                            | Whether each refit converged.                                                 |
| `ends`            | `tuple[ProfileEndName, ProfileEndName]` | Why the side below and the side above the fit end.                            |
| `evaluations`     | `int`                                   | Evaluations of the objective.                                                 |
| `replicate_rises` | \`list[float]                           | None\`                                                                        |

Source code in `commol/profiles/results.py`

```python
class Profile(_FrozenResult):
    """
    The profile of one parameter or prediction.

    Attributes
    ----------
    center : float
        The value at the fit.
    threshold : float
        The threshold of the statistic.
    values : list[float]
        The value of each point, increasing; the fit is one of them.
    statistics : list[float]
        The statistic of each point: the objective of its refit less that of
        the fit.
    parameters : list[dict[str, float]]
        Every parameter of each refit.
    multipliers : list[float | None]
        For a prediction, the multiplier of each point: minus the slope of
        the profile there.
    converged : list[bool]
        Whether each refit converged.
    ends : tuple[ProfileEndName, ProfileEndName]
        Why the side below and the side above the fit end.
    evaluations : int
        Evaluations of the objective.
    replicate_rises : list[float] | None
        With a bootstrap threshold, the rise of each replicate kept.
    box_crossings : tuple[str | None, str | None]
        For the side below and the side above, the free parameter whose bound
        makes the profile cross the threshold: it is on a bound at the
        crossing point that it is not on over the whole side from the fit.
        Such a side counts as open; its interval end stays, flagged in
        `ProfileResult.notes`. A parameter that stays on its bound from the
        fit to the crossing is not seen.
    refit_error : float | None
        For a parameter, ``|δ|``: the largest distance from the objective at
        the fit of a refit with the parameter at its fitted value, from each
        neighbour of the fit. A diagnostic of the optimizer.
    """

    center: float
    threshold: float
    values: list[float]
    statistics: list[float]
    parameters: list[dict[str, float]]
    multipliers: list[float | None]
    converged: list[bool]
    ends: tuple[ProfileEndName, ProfileEndName]
    evaluations: int
    replicate_rises: list[float] | None = None
    box_crossings: tuple[str | None, str | None] = (None, None)
    refit_error: float | None = None
```

## ProfileStructure

Bases: `_FrozenResult`

What resetting the other parameters says about a profile.

A profile is flat because other parameters compensate the parameter along it, or because nothing the data read depends on it. At each point of the profile inside the box, and at both ends of the box of the parameter, the other parameters are reset to their fitted values and the objective is evaluated once, with no optimizer; each reset is compared with the objective at the fit.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verdict`        | \`{in_combination, non_identifiable} | None\`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `largest_rise`   | \`float                              | None\`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `compensated_by` | `list[str]`                          | The parameters whose reset alone, where each moves most along the profile, raises it above the threshold. Noise parameters of observation models are never named. |
| `joint_rise`     | \`float                              | None\`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `undetermined`   | \`UndeterminedName                   | None\`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `on_bound`       | \`str                                | None\`                                                                                                                                                            |

Source code in `commol/profiles/results.py`

```python
class ProfileStructure(_FrozenResult):
    """
    What resetting the other parameters says about a profile.

    A profile is flat because other parameters compensate the parameter
    along it, or because nothing the data read depends on it. At each point
    of the profile inside the box, and at both ends of the box of the
    parameter, the other parameters are reset to their fitted values and the
    objective is evaluated once, with no optimizer; each reset is compared
    with the objective at the fit.

    Attributes
    ----------
    verdict : {"in_combination", "non_identifiable"} | None
        ``non_identifiable``: every reset is feasible and within the
        evaluation floor of the fit. ``in_combination``: the profile is flat
        and a feasible reset inside the box rises above the threshold. None
        otherwise, and `undetermined` says why.
    largest_rise : float | None
        The largest rise of a feasible reset over the objective at the fit;
        None when none was feasible.
    compensated_by : list[str]
        The parameters whose reset alone, where each moves most along the
        profile, raises it above the threshold. Noise parameters of
        observation models are never named.
    joint_rise : float | None
        The largest rise of resetting the parameters not named together, at
        the outermost point of each side, over the objective of that point,
        when it is above the evaluation floor: `compensated_by` may be
        incomplete. Infinite when such a reset is not feasible.
    undetermined : UndeterminedName | None
        Why there is no verdict.
    on_bound : str | None
        With ``undetermined="on_bound"``, the parameter on its bound at the
        fit.
    """

    verdict: Literal["in_combination", "non_identifiable"] | None
    largest_rise: float | None
    compensated_by: list[str]
    joint_rise: float | None
    undetermined: UndeterminedName | None = None
    on_bound: str | None = None

    def reason(self, name: str, threshold: float, floor: float | None) -> str:
        """
        The reason of the verdict of parameter `name` in a report.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name : str
            The parameter.
        threshold : float
            The threshold of its profile.
        floor : float | None
            The evaluation floor of the result.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The reason, which says that the verdict holds with the other
            parameters at their fitted values.
        """
        rise = (
            "no feasible reset"
            if self.largest_rise is None
            else (f"a largest rise of {self.largest_rise:.3g}")
        )
        if self.verdict == "in_combination":
            text = (
                f"profile likelihood: flat, and resetting the other parameters "
                f"gives {rise}, above the threshold {threshold:.3g}"
            )
            if self.compensated_by:
                text += (
                    f"; {name}, compensated by {', '.join(self.compensated_by)} "
                    "along its profile"
                )
            if self.joint_rise is not None:
                text += (
                    f"; the list may be incomplete (largest rise {self.joint_rise:.3g})"
                )
        elif self.verdict == "non_identifiable":
            text = (
                "profile likelihood: resetting the other parameters leaves the "
                f"objective within the evaluation floor {floor:.3g} of the fit "
                f"along the profile and at both ends of the box ({rise}): nothing "
                f"the data read depends on {name}"
            )
        else:
            text = (
                f"profile likelihood: flat, with no structural verdict "
                f"({self.undetermined}; {rise}, threshold {threshold:.3g})"
            )
        return f"{text}. {RESET_REASON}"
```

## Increments

Bases: `_Outputs`, `RangeChecked`

The increments of some outputs: at each end, the gain of their sum over `(end - window, end]`, as an observation with the window `window` reads it.

The positions of a quantity of increments are window ends, each at least `window` within the rounding of the window (`window_start` of `crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs`), so no window starts before 0.

Attributes:

| Name      | Type        | Description                                    |
| --------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `outputs` | `list[str]` | The outputs summed; one name is a list of one. |
| `window`  | `float`     | The width of each window, above 0.             |

Source code in `commol/quantities/quantities.py`

```python
class Increments(_Outputs, RangeChecked):
    """
    The increments of some outputs: at each end, the gain of their sum over
    ``(end - window, end]``, as an observation with the window `window`
    reads it.

    The positions of a quantity of increments are window ends, each at
    least `window` within the rounding of the window (`window_start` of
    `crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs`), so no window starts
    before 0.

    Attributes
    ----------
    outputs : list[str]
        The outputs summed; one name is a list of one.
    window : float
        The width of each window, above 0.
    """

    kind: Literal["increments"] = "increments"
    window: float = Field(description="The width.")

    def __init__(
        self,
        outputs: str | list[str],
        window: float,
        *,
        kind: Literal["increments"] = "increments",
    ) -> None:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, outputs=outputs, window=window, kind=kind)

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The series as a label reads it: the gain over windows of a width."""
        return f"{self.output_name} gain over windows of {_position_text(self.window)}"

    def check_ends(self, positions: Sequence[float]) -> None:
        """
        No window starts before 0, with the rule of the engine
        (`check_window_end` of `crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs`).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            With the message of the engine, if a window starts before 0.
        """
        for at in positions:
            commol_rs.calibration.check_window_end(at, self.window)
```

## ValueAt

Bases: `_OfSeries`, `_OneScalar`, `RangeChecked`

The value of a series at a position: the level of the outputs, or their gain over the window that ends there.

Attributes:

| Name     | Type    | Description                                           |
| -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `series` | \`Level | Increments\`                                          |
| `at`     | `float` | The position; with Increments, the end of the window. |
| `label`  | \`str   | None\`                                                |

Source code in `commol/quantities/quantities.py`

```python
class ValueAt(_OfSeries, _OneScalar, RangeChecked):
    """
    The value of a series at a position: the level of the outputs, or their
    gain over the window that ends there.

    Attributes
    ----------
    series : Level | Increments
        The series read; a name or a list of names is their `Level`.
    at : float
        The position; with `Increments`, the end of the window.
    label : str | None
        The name of the quantity in results and plots. If None, a name that
        says what the quantity reads.
    """

    kind: Literal["value_at"] = "value_at"
    at: float = Field(description="The position.")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _window_after_zero(self) -> Self:
        """The window of increments ends at least its width after 0."""
        self.series.check_ends([self.at])
        return self

    def default_label(self) -> str:
        """The series at `at`."""
        return f"{self.series.text} at {_position_text(self.at)}"
```

```python
class Gain(_Outputs, _OneScalar, RangeChecked):
    """
    The value at `end` minus the value at `start`: what entered a cumulative
    output over ``(start, end]``, as an observation with the window
    ``end - start`` that starts at exactly `start` reads it.

    Attributes
    ----------

    start : float
        The start of the window.
    end : float
        The end of the window, after `start`.
    label : str | None
        The name of the quantity in results and plots. If None, a name that
        says what the quantity reads.
    """

    kind: Literal["gain"] = "gain"
    start: float = Field(description="The start of the window.")
    end: float = Field(description="The end of the window.")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _end_after_start(self) -> Self:
        """A window ends after it starts."""
        if self.end <= self.start:
            raise ValueError(
                f"A gain ends after it starts, got start {self.start} and end "
                f"{self.end}"
            )
        return self

    def default_label(self) -> str:
        """The gain of `outputs` over the window."""
        start, end = _position_text(self.start), _position_text(self.end)
        return f"{self.output_name} gain over ({start}, {end}]"
```

## Peak

Bases: `_AtPositions`, `_OneScalar`, `RangeChecked`

The largest value of a series at the positions.

The series decides what the peak is: the peak of `Increments(acc, window=7)` at the ends 7, 14, ... is the largest gain of a window of 7, while the peak of the level of an accumulator, which never falls, is its value at the last position. A NaN at a position makes the peak NaN.

```python
class Trajectory(_AtPositions, RangeChecked):
    """
    The value of a series at each position: one scalar per position, for an
    analysis over the axis.

    Attributes
    ----------
    series : Level | Increments
        The series read; a name or a list of names is their `Level`.
    positions : list[float]
        The positions, ascending; with `Increments`, window ends.
    label : str | None
        The name of the series; each scalar is named after it and its
        position.
    """

        """The name of the series."""
        return self.label or self.series.text

        """Its name and each position."""
        return [(self._name(), at) for at in self.positions]
```

## Ratio

Bases: `_OneScalar`

The ratio of two quantities of one value each, numerator N over denominator D.

The ratio of a run whose denominator is 0 is NaN, also when the numerator is not 0, and follows the NaN rule of every method. A method that reduces the points of a design (`PRCC`, `Morris`, `Sobol`, `PolynomialChaos`) reads one value per point; with a stochastic engine, `replicate_rule` says how the replicates of a point combine. A `Propagation`, the `Scenarios` and the quantities of one run keep the ratio of each run.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `numerator`      | \`ValueAt                           | Gain                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `denominator`    | \`ValueAt                           | Gain                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `replicate_rule` | `{within, within_positive, pooled}` | "within": the mean of the ratio of each replicate, E[N/D]; a replicate with D = 0 leaves the point with no value. "within_positive": the mean of the ratio of the replicates with D > 0, E\[N/D |
| `label`          | \`str                               | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Source code in `commol/quantities/quantities.py`

```python
class Ratio(_OneScalar):
    """
    The ratio of two quantities of one value each, numerator N over
    denominator D.

    The ratio of a run whose denominator is 0 is NaN, also when the
    numerator is not 0, and follows the NaN rule of every method. A method
    that reduces the points of a design (`PRCC`, `Morris`, `Sobol`,
    `PolynomialChaos`) reads one value per point; with a stochastic engine,
    `replicate_rule` says how the replicates of a point combine. A `Propagation`,
    the `Scenarios` and the quantities of one run keep the ratio of each run.

    Attributes
    ----------
    numerator : ValueAt | Gain | Peak
        The quantity divided.
    denominator : ValueAt | Gain | Peak
        The quantity it is divided by.
    replicate_rule : {"within", "within_positive", "pooled"}
        ``"within"``: the mean of the ratio of each replicate, E[N/D]; a
        replicate with D = 0 leaves the point with no value.
        ``"within_positive"``: the mean of the ratio of the replicates with
        D > 0, E[N/D | D > 0]; a point with no such replicate has no value.
        ``"pooled"``: the ratio of the means, E[N]/E[D]; a point with
        E[D] = 0 has no value. With a deterministic engine, the three give
        N/D, and a point with D = 0 has no value.
    label : str | None
        The name of the quantity in results and plots. If None, a name that
        says what the quantity reads.
    """

    kind: Literal["ratio"] = "ratio"
    numerator: _Operand = Field(description="The quantity divided.")
    denominator: _Operand = Field(description="The quantity it is divided by.")
    replicate_rule: Literal["within", "within_positive", "pooled"] = Field(
        description="How the replicates of a stochastic run combine."
    )

    @field_validator("numerator", "denominator")
    @classmethod
    def _one_value(cls, value: QuantityBase) -> QuantityBase:
        """An operand gives one value per run."""
        if isinstance(value, PeakPosition | Trajectory):
            raise ValueError(
                f"A Ratio divides quantities of one value each (ValueAt, Gain, "
                f"Peak), got the {type(value).__name__} '{value.labels()[0]}'"
            )
        return value

    def default_label(self) -> str:
        """The numerator over the denominator."""
        numerator = self.numerator.labels()[0]
        denominator = self.denominator.labels()[0]
        return f"({numerator}) / ({denominator})"
```

## quantity_schedule

```python
quantity_schedule(quantities: Sequence[QuantityBase]) -> list[float]
```

The positions a run must report at for `quantities` to read it.

They are every position a quantity reads and the start of every window, sorted, each once. A `SimulationResults` of `Simulation.run_at(quantity_schedule(quantities))` holds them all, so `SimulationResults.quantities` reads it; a `Propagation` runs at the same positions.

Parameters:

| Name         | Type                 | Description     | Default    |
| ------------ | -------------------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| `quantities` | `Sequence[quantity]` | The quantities. | *required* |

Returns:

| Type          | Description               |
| ------------- | ------------------------- |
| `list[float]` | The positions, ascending. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description              |
| ------------ | ------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If there is no quantity. |

Source code in `commol/quantities/quantities.py`

```python
def quantity_schedule(quantities: Sequence[QuantityBase]) -> list[float]:
    """
    The positions a run must report at for `quantities` to read it.

    They are every position a quantity reads and the start of every window,
    sorted, each once. A `SimulationResults` of
    ``Simulation.run_at(quantity_schedule(quantities))`` holds them all, so
    `SimulationResults.quantities` reads it; a `Propagation` runs at the same
    positions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quantities : Sequence[quantity]
        The quantities.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        The positions, ascending.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If there is no quantity.
    """
    if not quantities:
        raise ValueError("Give at least one quantity of interest.")
    return commol_rs.inference.quantity_schedule(engine_json(list(quantities)))
```

## applied_parameters

```python
applied_parameters(values: CalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float], problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None, sample: SummarizedSample | None = None, confidence_level: float | None = None) -> AppliedParametersReport
```

Report every parameter of the model, and the values of its kind.

Call it on the model **after** `apply_calibration_parameters`. Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones. The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds `initial_amounts` and `category_splits`.

Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values. `factor` and `noise` parameters have no place in the model, so they are reported from `problem` when it is given.

`initial_amounts` gives each bin and each overridden compartment of an aggregate model its `amount` the engine builds and the `unit` of its bin, so bins of different units are reported side by side; no row is a share of a total. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a `None` amount as its "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments. `category_splits` gives each category its `fraction` of the group it splits, and that `group`: the categories a conditional stratification is conditioned on, empty when it splits every bin.

With a `sample` each entry gains an `interval` holding the weighted statistics of its draws (`ParameterSample.summary`). Every entry is in the unit it was calibrated in: a parameter in its own, an amount in the unit of its bin, and a category split as a fraction of its group.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type                 | Description | Default                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `values`           | \`CalibrationResult  | Mapping\`   | The calibration result, or a mapping of parameter id to value such as one draw of a sample. |
| `problem`          | \`CalibrationProblem | None\`      | The problem the values came from, used to report factor and noise parameters.               |
| `sample`           | \`ParameterSample    | None\`      | Draws of the parameters, such as the sample of an uncertainty method.                       |
| `confidence_level` | \`float              | None\`      | Confidence level of the intervals; required with a sample.                                  |

Returns:

| Type                      | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AppliedParametersReport` | Key parameters and the sections of the kind (initial_amounts and category_splits for an aggregate model), preceded by confidence_level when there is one. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If a sample is given without a confidence level. |

Source code in `commol/_model/model.py`

```python
def applied_parameters(
    self,
    values: CalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float],
    problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None,
    sample: "SummarizedSample | None" = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
) -> "AppliedParametersReport":
    """
    Report every parameter of the model, and the values of its kind.

    Call it on the model **after** `apply_calibration_parameters`. Each
    entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set
    it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted
    ones. The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind
    (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds
    ``initial_amounts`` and ``category_splits``.

    Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a
    series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values.
    ``factor`` and ``noise`` parameters have no place in the model, so
    they are reported from `problem` when it is given.

    ``initial_amounts`` gives each bin and each overridden compartment of
    an aggregate model its ``amount`` the engine builds and the ``unit``
    of its bin, so bins of different units are reported side by side; no
    row is a share of a total. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a ``None``
    amount as its "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch
    some of its compartments. ``category_splits`` gives each category its
    ``fraction`` of the group it splits, and that ``group``: the
    categories a conditional stratification is conditioned on, empty when
    it splits every bin.

    With a `sample` each entry gains an ``interval`` holding the weighted
    statistics of its draws (`ParameterSample.summary`). Every entry is in
    the unit it was calibrated in: a parameter in its own, an amount in
    the unit of its bin, and a category split as a fraction of its group.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values : CalibrationResult | Mapping
        The calibration result, or a mapping of parameter id to value such
        as one draw of a sample.
    problem : CalibrationProblem | None, optional
        The problem the values came from, used to report factor and noise

    sample : ParameterSample | None, optional
```
