## Transition

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a rule for system evolution.

Attributes:

| Name               | Type                   | Description                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`               | `str`                  | Id of the transition.                                            |
| `source`           | `list[str]`            | The origin compartments.                                         |
| `target`           | `list[str]`            | The destination compartments.                                    |
| `accumulators`     | `list[str]`            | Ids of the accumulators that add up the flow of this transition. |
| `rate`             | \`str                  | None\`                                                           |
| `stratified_rates` | \`list[StratifiedRate] | None\`                                                           |
| `per_compartment`  | \`bool                 | None\`                                                           |
| `impulse_at`       | \`list[float]          | None\`                                                           |
| `impulse_every`    | \`tuple[float, float]  | None\`                                                           |

Source code in `commol/_model/transition.py`

```python
class Transition(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a rule for system evolution.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Id of the transition.
    source : list[str]
        The origin compartments.
    target : list[str]
        The destination compartments.
    accumulators : list[str]
        Ids of the accumulators that add up the flow of this transition.
    rate : str | None
        Default mathematical formula, parameter name, or constant value for the flow.
        Used when no stratified rate matches. ``ModelBuilder.add_transition``
        writes a number as its string.

        Operators: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ or ** (power)
        Functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, min, max, if, etc.
        Constants: pi, e

        Note: Both ^ and ** are supported for exponentiation (** is converted to ^).

        Examples:
        - "k1" (parameter reference)
        - "0.5" (constant, can also be passed as float 0.5)
        - "k1 * A * B / total" (mathematical formula)
        - "0.3 * sin(2 * pi * t / 365)" (formula that changes along the axis)
        - "2^10" or "2**10" (power: both syntaxes work)
    stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRate] | None
        Stratification-specific rates. Each rate applies to compartments that match
        all specified stratification conditions.
    per_compartment : bool | None
        When True, the id of each source and target bin in a rate reads the
        compartment of each flow; any other bin keeps its total. A transition
        between categories ignores it.
    impulse_at : list[float] | None
        Positions on the axis where the transition is an impulse: at each one,
        the rate is a fraction (proportional) or an amount (absolute) moved at
        once. Between them the transition moves nothing.
    impulse_every : tuple[float, float] | None
        ``(period, offset)``: the transition is an impulse at ``offset``,
        ``offset + period``, ``offset + 2 * period``, and so on. At most one
        of `impulse_at` and `impulse_every` is set.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Id of the transition.")
    source: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Origin compartments.")
    target: list[str] = Field(default=..., description="Destination compartments.")
    accumulators: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Cumulative event counters incremented by this transition flow.",
    )

    rate: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description=(
            "Default rate expression (fallback when no stratified rate matches). "
            "Can be a parameter reference (e.g., 'k1'), a constant (e.g., '0.5'), "
            "or a mathematical expression (e.g., 'k1 * A * B / total')."
        ),
    )

    stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None = Field(
        default=None, description="List of stratification-specific rates"
    )

    per_compartment: bool | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "When True, the id of each source and target bin in a rate reads "
            "the compartment of each flow; any other bin keeps its total. A "
            "transition between categories ignores it."
        ),
    )

    impulse_at: list[float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Positions on the axis where the transition is an impulse: at each "
            "one, the rate is a fraction (proportional) or an amount (absolute) "
            "moved at once. Between them the transition moves nothing."
        ),
    )

    impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "(period, offset): the transition is an impulse at offset, "
            "offset + period, offset + 2 * period, ..."
        ),
    )

    @property
    def is_impulse(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the transition is an impulse rather than a continuous flow."""
        return self.impulse_at is not None or self.impulse_every is not None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _validate_impulse(self) -> Self:
        """
        Check the impulse with the rule of the engine (`check_impulse` of
        `crates/commol-model/src/values.rs`): one of `impulse_at` and
        `impulse_every`, at least one position on the axis, a positive period
        and an offset that is not negative.
        """
        commol_rs.model.check_impulse(self.id, self.impulse_at, self.impulse_every)
        return self

    @field_validator("rate")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_rate(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Check the rate, when there is one, with the parser of the engine."""
        if value is None:
            return value
        return _checked_rate(value)
```


Whether the transition is an impulse rather than a continuous flow.

## Engine

The engine's list of engines (`crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs`) validates the settings: settings of another engine raise an error that names both. `ODESolver` is documented in [Simulation API](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/simulation/index.md).

## ModelEngine

Bases: `BaseModel`

The engine that runs a model, and its settings.

Attributes:

| Name       | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`     | `str`            | Name of an engine of the engine's list, such as "DifferenceEquations" (discrete time) or "DifferentialEquations" (continuous time). The engine must run the kind of the structure of the model. |
| `settings` | \`EngineSettings | None\`                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Source code in `commol/engines/engine.py`

```python
class ModelEngine(BaseModel):
    """
    The engine that runs a model, and its settings.

    Attributes
    ----------
    type : str
        Name of an engine of the engine's list, such as
        ``"DifferenceEquations"`` (discrete time) or
        ``"DifferentialEquations"`` (continuous time). The engine must run the
        kind of the structure of the model.
    settings : EngineSettings | None
        Settings of that engine; None uses its defaults.
        ``DifferentialEquations`` takes `ODESolver`, ``StochasticEvents``
        takes `StochasticEventsSettings` and ``StochasticSteps`` takes
        `StochasticStepsSettings`.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    type: str = Field(..., description="Name of the engine.")
    settings: EngineSettings | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Settings of the engine; None uses its defaults."
    )

    @field_validator("settings", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _settings_of_the_engine(
        cls,
        value: EngineSettings | Mapping[str, JsonValue] | None,
        info: ValidationInfo,
    ) -> EngineSettings | Mapping[str, JsonValue] | None:
        """Read settings given as a mapping with the class of their engine."""
        settings_class = _SETTINGS.get(info.data.get("type", ""))
        if isinstance(value, Mapping) and settings_class is not None:
            return settings_class.model_validate(value)
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check_settings(self) -> Self:
        """Ask the engine's list whether it has the engine and the settings."""
        settings_json = None if self.settings is None else engine_json(self.settings)
        commol_rs.engine.EngineType(engine_json(self.type)).check_settings(
            settings_json
        )
        return self
```

## Initial conditions

`Aggregate` holds the fields and methods of `InitialConditions`, and checks them against the process when the model is built.

## InitialConditions

Bases: `BaseModel`

How much starts where: the amount of each bin and the split of it.

Every amount is in the unit of its bin, so bins of different units, such as a count and a concentration, start without a total over them. `Aggregate` holds these fields and their methods; the checks against the bins and the stratifications of the process are in `Aggregate.check_model`.

Attributes:

| Name                       | Type                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bin_amounts`              | \`dict\[str, float            | None\]\`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `stratification_fractions` | `dict[str, dict[str, float]]` | The fraction of each category, by stratification id and category: the split of the amount of every bin the stratification applies to; each from 0 to 1, and a sum of 1 within 1e-6. A conditional stratification splits only the group its conditions select. |
| `compartment_amounts`      | `dict[str, float]`            | Amounts of single expanded compartments, by compartment name, applied after the expansion.                                                                                                                                                                    |

Source code in `commol/_model/initial_conditions.py`

```python
class InitialConditions(BaseModel):
    """
    How much starts where: the amount of each bin and the split of it.

    Every amount is in the unit of its bin, so bins of different units, such
    as a count and a concentration, start without a total over them.
    `Aggregate` holds these fields and their methods; the checks against the
    bins and the stratifications of the process are in
    `Aggregate.check_model`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    bin_amounts : dict[str, float | None]
        The amount of each bin at the start, by bin id, in the unit of the
        bin; finite and not negative. None leaves an amount for calibration.
    stratification_fractions : dict[str, dict[str, float]]
        The fraction of each category, by stratification id and category: the
        split of the amount of every bin the stratification applies to; each
        from 0 to 1, and a sum of 1 within 1e-6. A conditional stratification
        splits only the group its conditions select.
    compartment_amounts : dict[str, float]
        Amounts of single expanded compartments, by compartment name, applied
        after the expansion.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    bin_amounts: dict[str, float | None] = Field(
        ...,
        description=(
            "The amount of each bin, by bin id, in the unit of the bin. None "
            "leaves an amount for calibration."
        ),
    )
    stratification_fractions: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="The fraction of each category, by stratification id.",
    )
    compartment_amounts: dict[str, float] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "Amounts of single expanded compartments, applied after the expansion."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _reject_fractions_of_a_total(cls, data: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
        """Name the field of amounts that replaces a field of fractions.

        A total over bins of different units has no meaning, so the initial
        state is stated as amounts, and a structure with ``total``,
        ``bin_fractions`` or ``compartment_fractions`` is rejected with the
        field to use.
        """
        if isinstance(data, Mapping):
            stated = [field for field in _FRACTION_FIELDS if field in data]
            if stated:
                replacements = sorted({_FRACTION_FIELDS[field] for field in stated})
                raise ValueError(
                    f"An aggregate structure states the amount of each bin in "
                    f"the unit of the bin, not fractions of a total: replace "
                    f"{', '.join(stated)} with {' and '.join(replacements)}, "
                    f'such as bin_amounts={{"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}}.'
                )
        return data

    @field_validator("bin_amounts")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_bin_amounts(
        cls, value: dict[str, float | None]
    ) -> dict[str, float | None]:
        """Check every bin amount with the rule of the engine."""
        commol_rs.model.check_bin_amounts(list(value.items()))
        return value

    @field_validator("stratification_fractions")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_stratification_fractions(
        cls, value: dict[str, dict[str, float]]
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
        """Check the fractions of every stratification with the rule of the
        engine."""
        _check_fractions(value)
        return value

    @field_validator("compartment_amounts")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_compartment_amounts(cls, value: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Check every compartment amount with the rule of the engine."""
        commol_rs.model.check_compartment_amounts(list(value.items()))
        return value

    def get_uncalibrated_bins(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Get list of bin IDs that have uncalibrated amounts (value = None).

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            List of bin IDs with uncalibrated initial conditions.
        """
        return [bin_id for bin_id, amount in self.bin_amounts.items() if amount is None]

    def get_categories_with_fractions(self) -> set[str]:
        """
        Get the categories that have a declared initial fraction.

        Returns
        -------
        set[str]
            Category names collected from ``stratification_fractions``. A
            category declared on a stratification but absent from the initial
            conditions is not included.
        """
        return {
            category
            for categories in self.stratification_fractions.values()
            for category in categories
        }

    def resolve_category(self, category: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Resolve a category id to its stratification and its bare name.

        A qualified id (``group:g1``) names the stratification. A bare name
        must be declared by exactly one stratification.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A bare or qualified category id.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[str, str]
            The stratification id and the bare category name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        stratification_id, separator, name = category.rpartition(CATEGORY_SEPARATOR)
        owners = [
            stratification
            for stratification, categories in self.stratification_fractions.items()
            if (not separator or stratification == stratification_id)
            and name in categories
        ]
        if len(owners) > 1:
            qualified = " or ".join(
                f"'{owner}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{name}'" for owner in owners
            )
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' is ambiguous: it is declared by "
                f"stratifications {owners}. Qualify it as {qualified}."
            )
        if not owners:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Category '{category}' not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available categories: {sorted(self.get_categories_with_fractions())}"
            )
        return owners[0], name

    def category_id(self, stratification: str, category: str) -> str:
        """
        Shortest id that names a category without ambiguity.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stratification : str
            Id of the stratification that declares the category.
        category : str
            Bare category name.

        Returns
        -------
        str
            The bare name, or ``stratification:category`` when another
            stratification declares a category of the same name.
        """
        declaring = sum(
            category in categories
            for categories in self.stratification_fractions.values()
        )
        if declaring > 1:
            return f"{stratification}{CATEGORY_SEPARATOR}{category}"
        return category

    def get_category_fraction(self, category: str) -> float:
        """
        Get the fraction of a category within the group it subdivides.

        Parameters
        ----------
        category : str
            A category id, bare or qualified (``group:g1``).

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The declared fraction, relative to the group the category's
            stratification applies to rather than to the whole model.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the category is not found or a bare name is ambiguous.
        """
        stratification, name = self.resolve_category(category)
        return self.stratification_fractions[stratification][name]

    def _updated_fractions(
        self, stratification: str, named: Mapping[str, float]
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """The fractions of a single stratification after an update that
        names ``named``; the one category left unnamed takes the rest."""
        categories = self.stratification_fractions[stratification]
        unnamed = [category for category in categories if category not in named]
        if len(unnamed) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot update stratification '{stratification}': "
                f"categories {sorted(unnamed)} were left unnamed. At most one "
                f"category may be omitted, so that it can take the remaining "
                f"fraction."
            )
        remainder = max(0.0, 1.0 - sum(named.values()))
        return {category: named.get(category, remainder) for category in categories}

    def update_stratification_fractions(self, fractions: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Update stratification category fractions by category name.

        Categories belonging to several stratifications may be given in one
        call. A category name declared by more than one stratification must be
        qualified with its stratification, as in ``group:g1``. Within each
        stratification, at most one category may be omitted; the omitted
        category receives the rest of 1, or 0 when the given values pass 1.
        The fractions of every stratification are checked with the rule of the
        engine before any of them changes.

        Parameters
        ----------
        fractions : Mapping[str, float]
            Dictionary mapping category names, bare or qualified, to their new
            fraction values.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a category is not found or is ambiguous, or a stratification
            has more than one category omitted; with the message of the
            engine, if a fraction is not from 0 to 1 or the fractions of a
            stratification do not sum to 1 within 1e-6.
        """
        by_stratification: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        for category, value in fractions.items():
            stratification, name = self.resolve_category(category)
            by_stratification.setdefault(stratification, {})[name] = value

        updated = {
            stratification: self._updated_fractions(stratification, named)
            for stratification, named in by_stratification.items()
        }
        _check_fractions(updated)
        for stratification, categories in updated.items():
            self.stratification_fractions[stratification].update(categories)

    def _upsert_compartment_amounts(self, amounts: Mapping[str, float]) -> None:
        """
        Upsert per-compartment overrides by expanded compartment name.

        A compartment already present in ``compartment_amounts`` has its
        amount replaced; a new one is appended. Compartment names depend on
        the expansion of the process, so
        :meth:`~commol._model.aggregate.Aggregate.update_compartment_amounts`
        validates them against the engine, not here.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            With the message of the engine, if an amount is not finite or is
            negative.
        """
        commol_rs.model.check_compartment_amounts(list(amounts.items()))
        self.compartment_amounts.update(amounts)

    def update_bin_amounts(self, amounts: Mapping[str, float | None]) -> None:
        """
        Update bin amounts by bin ID.

        Every amount is checked before any bin changes, so a rejected call
        leaves the initial conditions unchanged. The bins of one unit keep no
        sum: to move an amount between bins, update every bin involved.

        Parameters
        ----------
        amounts : Mapping[str, float | None]
            Dictionary mapping bin IDs to their new amount, in the unit of the
            bin. None marks a bin that needs calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a bin ID is not found in the initial conditions, or, with the
            message of the engine, an amount is not finite or is negative.
        """
        unknown = sorted(set(amounts) - set(self.bin_amounts))
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Bin(s) {unknown} not found in initial conditions. "
                f"Available bins: {list(self.bin_amounts)}"
            )
        commol_rs.model.check_bin_amounts(list(amounts.items()))
        self.bin_amounts.update(amounts)
```

# Changelog

# Changelog

[Back to Home](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/index.md)

All notable changes to Commol will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- `ObservedDataPoint(scale=...)`: a known positive number, 1 by default, that multiplies the prediction of the observation, with its factor. A count model reads the mean `scale · model`, so counts observed on a known part of what the model describes stay whole. The loss, the likelihood, the predictive, the scores, the figures and the `observed` block of a report (`scales`) read it. See [Observations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-observations/#known-shares-scales).
- `GibbsResult` and `ConformalResult` give `block_length` and `block_length_estimates`, as the bootstraps, the jackknife and the sandwich do: the length a method ran with, and with `block_length="auto"` the estimate of each series, by label. `GibbsResult` gives them for `InformationMatchingEta` and `BootstrapCoverageEta`, and `None` for a number `η`; `ConformalResult` for `JackknifePlus` and `EnbPI`, and `None` for the variants without blocks. See [Sequential Monte Carlo](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/smc/#what-means) and [Conformal Prediction Intervals](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/conformal/#results-plots-and-reports).
- `ProfileIdentifiability(result=profiles)` in `commol.identifiability`: the identifiability report of the verdicts of a `ProfileResult`, run through `Calibrator.identifiability` as every identifiability method. It runs no model, and it refuses the profiles of another problem with a `ValueError` that names the parameters of both. See [Profile Likelihood](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/profiles/#verdicts-and-the-identifiability-report).

### Changed

- **Breaking:** `Calibrator.delta_band(result, positions, confidence_level)` is `LocalResult.delta_band(calibrator, positions, confidence_level)`, a method of the result of `Laplace` and of `Sandwich`. `DeltaBand` is documented with `commol.local`. Migration: `calibrator.delta_band(laplace, [10, 20], 0.9)` is `laplace.delta_band(calibrator, [10, 20], 0.9)`. See [Local Approximations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/local/index.md).
- **Breaking:** `ProfileResult.identifiability()` is removed. Migration: `profiles.identifiability()` is `calibrator.identifiability(ProfileIdentifiability(result=profiles))`.
- **Breaking:** each public name outside the main flow lives in the module of its page of the guide, and the root `commol` holds only the main flow: build (`ModelBuilder`, `Model`, `StratificationCondition`, `StratifiedRate`, `SeriesValue`, `AxisUnits`, `AxisPattern`), the structures (`Aggregate`, `Complete`, `Groups`), simulate (`Simulation`, `InfeasibleStateError`), calibrate (`Calibrator`, `CalibrationProblem`, `CalibrationParameter`, `CalibrationConstraint`, `ObservedDataPoint`, `NelderMeadConfig`, `ParticleSwarmConfig`, `Quantile`) and `build_info`. The modules are `commol.engines`, `commol.plotting`, `commol.parallelism`, `commol.distributions`, `commol.quantities`, `commol.observations`, `commol.uncertainty`, `commol.scores`, `commol.resampling`, `commol.profiles`, `commol.local`, `commol.smc`, `commol.conformal`, `commol.identifiability` and `commol.sensitivity`; the [API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md) lists the names of each. The packages `commol.api`, `commol.context` and `commol.utils` and the module `commol.constants` are removed: the code is in the package of its module, and the code of the root in private packages. Migration: `from commol import BayesianBootstrap, Predictive` is `from commol.resampling import BayesianBootstrap` and `from commol.uncertainty import Predictive`; `commol.threads(2)` is `commol.parallelism.threads(2)`.
- **Breaking:** each module logs as `commol.<module>`, such as `commol.resampling`, and the main flow as `commol`; the loggers of the old paths, such as `commol.api.calibrator`, are gone. Migration: a handler or a level on `commol` still reaches every message; read one module with `logging.getLogger("commol.resampling")`.
- **Breaking:** a pickle of an object of commol 0.10 does not load: the path of each class changed. Migration: save a model with `Model.to_json` and a result with `model_dump_json`, which do not depend on the path.
- **Breaking:** `ParticleSwarmConfig` is one class with plain fields, and its chained methods `.inertia`, `.acceleration`, `.velocity`, `.mutation`, `.improvement_stop` and `.radius_stop` and their `*_config` properties are removed, with the `PSO*` classes of `commol.context.calibration` and the `PSO*` enumerations of `commol.context.constants`. Each strategy is a name (`inertia`, `acceleration`, `mutation`, `initialization`), and its numbers are fields: `inertia_factor`, `inertia_min`, `inertia_max`, `cognitive`, `social`, `cognitive_initial`, `cognitive_final`, `social_initial`, `social_final`, `mutation_scale`, `mutation_probability`, `mutation_application`, `velocity_clamp_factor`, `velocity_mutation_threshold`, `improvement_window`, `improvement_tol_abs`, `improvement_tol_rel` and `radius_tol`. A number set without its strategy raises `ValueError`. Migration: `ParticleSwarmConfig().inertia("chaotic", w_min=0.4, w_max=0.9).improvement_stop(window=30, tol_abs=1e-12, tol_rel=1e-9)` is `ParticleSwarmConfig(inertia="chaotic", inertia_min=0.4, inertia_max=0.9, improvement_window=30, improvement_tol_abs=1e-12, improvement_tol_rel=1e-9)`; `c1_*` is `cognitive_*`, `c2_*` is `social_*`, `.velocity(clamp_factor=…, mutation_threshold=…)` is `velocity_clamp_factor=…, velocity_mutation_threshold=…` and `.radius_stop(tol)` is `radius_tol=tol`. See [Particle swarm](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-optimizers/#particle-swarm).
- **Breaking:** the members that converted an object to the engine are removed: `Calibrator.rust_problem` and `rust_optimizer`, `rust_predictive`, `rust_observation_draws` and `rust_log_score` of `Calibrator` and `SensitivityAnalysis`, `SensitivityAnalysis.rust_analysis`, `rust_parameters` and `rust_prior` of the distributions, `Priors.rust_priors`, `InputSpace.rust_distributions`, `rust_json` of the quantities and `ParameterSample.rust_sample`; the predictive members of a source are private. Migration: build a predictive with `Predictive` and score it with `commol.scores`, as before; the engine reads each object from the JSON of its `model_dump()`.
- **Breaking:** the tag of `Complete` and `Groups` in the JSON of a model is `kind`, in place of `type`. Migration: in a saved model, rename the key `"type"` of each `neighbors` entry to `"kind"`.
- **Breaking:** `Model.describe()` gives a graph of the strata, between the graph of the bins and the graph of the compartments, when the model moves amounts between categories, so `ModelDescription.graphs()` gives three graphs for such a model. A move between categories, also one by a stratified rate whose condition has `to`, is an edge between categories, not an edge from a bin to itself. The graphs of the bins and of the strata hold one edge per pair of nodes, labelled with the formula of its one rate or with the parameters that its rates read, and one node `none` for the inflows and one for the outflows; the label no longer starts with the id of the transition. The Markdown rendering draws both graphs. See [The state graphs](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/describing-models/#the-state-graphs).
- Each data object reaches the engine as the JSON of its `model_dump()`: the model, the calibration problem and each inference method, whole. A setting that the engine rejects raises `ValueError` with the path of its field before the message of the engine (`optimization_config.inertia_factor: inertia_factor is a number greater than 0, got -1`). `NelderMeadConfig`, `ParticleSwarmConfig`, the four bootstraps and the observation noises have a field `kind` with a default, the tag of their union. The engine fits the problem for each method that needs a fit, and calibrates `η` and the threshold of a profile. The results are the same for the same settings and seed.
- An unknown name of an engine, a model kind, the levels of `commol.set_threads`, or the `score` or `by` of a conformal method gives the message of the reader of the engine, which lists the valid names, such as `` unknown variant `Stochastic`, expected one of `DifferenceEquations`, … `` or `` score: unknown variant `other`, expected one of `absolute`, `normalized`, `spread` ``. A conformal method without `score` or `by` gives `` missing field `score` ``.
- The JSON of every result (`model_dump_json`) is standard JSON: a number that is not finite is the text `"Infinity"`, `"-Infinity"` or `"NaN"`, as at the port of the engine. Before, `ParameterSample`, `SMCResult`, `JackknifeResult`, `ConformalResult`, `PredictionIntervals` and `SeriesIntervals` wrote the bare `Infinity` and `NaN`, which a standard JSON reader rejects, and the other results wrote `null`, which did not load back. A result reads its JSON back equal, a NaN included, and a result that 0.10 saved with bare `Infinity` or `NaN` still loads.
- A method that fits the problem before it runs (the bootstraps, the jackknife, the local approximations, the conformal methods, the profiles, and the Gibbs posterior with a calibration of `η`) no longer logs `Starting calibration …` at info level, since the engine runs that fit. A start of the fit that fails is still logged as a warning, and `Calibrator.run` still logs its start.
- A formula has at most 100 000 nodes (numbers, variables, operators and calls), next to its limit of 100 levels of nesting: a longer one raises `ValueError` when its object is built, before it compiles. A message of the parser or of the compiler quotes the formula cut after its first 80 characters. See [Limits of the parser](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/mathematical-expressions/#limits-of-the-parser).
- A rate gives the same description with or without spaces: the description and its LaTeX are written from the tree that the parser of the engine reads, so `k1*A*B/total` and `k1 * A * B / total` give one description. A formula shows one space around each operator, only the parentheses that its grouping needs, `^` for a power and each number as its value (`1e-5` shows as `1e-05`, `2.0` as `2`). In LaTeX, a power raises its exponent (`A^{2}`), `%` is `\bmod` and a comparison has its symbol (`\leq`). See [The equations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/describing-models/#the-equations).
- The unit check reads the tree of the engine: it reads `!` in a condition and a variable named like a word of Python, such as `lambda`, and a formula outside the language gives the message of the parser.
- **Breaking:** `AxisUnits.rate_from_mean_span` takes a required keyword `keep`, with no default: `"survival"` gives the rate of today, which keeps the exponential survival at every step (`1 - exp(-1/n)` on a per-step engine), and `"mean"` gives `1/n`, whose mean residence is `n` steps on a per-step engine. A continuous engine gives `1/n` with both. With `keep="mean"`, a per-step engine rejects a span shorter than one step with `ValueError`. Migration: add `keep="survival"` to keep each rate as it is. Another value of `keep` raises `ValueError` with the message of the engine, `` unknown variant `median`, expected `survival` or `mean` ``. See [Units of the axis](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/core-concepts/#units-of-the-axis).
- **Breaking:** the package root exports only the names a user writes: 99 names, down from 147. A result is reached from the object that returns it, typed as the return of that member and documented on its page; it is not an import. The names that leave `commol` are the results (`SimulationResults`, `SimulationReplicates`, `ReplicateRuns`, `CalibrationResult`, `CalibrationEvaluation`, `CalibrationHistory`, `StartSummary`, `ModelDescription`, `Process`, `BuildInfo`, and the result of every uncertainty, identifiability and sensitivity method with its parts), the bases `ModelStructure`, `InferenceMethod`, `UncertaintyMethod`, `IdentifiabilityMethod` and `SensitivityMethod`, the union `ObservationModel`, and the functions `sample`, `windowed_totals` and `ci_percentiles`. Migration: remove the import and annotate with the class of its module, such as `commol.api.results.SimulationResults`, or with no annotation. See [API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md).
- **Breaking:** a condition is a `StratificationCondition` and a stratified rate is a `StratifiedRate`, which the package root exports; `ModelBuilder.add_stratification`, `ModelBuilder.add_transition` and `AxisPattern` take them, not dicts, and `ConditionDict` and `StratifiedRateDict` are removed. A `StratifiedRate` checks its rate with the parser of the engine when it is built, with `$compartment` set to the name of a compartment, and keeps a number as its string. Migration: `{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}` is `StratificationCondition(stratification="group", category="g1")`, and `{"conditions": [...], "rate": "k1"}` is `StratifiedRate(conditions=[...], rate="k1")`. See [Stratified rates](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/transitions/#stratified-rates).
- **Breaking:** a choice among names is a string of a `Literal`, not an enum or an alias: `CalibrationParameter.parameter_type` is one of `"parameter"`, `"initial_condition"`, `"factor"` and `"noise"`, `CalibrationProblem.loss_function` one of `"sse"`, `"rmse"` and `"mae"`, and the `mode` of `AxisPattern.combine` one of `"sum"`, `"max"` and `"min"`. `commol.context.constants` (`CalibrationParameterType`, `LossFunction`, `OptimizationAlgorithm`), `CombineMode` and `AxisPattern.SUM`, `MAX` and `MIN` are removed, with the aliases of strings of the signatures, such as `DescriptionFormat` and `Pooling`. Another value raises the `ValidationError` of pydantic, or `ValueError` for `combine`, which lists the values. Migration: write the string, such as `mode="max"` for `mode=AxisPattern.MAX`.
- **Breaking:** `SimulationResults.sample(ids, at)` and `SimulationResults.windowed_totals(ids, window, at=None)` read the bins, the accumulators and the outputs of a run; `Simulation.sample` and `Simulation.windowed_totals` are removed. Results without a model read output names. Migration: `simulation.windowed_totals(results, ["cum"], 7)` is `results.windowed_totals(["cum"], 7)`. See [Windowed totals](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#windowed-totals).
- **Breaking:** the pydantic validators of the public classes are private: each name starts with `_`, such as `CalibrationProblem._validate_loss_or_models`.

### Removed

- **Breaking:** `commol.utils.security` is removed, with `SecurityConfig`, `SecurityError`, `validate_expression_security` and the `config=` argument of `AxisPattern.combine` and `AxisPattern.from_formula`. The parser of the engine is the only check of a formula: a rate, a formula parameter, a calibration constraint or an axis pattern that it rejects raises `ValueError` with its message, and no setting changes its limits. Remove the `config=` argument, and catch `ValueError` instead of `SecurityError`. A formula of the language that the old text guards rejected is now valid: a name with letters outside ASCII (`α * β`), a name such as `__import__`, `os` or `my_key`, a number such as `1e400`, `nan` as the name of a variable, and a formula of more than 1000 nodes, 10 000 characters or 10 levels of nesting, within the limits of the parser. The build still rejects a variable that the model does not define. See [Limits of the parser](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/mathematical-expressions/#limits-of-the-parser).

### Fixed

- A number that is not finite in a model or in the settings of an engine reached the engine as `null`. An infinite tolerance of `ODESolver` raised a message about the type of the setting, and an infinite parameter value failed when the model ran, with a message about a parameter index. Such a number now reaches the engine as its text, as every setting does: `ODESolver(atol=float("inf"))` raises `atol is a finite number greater than 0, got inf`, and the infinite parameter value is rejected when the engine is built, with the name of the parameter.
- The flow of a proportional rate is the whole rate times its source, in the description and in the unit check: a rate `k1 + k2` from `B` is `(k1 + k2) * B`; before, both read `k1 + k2 * B`, and the unit check of such a model failed. In LaTeX, a division followed by a product is a fraction times the product: the flow of a proportional rate `a / b` from `B` is `\frac{a}{b} \cdot B`, no longer `\frac{a}{b \cdot B}`.

### Documentation

- [Design principles](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/design-principles/index.md): the structure, the rules of each unit and of the interface, and the proof that every part of the code follows. «Before you change code» of `AGENTS.md` links them. `tests/suite/test_architecture.py` fails when a crate of `crates/` depends on PyO3 or on the bridge.
- A numbered list of the documentation keeps its first number, and a line inside a paragraph that starts with a number and a period, such as `512.`, stays in its paragraph: the site reads lists with `sane_lists`.

## [0.10.2] - 2026-10-24

This release makes the engine the one source of every rule: the range of each setting, the values of a model, the windows, the checks of a model and a calibration, and the language of formulas, which commol now reads with a parser of its own. A value that was valid stays valid, and an invalid one still raises `ValueError` when its object is built, but the messages are the engine's. Read the changes before you upgrade: seeded results change value, as every draw comes from one seed scheme in which neighbouring seeds share no replicate; a chain of powers groups from the right, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` is 512; `BootstrapCoverageEta` gives a slightly different η; a stratification fraction outside 0 to 1 is rejected; and two results are equal when their values, a NaN included, and their positions, seed and model are equal, so a run is no longer equal to a plain `dict`. See [Building models](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/building-models/index.md) and [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/index.md).

### Changed

- The engine holds the range rule of every setting: a count, a share, a length, a scale, a tolerance, a bound of an optimizer, an observation, an observation model, an axis pattern, a distribution, a quantity of interest and the setting of an uncertainty, identifiability or sensitivity method. A value outside its range still raises `ValueError` when the object is built, and the same values are valid; the message is the engine's, and names the setting and its range: `replicates is a whole number of at least 1, got 0`, `sd is a finite number greater than 0, got 0`. A count gives one message for every value outside its range, a negative one included, also when a binding is called with no Python object in between, and for `Simulation.replicates` (`count is a whole number of at least 1, got 0`) and `Calibrator.run` (`starts is a whole number of at least 1, got 0`). A seed outside its range gives `seed is a whole number from 0 to 18446744073709551615, got -1` in every function that takes one: `Simulation.run`, `Simulation.run_at`, `Simulation.replicates`, `CalibrationProblem`, `SensitivityAnalysis` and each binding.
- The engine holds the rule of every value of a model and of every window. An initial amount, an impulse and the points of a series fail when their object (`Aggregate`, `Transition`, `SeriesValue`) is built or an amount is updated, as before, and the same values are valid; the message is the one the model compiler gives, which names the bin, the compartment or the transition: `Bin 'B': initial amount is a finite number of at least 0, got -1`, `Transition 't': impulse period is a finite number greater than 0, got 0`, `a series has one point per position, got two at 2`. The windows of `windowed_totals`, of reports, of figures and of `AxisUnits.window_start`, `window_end`, `window_index` and `window_ends` come from the engine, with its messages (`window is a finite number greater than 0, got 0`, `index is a whole number of at least 0, got -1`), and an observation or a quantity whose window starts before 0 gives `the window 4 that ends at 3 starts before 0; an end is at least its window`. A `tick_every` of a figure that is not a finite number greater than 0 raises `ValueError`.
- A calibration, a sensitivity analysis or any other method that sets a model parameter raises `ValueError` when it is built if the parameter is a formula or a series parameter. The engine computes such a parameter at each step, so a value set on it was lost and the method fitted nothing. The message is the engine's, for this case and for a parameter the model does not have: `Parameter 'k9' is not in the model; the parameters that can be set are k1, k2`. Python keeps no copy of this check.
- The four engines of the aggregate kind name themselves in their messages by the name of the engine: a position an engine does not report at gives `The DifferenceEquations engine reports only at integer steps; 2.5 is not one`, and an impulse or a series point between two steps names `the DifferenceEquations engine` or `the StochasticSteps engine`.
- `Predictive.at_observations` and every method that reads a predictive at other observations raise `ValueError` for a position the engine rejects, with the message of the engine, as a calibration does. The bands, the automatic block lengths and their estimates keep their values: one Rust function of each computes them for every method.
- The engine decides the practical verdicts of `Collinearity` and `SampleIdentifiability` and the two notes of a profile on its refits, and results read a position with the rule of an observation: the verdicts, reasons, notes and values stay. `windowed_totals` reads each window as a calibration reads a windowed observation, and it gives floats. A figure asked for a series that is neither an output nor a bin or accumulator raises `KeyError` with the message of `Simulation.outputs_for`, and a sum of outputs that the results do not hold gives one message, `Missing output series in results`, in a simulation, a report and a figure.
- The engine checks a model, a calibration and the engine settings, and Python repeats none of its checks, so each mistake gets the message of the engine. A parameter named after an engine variable, a bin, a compartment or a subgroup total names each conflict and asks to rename the parameter. An observation of an output the model does not have names the output, the observation and the outputs: `Invalid observed output name 'X' for observation 'series1' (available: A, B, C)`. A factor with a bound of 0 or below fails with `Factor parameter 'f' must have positive bounds (got min=0, max=2)`. `Collinearity` checks `max_subset_size` when it runs, with `max_subset_size must be from 2 to the number of parameters (3), got 9`. The needs of a stochastic engine (`replicates`, `seed` and `replicate_summary` of a calibration; `replicates` and `seed` of a sensitivity analysis) keep their messages, which the engine now gives.
- `ODESolver` and `StochasticEventsSettings` take their defaults from the engine and check themselves with the engine when they are built: `StochasticEventsSettings(epsilon=1.5)` gives `epsilon is strictly between 0 and 1, got 1.5`. Every other setting strictly between 0 and 1 (`target_cess`, `stay_probability`, `min_acceptance`, the `quantile` of `ABCRejection`, `correlation_threshold`) gives `<name> is strictly between 0 and 1, got <value>`, `Quantile(1.5)` gives `A quantile level is between 0 and 1, got 1.5`, and a Sobol analysis of the Rust API with fewer than 2 draws says `draws`, the name of the setting.
- A negative count that reaches the engine, such as `Simulation.run(-1)`, the `replicates` of a `SensitivityAnalysis` or the `max_subset_size` of `Collinearity`, raises `ValueError` that names the setting, `num_steps is a whole number from 0, got -1`, in place of an `OverflowError` with no name. Every count of the bindings reads this way.
- The engine draws a seed that its user does not set, in one place, and the result gives the seed it ran with, as before: `results.seed`, `SimulationReplicates.seed`, `Calibrator.seed` and `SensitivityAnalysis.seed`. A calibrator with no seed logs the seed it drew when it is built, not when it first runs.
- Ruff checks that every signature of the package has annotations and that none is `typing.Any`; the raw input of a validator is a `JsonValue`. A keyword that `Quantile`, `Groups`, `Level` or `Increments` does not take raises `TypeError` that names it, such as `Quantile(0.5, unknown=1)`, in place of the `ValidationError` `Extra inputs are not permitted`. A `ParameterSample` whose `names`, `bounds` or `values` are not valid gets the pydantic message of that field before the engine checks the log weights.
- A calibration and every fit of a replicate of a bootstrap, the jackknife, a profile threshold or a conformal method run their starts with one rule: the engine chooses the best start, the first of lowest loss, and the seed gives the Latin hypercube and the seed of each start from two streams of its own. So a calibration with a seed, its structural rank and its fits of replicates give other values than in 0.10.1; a run stays reproducible from its seed on one version. When every start fails, the message lists the reason of each start, also in the message of a replicate that fails.
- A particle swarm draws its numbers with the generator of commol from the seed of its start, which a calibration always gives: a verbose calibration with a swarm is the calibration without `verbose`, and `Calibrator.run_with_history` is start 0 of `Calibrator.run`.
- The summaries of `PropagationResult`, of the scenarios and of `member_statistics`, the effective size of a propagation and the densities of observation models and priors keep their values: one Rust function computes each, and Python calls the summary as `commol_rs.inference.weighted_summary`. The error of a `Laplace` fit on its bound points to `ProfileLikelihood` and cites no issue.
- `BootstrapCoverageEta` takes `η` with the one quantile of commol, the one of `weighted_quantiles`, on the logs of the thresholds, so `η` changes once. It needs at least `1/(2(1 − c))` replicates times parameters, where it needed `1/(1 − c) − 1`.

### Fixed

- A fraction of a stratification outside 0 to 1 raises `ValueError` when its `Aggregate` is built, with the message of the engine: `Stratification 'g', category 'g1': fraction is a number from 0 to 1, got 1.5`. Before, only the sum was checked, so fractions such as `{"g1": 1.5, "g2": -0.5}` built a model whose compartment started at a negative amount. The sum of the fractions of a stratification, 1 within 1e-6, is checked at the same time (`Stratification 'g': the fractions of its categories sum to 1 within 1e-6, got 0.9`), where it was checked by `build`, and `update_stratification_fractions` and the model compiler give the same messages.
- Two results of commol with the same values are equal, also when they hold a NaN: a NaN equals a NaN, whatever the objects that hold it. Before, `==` compared the identity of the items of a list first, so two runs with one seed gave results that were not equal when one held a NaN, such as a PRCC coefficient of an input that the other inputs explain entirely. A frozen result has a hash that agrees with `==`, also when it holds a list, a dict or a NaN. `ParameterSample` compares as every other result. A result no longer compares its private attributes ([Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/#comparing-results)).
- `==` of `SimulationResults` and `SimulationReplicates` now also compares their positions, seed and model, and a NaN equals a NaN. Before, it read only the values, so two runs at other positions or with other seeds and the same values were equal, and two runs with one seed that held a NaN were not. A plain `dict` or `list` with the same values is no longer equal to a result: compare `dict(results)` to read the values only ([Running Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#results)).
- A profile reads a parameter with one finite bound, such as `[0, +∞)`, on its bound within `1e-8` of `max(1, |bound|)`, the rule of `Laplace`. Before, every value of such a parameter was on its bound, so a profile never saw the ridge leave the box through it, and the structure of a flat profile gave `undetermined="on_bound"` with that parameter in place of a reading.
- A window whose start rounds to just below 0, such as a window of `1000 + 1e-7` that ends at 1000, starts at 0 in an observation, a calibration and a quantity, as `windowed_totals` reads it. Before, a calibration rejected it while the same window that ends at 2000 was accepted. One rule of the engine gives the start of a window.
- Two neighbouring seeds share no replicate: before, replicate `i + 1` of `simulation.replicates(n, seed=42)` was replicate `i` of `seed=43`, and so were the starts and the swarms of a calibration with neighbouring seeds. Two methods that take one seed no longer draw from one sequence either: every random method draws from a stream of its own of the seed, and with one seed, replicate `i + 1` of a bootstrap no longer has the generator of particle `i` of an SMC sampler, nor the draws of `Laplace` the design of a sensitivity analysis. Every method draws with the samplers of the one generator of commol. So with one seed, the draws of the random methods and the replicates of a stochastic engine differ from 0.10.1; a run stays reproducible from its seed on one version.
- One check of the engine defines the language of formulas, the one [Mathematical expressions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/mathematical-expressions/index.md) documents, for rates, formula parameters, calibration constraints and the unit check. A formula outside it fails when it is added, with a message that names the formula and its first part outside the language. Before, `k1 * (step > 30)` was accepted as a formula parameter, and `step > 1` as a rate became a parameter named `step > 1` that failed only when the model ran. A formula that calls a function the guide does not list, such as `erf`, `fma` or `trunc`, fails as a rate always did; a formula parameter accepted it before.
- A rate or a formula parameter that reads a variable the model does not define fails when the model is built. Before, only a transition rate was checked, and a formula parameter failed when the model ran. A category id is not a variable: before, a rate that read one passed the build and failed when the model ran.
- An error of a rate when the model runs names its transition, not the indices of its compartments.
- `SecurityConfig.max_complexity_score` limits the number of nodes of the tree of a formula (numbers, variables, operators and calls), as the guide documents. Before, it limited nothing.
- The unit check reads `^` as a power, as the engine does, and `cbrt` takes the cube root of a unit.
- A formula with a long chain of terms, such as a sum of 20 000 terms, no longer stops the Python process with a segmentation fault. The engine reads formulas with a parser of its own: a sum or a product of any length is one level, and a formula that nests deeper than 100 levels of parentheses, calls, signs and powers fails with a message that names the limit. Before, the parse used one step of the stack for each term, and the process crashed near 20 000 terms, or near 2 000 on a thread of the parallel work.
- A chain of powers groups from the right, as in Python: `2 ** 3 ** 2` is 512. Before, it was 64, `(2 ** 3) ** 2`.
- `ParticleSwarmConfig.inertia("constant")` and `.acceleration("constant")` take the weight and the coefficients of canonical particle swarm, `1/(2 ln 2)` and `0.5 + ln 2`, which a swarm with no inertia or acceleration strategy uses. Before, their defaults were the rounded `0.721` and `1.193`, so a swarm that named the constant strategy moved a little differently from one that did not.
- Three messages of a calibration with observation models no longer hold a run of spaces in the middle of a sentence.

## [0.10.1] - 2026-10-23

This release ships the fixes of the audit at 0.9.0 that change no API. In the `StochasticEvents` engine, a parameter or a seed changed between two runs acts from the position where the first run stopped. The documentation reads as one account of the library and names no application field, and commol no longer installs `cffi`. CI runs with read rights and pinned tools, and the test suite checks its own layout. Nothing breaks: code that runs on 0.10.0 runs on 0.10.1. See [Stochastic engines](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/stochastic/index.md) and the [Quickstart](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/quickstart/index.md).

### Removed

- `cffi` is no longer a dependency of commol: no code of commol uses it, so `pip install commol` no longer installs it. Code that imports `cffi` installs it itself.

### Fixed

- In the `StochasticEvents` engine, a parameter or a seed changed between two runs acts from the position where the first run stopped. The pending wait is drawn again from there, and a pending leap keeps only its events up to there, by binomial thinning. Before, the new rate acted back from the last event, and copies of one state with new seeds shared their next event. In Python this changes only `simulation.engine.set_seed` between two calls of `simulation.engine.step()`; `Simulation.run`, replicates and calibration reset the engine after the seed, so their results do not change.
- The documentation and the docstrings name no application field, as [Conventions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/conventions/index.md) asks: the dispersion of `NegativeBinomialObservations` is "the dispersion `k` (`size` in R)", and bins of different units are "a count and a concentration". A test checks the words of the user pages and of the source of `commol`.

### Documentation

- The documentation reads as one account of the library: the home page, the quickstart and the examples show one process run by several engines, then calibration, uncertainty, the comparison of runs and parallel work, and the guide follows that order. Each rule lives in one page and the others link to it; a test checks that every page is in the navigation and that no text repeats across pages. The API reference names every name of `commol.__all__` and the module of each name that the root does not export. The maintainer pages name the paths, symbols and tests of the code, and the design note of per-compartment initial conditions is part of [Initial conditions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/decisions/initial-conditions/index.md).

## [0.10.0] - 2026-10-23

This release makes equivalent things the same across commol, after an audit of the code, the repository and the documentation at 0.9.0. A setting that means the same thing has one name, every method takes its seed from its source and fits from its starts, equivalent results hold their failed fits in one place, equivalent methods raise one error type, a replicate summary takes the one quantile of commol, and commol adds no log handler. Before you upgrade, read each **Breaking** entry: most code changes only the names of settings and the type of an exception. See [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/index.md) and [Log messages](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/quickstart/#log-messages).

### Added

- `Laplace`, `Sandwich`, `InformationMatchingEta` and `BootstrapCoverageEta` take `starts`, at least 1 with the default 1: their fit is the best of `starts` starts, `Calibrator.run(starts)`, as in every bootstrap, jackknife, conformal method and profile. Code that does not pass it runs as before. See [Local Approximations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/local/#laplace-approximation-and-the-delta-method) and [What `η` means](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/smc/#what-means).

### Changed

- **Breaking:** every uncertainty and identifiability method takes its random numbers from the seed of its source, `Calibrator.seed` (`problem.seed`) or `SensitivityAnalysis.seed`, and has no seed of its own. Remove `seed=` from `StructuralRank` and from `scores.pit`, and set `problem.seed` (or the seed of the analysis) to choose the random numbers. The PIT randomizes ties from a stream of the seed of its draws, so its values at tied draws change for the same seed. See [Scores](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/#scores).
- `LaplaceMixture.starts` defaults to 1.
- **Breaking:** every uncertainty, identifiability and sensitivity method raises one exception for one kind of error: `ValueError` when a setting, an input, the data or the model does not fit the method, and `RuntimeError` when a computation that could start fails (an engine run, an optimizer, every replicate, a sampler that stops before its target). An input error of an SMC method, a bootstrap, the jackknife or a profile that raised `RuntimeError`, such as a loss of 0 at the fit or a fit outside the support for `BootstrapCoverageEta`, now raises `ValueError`. Catch `ValueError` for these errors where your code caught `RuntimeError`. See [Design decisions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/decisions/uncertainty/#methods-raise-one-error-type).
- **Breaking:** a setting that means the same thing has one name in every method. The level of an interval is `confidence_level`, a count is a plain plural noun, and the rule that combines the replicates of a ratio is `replicate_rule`. An old name raises a `ValidationError` that names it as not permitted. Rename each old name in your code:

| Where                                                                                    | Before                      | Now                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `SplitConformal`, `RollingConformal`, `JackknifePlus`, `EnbPI`, `AdaptiveConformal`      | `level=`                    | `confidence_level=`                       |
| `ConformalResult.intervals` (`PredictionIntervals`), and its report block                | `.level`, `"level"`         | `.confidence_level`, `"confidence_level"` |
| `Threshold`, `Threshold.chi_square`, `Threshold.beale`, `Threshold.bootstrap_calibrated` | `level`                     | `confidence_level`                        |
| `ProfileSection` (`IdentifiabilityReport.profile`)                                       | `.level`                    | `.confidence_level`                       |
| `ParticleSwarmConfig`                                                                    | `num_particles=`            | `particles=`                              |
| `Sobol`                                                                                  | `base_draws=`, `bootstrap=` | `draws=`, `replicates=`                   |
| `Ratio`                                                                                  | `replicates=`               | `replicate_rule=`                         |
| `Simulation.replicates`, `ReplicateRuns`                                                 | `n`                         | `count`                                   |

See [A setting has one name and one check](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/decisions/results/#a-setting-has-one-name-and-one-check).

- One check, in Rust, rejects a confidence level that is not strictly between 0 and 1, with one message in every method: `confidence_level is strictly between 0 and 1, got 1.5; use 0.95 for a 95% interval`. Every other setting strictly between 0 and 1 (`target_cess`, `stay_probability`, `min_acceptance`, the `quantile` of `ABCRejection`, `correlation_threshold`) says `<name> is strictly between 0 and 1, got <value>`.
- **Breaking:** a calibration with `replicate_summary=Quantile(q)` compares the observations with the one quantile of commol, the one of `weighted_quantiles`, `SimulationReplicates.quantiles` and every interval (NumPy's `method="hazen"` with equal weights), instead of NumPy's default `linear` quantile. `Quantile(0.25)` of the replicates 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 is now 1.75, not 2.0. So for `q` other than 0.5 the loss and the fitted values change slightly; `"median"` and `Quantile(0.5)` do not change. Your code does not change; run again a calibration with `Quantile(q)` whose result you stored. See [One confidence-interval convention](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/decisions/results/#one-confidence-interval-convention).
- **Breaking:** results that hold the same thing hold it in the same place, under the same name. Every result of a method that fits several times lists each fit that failed in `failed`, `"<Start|Replicate|Block|Origin> <index> failed: <reason>"`, logged as a warning, and counts the fits kept although their optimizer did not converge in `not_converged`. Change your code:

| Before                                                                                                     | Now                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CalibrationResult.failed_runs`                                                                            | `CalibrationResult.failed`                                                                                                       |
| `BootstrapResult.diagnostics.failed`, `.diagnostics.not_converged`                                         | `BootstrapResult.failed`, `.not_converged`                                                                                       |
| `JackknifeResult.diagnostics.failed`, `.diagnostics.not_converged`                                         | `JackknifeResult.failed`, `.not_converged`; an entry names the block by its index from 0, `"Block 2 failed: …"`, not by its span |
| `ProfileResult.failed_replicates`                                                                          | `ProfileResult.failed`, and the new `ProfileResult.not_converged`                                                                |
| The failed refits of `RollingConformal`, `JackknifePlus` and `EnbPI`, only logged as `"Refit i failed: …"` | `ConformalResult.failed` and `ConformalResult.not_converged`                                                                     |
| The failed replicates of `BootstrapCoverageEta` in `GibbsResult.diagnostics.notes`                         | `GibbsResult.failed`                                                                                                             |
| `ProfileResult.report()`                                                                                   | `ProfileResult.identifiability()`; its `report()` gives the data                                                                 |
| `sample.effective_size()`                                                                                  | `sample.effective_size`, a property, as on every other object                                                                    |

When a method has fewer successful fits than it needs, its `RuntimeError` says how many of how many fitted, how many it needs, and the first reasons, and names the unit: `"Only 1 of 5 blocks fitted, and the method needs 2; …"`. It says `"Every origin failed: …"` (or replicate, block) only when none fitted. The jackknife and jackknife+ no longer say that every replicate failed when one fit succeeded. See [Resampling](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/resampling/#the-result).

### Removed

- **Breaking:** `commol.add_stderr_logger` is removed: commol configures no logging, and adds only a `NullHandler` to the logger `commol`. Call `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` instead, or add a handler of your own to `logging.getLogger("commol")`. See [Log messages](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/quickstart/#log-messages).

### Fixed

- `IdentifiabilityReport.report()` gives the `profile` section, the evidence of each profile likelihood; before, the report data had no such section.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-10-22

This release gives control over the work of a calibration and over what a result records. `commol.threads(n, levels)` sets how many threads the parallel methods use and which levels run in parallel, a particle swarm can stop when it has converged, a polynomial chaos takes a truncated basis for many inputs, and `Ratio` gives a sensitivity analysis the ratio of two quantities. A calibration result records its seed, and `commol.build_info()` names the version and the commit of the package. Before you upgrade, read the **Breaking** entry: `CalibrationResult` requires `seed`. See [Parallelism](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/parallelism/index.md) and [Sensitivity Analysis](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/index.md).

### Added

- `PolynomialChaos(q_norm=..., max_interaction=...)`: a truncated basis for many inputs. `max_interaction` keeps the terms of at most that many inputs, and `q_norm`, in `(0, 1]`, the terms whose degrees have `Σ α_i^q ≤ degree^q`; the defaults keep the total-degree basis. 20 inputs at degree 4 with `max_interaction=2` have 1,221 terms instead of 10,626, and the number is known before any run. `ChaosResult` records both. See [Bases for many inputs](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/#bases-for-many-inputs).
- `ParticleSwarmConfig.improvement_stop(window=..., tol_abs=..., tol_rel=...)` and `ParticleSwarmConfig.radius_stop(tol)`: a particle swarm stops when its best loss improved by at most `tol_abs + tol_rel·|best loss|` over the last `window` iterations, or when every particle is within `tol` of the best position, as a fraction of the size of the search box. Both are off by default and have no default values. A run that stops by a rule reports `converged=True`, so a profile that holds a prediction with a swarm also converges. See [Stop rules](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-optimizers/#stop-rules).
- `commol.set_threads(n)`, the context manager `commol.threads(n, levels)`, `commol.get_threads()` and `commol.get_levels()` choose the number of threads of every parallel method and the levels that run in parallel. The setting holds per Python thread (`contextvars`); without it, commol uses one thread per core. A particle swarm scores the particles of each iteration in parallel, in the order of the particles, with `levels="all"`, the default; `levels="outer"` keeps them in order. A seed gives the same result, history included, with any number of threads and either level. See [Threads and Parallelism](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/parallelism/index.md).
- A calibration result records the seed it used, `CalibrationResult.seed` (`Calibrator.seed`: `problem.seed`, or the seed the calibrator drew), and the sample of every uncertainty method and of `Calibrator.point_sample` names it in `method.settings["seed"]`. Set as `problem.seed`, it repeats the run, also from a result read back from JSON. See [Reproducibility](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-optimizers/#reproducibility).
- `commol.__version__` gives the installed version, and `commol.build_info()` gives a `BuildInfo` with the version and the full commit the extension was built from (`None` when the source has no git metadata, such as a source distribution). A build that is not a release, such as an install from a git commit, names its commit as a PEP 440 local version: `0.1.0+g<first 7 characters of the commit>`. See [Check the installation](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/getting-started/installation/#check-the-installation).
- `Ratio(numerator, denominator, replicates)` is a quantity of interest: one `ValueAt`, `Gain` or `Peak` over another, in each run, so PRCC, Morris, Sobol and a polynomial chaos read a ratio whose denominator depends on the inputs. `replicates` is required: with a stochastic engine, a point of a design holds the mean of the ratios (`"within"`), the mean of the ratios of the replicates with a positive denominator (`"within_positive"`) or the ratio of the means (`"pooled"`). A denominator of 0 makes the ratio of a run NaN, and every method follows the NaN rule. See [A ratio of two quantities](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/#a-ratio-of-two-quantities).

### Changed

- The tolerance of a profile under a particle swarm with the improvement stop rule is the improvement the rule allows at the fit, `tol_abs + tol_rel·|objective at the fit|`; without that rule it stays `1e-6·max(1, |objective at the fit|)`. See [Verdicts](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/profiles/#verdicts-and-the-identifiability-report).
- The parallel methods run in a thread pool of commol, not in the global pool of `rayon`: the environment variable `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` no longer limits them; use `commol.set_threads`. A particle swarm, which scored its particles one after the other, now scores them in parallel by default.
- **Breaking:** `CalibrationResult` requires `seed`; a result saved by an earlier version, or built by hand, needs one to load.

### Fixed

- A particle swarm without `problem.seed` takes the seed the calibrator draws and logs, so that seed repeats it; before, it drew one of its own that no result or log kept.
- A profile that holds a prediction with a particle swarm scores its particles in parallel only when the levels of `commol.threads` are `"all"`, and stops with the error of the first failing particle, as every other swarm does; before, it scored them in parallel at any level and reported the error of any failing particle.

## [0.8.0] - 2026-10-22

This release compares runs. `Scenarios` runs every draw of a sample under several sets of parameter values and compares them in pairs, a quantity of interest reads a series and reduces it (the peak of the gains over windows, for example), and `results.quantities` reads the quantities of one run. Figures are methods of the results they draw: `plot.series`, `plot.observations` and `plot_compared`, which draws several runs or samples on the same panels. Before you upgrade, read the **Breaking** entries: `SimulationPlotter` and seaborn are removed and matplotlib is the optional extra `commol[plot]`, the quantities take a `series`, and the runs of the draws of a stochastic sample follow one tree of seeds, so their numbers change. See [Sensitivity Analysis](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/index.md) and [Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/index.md).

### Added

- `Scenarios(source, sample, scenarios, positions)` runs every draw of a sample under each scenario, a set of parameter values that override those of the model, and is a mapping from the name of a scenario to its `Predictive`. Every scenario runs with the seed of the source, so run `k` of each scenario is the same draw with the same seed (common random numbers). `compare(name, baseline, quantities, confidence_level)` takes the difference of each quantity of interest within each run and reduces the differences with the weights of the runs; `summary` reduces one scenario. Both give a `ScenarioSummary` per label, with no interval when there is one run. `Predictive.quantities(quantities)` gives the quantities of every draw, `Calibrator.point_sample(result)` the point estimate of a fit as a sample of one draw, and `Calibrator.with_model` and `SensitivityAnalysis.with_model` the same source on another model with the same seed. See [Scenarios](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/#scenarios).
- `plot.observations(observed_data, …)` of `SimulationResults`, `SimulationReplicates` and `Predictive` draws one panel per observed series (one `label`), with the model read through the observation operator of each observation: the sum of its `outputs`, its `window` and its factor. A series that sums some outputs, such as `B_g2 + B_g3`, gets its own panel. A value with a window is a step over its window, and the band of replicates or of a predictive (`at_observations(…, NoNoise())`) a rectangle over it; its legend says that it is a band of the model, not a prediction interval. See [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#a-panel-per-observed-series).
- `SimulationResults.quantities(quantities)` reduces one run to its quantities of interest, as `dict[str, float]`, and `SimulationReplicates.quantities(quantities)` gives one such dict per replicate, with the Rust code of `Propagation`. `quantity_schedule` gives the positions to run at; a run that lacks one raises `ValueError` that lists each missing position with its quantity. The guide shows how to take a ratio of two quantities row by row. See [The quantities of one run](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/#the-quantities-of-one-run).
- `plot_compared({label: result}, …)` draws several runs, replicates or predictives of the same model on the same panels: one line per result, labelled with its key and in the same color in every panel, the band of each set of replicates and of each predictive, and the observations once. `window=` draws the gain of each series over each window. A result without the outputs of the first raises `ValueError` that names its key. See [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#compare-results-on-the-same-panels).
- Every figure takes `axes=`, the `Figure` of an earlier figure of commol, and draws each series on the panel of that series: each panel has the id of its series as the label of its `Axes`. A series with no panel raises `ValueError` that names it. See [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#several-results-on-one-figure).
- A quantity of interest reads a series and reduces it. The series is a name or a list of names, their `Level`, or `Increments(outputs, window)`: the gain of their sum over each window that ends at a position. So `Peak(series=Increments("acc", window=7), positions=ends)` is the largest gain of `acc` over a window of 7, and `PeakPosition` with the same arguments the end of that window, with no class of their own. `commol` exports `Level` and `Increments`. See [Quantities of interest](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/#quantities-of-interest).
- `PropagationResult.where(mask)` keeps the runs where `mask` is true and renormalises their weights to sum to 1, and `PropagationResult.effective_size` gives Kish's effective size of the weights. A filter conditions the result on the condition of the mask.
