- `plot_compared(…, panels="observations")` draws one panel per observed series (one `label` of `observed_data`), with each result read through the observation operator of each observation, as `plot.observations` reads one result: the steps, markers and band of each result in the color of its key, and the observations once. The default, `panels="series"`, draws one panel per series. See [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#compare-results-on-the-same-panels).

### Changed

- **Breaking:** each figure is a method of the results it draws, and `SimulationPlotter` is removed. Each figure returns the matplotlib `Figure`. A predictive gives its own figures, so no `Simulation` is built only to draw it. See [Plotting](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/#plotting).

| Before                                                                                                                        | Now                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SimulationPlotter(simulation, results).plot_series(…)`, `.plot_cumulative(…)`                                                | `results.plot.series(…)`, `results.plot.cumulative(…)`                                            |
| `SimulationPlotter(simulation, replicates, confidence_level=c).plot_series(…)`                                                | `replicates.plot.series(…, confidence_level=c)`                                                   |
| `SimulationPlotter(simulation, run, confidence_level=c).plot_series(calibration_result=predictive, …)`, and `plot_cumulative` | `predictive.plot.series(…, confidence_level=c)`, `predictive.plot.cumulative(…)`                  |
| `SimulationPlotter.plot_prcc(result)`, `plot_morris`, `plot_sobol`, `plot_profiles`                                           | `result.plot()` of `PRCCResult`, `MorrisResult`, `SobolResult`, `ChaosResult` and `ProfileResult` |

- **Breaking:** matplotlib draws the figures, and is the optional extra `commol[plot]` (`pip install 'commol[plot]'`); seaborn is no longer a dependency, and `import commol` loads no plotting library. Without matplotlib, a figure raises `ImportError` with the install line. The other keyword arguments of a figure go to `Axes.plot`, not to `seaborn.lineplot`.
- **Breaking:** `PlotConfig.style` takes a matplotlib style or a list of styles, and `PlotConfig` has no `palette` and no `context`. The style sheets of matplotlib give the former values: `style="whitegrid", context="talk", palette="colorblind"` is `style=["seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid", "seaborn-v0_8-talk", "seaborn-v0_8-colorblind"]`. The presets (`presentation`, `publication`, `notebook`) use these sheets.
- **Breaking:** `ValueAt`, `Peak`, `PeakPosition` and `Trajectory` take `series` in place of `outputs`: `ValueAt(outputs="B", at=10)` is `ValueAt(series="B", at=10)`. `Gain(outputs, start, end)` keeps `outputs`, and the outputs of a quantity read back as a list. The quantities live in `commol.context.inference.quantities`, and cross to Rust as the JSON of their classes.
- Every reduction across runs raises `ValueError` on a quantity that is NaN: `PropagationResult.summary()`, `member_statistics`, `weighted_quantiles`, and Morris, Sobol and the polynomial chaos before they estimate, as PRCC did. The message of a method names the quantity, the points where it is NaN, and the point, inputs, replicate and seed of the first such run. `PropagationResult.values` keeps the NaN of each run.
- **Breaking:** the runs of the draws of a sample follow one tree of seeds. Draw `j` of a stochastic `Predictive`, `Propagation`, `at_observations` or score takes a seed of its own, and its replicate `i` takes the seed that replicate `i` of `Simulation.replicates(n, seed=…)` takes from it. Before, the seed of a replicate depended on the number of replicates. So the numbers of these methods with a stochastic engine change from 0.7.0. The runs of a draw no longer change with the number of replicates or of draws, and `Predictive.draw_seeds` and `PropagationResult.draw_seeds` give the seed of each draw: `Simulation.replicates(n, seed=draw_seeds[j])` of the model at the values of draw `j` gives its runs. See [The predictive](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/#the-predictive).

### Fixed

- A NaN in the values a `Peak` or a `PeakPosition` reads makes it NaN. The peak skipped the NaN, and the position of the peak was the first position when the value there was NaN.
- A weighted quantile of values with a NaN raises `ValueError`, where it sorted the NaN by its sign bit and gave a wrong number.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-10-22

This release reads a run through the classes of commol. The axis of a model gives the window grid (`AxisUnits.window_end` and the other methods) and, from a calendar origin, the date of each position. `Simulation.sample`, `total_series` and `windowed_totals` read bins, accumulators and output names, and each report is a method of the object it describes. Before you upgrade, read the two **Breaking** entries: the module functions of the window grid and the report functions are removed, and the table under Changed gives the method that replaces each one. See [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md) and [Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/index.md).

### Added

- `commol.sample(series, positions, at)` reads a series at given positions, and `Simulation.sample(results, ids, at)` reads bins and accumulators by id at given positions, next to `Simulation.windowed_totals`: for example, the amount in a bin at the end of each window. An id stands for all its outputs, summed; an output name stands for itself.
- An axis of time can start at a calendar date: `ModelBuilder(origin=...)` takes a `date` or a `datetime` with no time zone, and `Model.axis_units()` gives `position_of`, `moment_of`, `day_ends` and `week_ends` (weeks that start on a weekday of the caller). `SimulationPlotter.plot_series` labels the ticks of such a model with dates when it has no `position_label`. An origin needs a step unit of time of a whole number of days or a whole fraction of a day: `month` and `year` raise `ValueError`.
- `Simulation.total_series` and `Simulation.windowed_totals` take output names as well as bin and accumulator ids. An output name stands for itself, so `simulation.windowed_totals(results, ["moved_g2", "moved_g3"], 2)` sums two strata of the accumulator `moved`; a bin or accumulator id still stands for all its outputs. An id that is neither raises `KeyError` with the bins, accumulators and outputs of the model.
- The window grid on the axis: `AxisUnits.window_start(index, span, unit)`, `window_end(index, span, unit)`, `window_index(at, span, unit)` and `window_ends(span, unit, end)`, for a window of a span in a unit, such as one week. The width must be a whole number of steps.
- `SimulationResults.model` and `SimulationReplicates.model`: the results of `Simulation.run`, `run_at` and `replicates` hold a reference to their `Model`, and the runs of `Predictive.runs()` the model of its source. A report reads the outputs of each bin and accumulator from it; results with their model still pickle. See [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md).

### Changed

- **Breaking:** the module functions `window_start`, `window_end`, `window_index` and `window_ends` are removed from `commol`. Use the methods of `AxisUnits` (`Model.axis_units()`), with the width as a span and a unit: `window_end(2, 168)` on an axis of hours is `units.window_end(2, 1, "week")`, and a width of 7 steps is `(7, "day")`, or `(7, "step")` when the model declares no step unit.
- **Breaking:** each report is a method of the object whose data it describes, and `commol` exports no report function. The private functions of `api/reporting.py` build the blocks, with the same keys in the same order. See [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md).

| Before                                                                         | Now                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `simulation_report(simulation, results, at, window, num_windows, …)`           | `results.report(positions, window, windows, …)`                                        |
| `simulation_report(…, ensemble_runs=replicates, confidence_level=c)`           | `replicates.report(c, positions, window, windows, …)`                                  |
| `simulation_report(…, ensemble_runs=predictive, confidence_level=c)`           | `predictive.report(c, positions, window, windows, …)`, with no run of a point estimate |
| `applied_parameters_report(model, result, problem, …)`                         | `model.applied_parameters(result, problem, …)`                                         |
| `identifiability_report(report)`                                               | `report.report()`                                                                      |
| `commol.api.reporting.observed_report`, `series_report`, `accumulators_report` | The blocks `observed`, `series` and `accumulators` of a report                         |

## [0.6.1] - 2026-10-22

This release fixes bugs of 0.6.0 and changes no API. A series point or an impulse that the engine cannot run now fails at `ModelBuilder.build` and `Model.update_parameters`, not at `Simulation`. Errors of a `Predictive` draw say what was not feasible. A PRCC analysis with a NaN value raises a `ValueError` and no longer runs forever. The quantities of a sensitivity analysis read a gain at its start and give different labels to close positions. A windowed series is plotted at the position of each observation, and a figure no longer changes the global style of matplotlib.

### Fixed

- The default label of a quantity of interest wrote each position with 6 significant digits, so two positions close together gave one label and the analysis raised `ValueError`: `Trajectory(outputs="A", positions=[1000000, 1000001])` gave `"A at 1e+06"` twice. The label now writes each position in full (`"A at 1000000"`, `"A at 1000001"`).
- `ModelBuilder.build` and `Model.update_parameters` accepted a series point or an impulse position that the engine cannot run, such as a point or an `impulse_at` of 1.5 under `DifferenceEquations` or `StochasticSteps`, or a `"pulse"` point at 1.5 under any engine; the error came only at `Simulation(model)`, as `RuntimeError`. Both now raise `ValueError` with the message of the engine, and a rejected update leaves the model unchanged.
- The `InfeasibleStateError` of a draw of a `Predictive` said only `InfeasibleRun`. It now gives the message of the run after the index of the parameter set: the compartment, the step and the flows, as `Simulation.run` reports them.
- The `InfeasibleStateError` of a draw of a `Predictive` whose initial amounts leave the remainder below zero said only `InfeasibleStart { excess: ... }`. It now gives the message a calibration gives for the same values after the index of the parameter set: what the amounts exceed, the remainder and by how much.
- A `Gain(start, end)` quantity read its start at `end - (end - start)`, which can round away from `start`: `Gain(start=0.1, end=0.4)` read it at `0.09999999999999998`, so on the `DifferentialEquations` engine the gain did not start where `ValueAt(0.1)` reads. A gain now reads its start at exactly `start`.
- `SimulationPlotter.plot_series` read the model of a windowed series with the first window it found, at the window ends of a grid from 0, so with observations at 7.5 and 17.5 no model value sat on an observation and the windows of the other observations were ignored. When the observations of a series have a window, or differ in outputs or factor, the model line, the band of the replicates and the band of a `Predictive` now read each observation through its own operator at its own position, as the loss reads it. Observations with several factors no longer leave the line unscaled or raise `ValueError` with a `Predictive`.
- A figure of `SimulationPlotter` with a `PlotConfig` `style`, `palette` or `context` changed the global style of matplotlib, so every figure drawn with matplotlib after it had the style of commol. The style now applies to the figure of that plot only, and `matplotlib.rcParams` is as it was before the call.
- `PRCC` never returned when a quantity was NaN at a draw. It now raises `ValueError` that gives the index of the quantity and the draws where it is NaN, before it ranks any value.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-10-22

This release adds the first uncertainty methods with a stated model of the data: observation models and their likelihood, the Bayesian posterior and the Gibbs posterior by sequential Monte Carlo, approximate Bayesian computation, priors, local approximations (Laplace, the sandwich and the Laplace mixture), conformal intervals, the profile likelihood and sensitivity analysis with no data. Before you upgrade, read the **Breaking** entries: an `Aggregate` states the initial amount of each bin in the unit of that bin, a `CalibrationProblem` needs a `loss_function`, a `Predictive` takes a `Calibrator`, and public class names write every letter of an acronym in capitals. See [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/index.md).

### Added

- Local approximations through `Calibrator.uncertainty`, on the unbounded scale of the parameters, with a fit on a bound refused: `Laplace(draws)`, the normal `N(θ̂, H⁻¹)` of the observation models, and `Calibrator.delta_band(result, positions, level)`, the band of the outputs by the delta method; `Sandwich(block_length, draws)`, the covariance `H⁻¹ B H⁻¹` with the scores summed over blocks (CR1) and a Student t with `G − 1` degrees of freedom, which needs no noise model and refuses `loss_function="mae"` and too few blocks; `LaplaceMixture(starts, draws, target)`, a Laplace approximation at each optimum of a multi-start fit as the proposal of Pareto-smoothed importance sampling of a `LikelihoodTarget(priors)` or `GibbsTarget(priors, eta)`, which reports `k_hat` and marks a sample with `k_hat > 0.7` as unreliable. `curvature` is `"gauss_newton"` (the expected Fisher information of each observation model, by default) or `"hessian"`. See [Local Approximations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/local/index.md).
- `GibbsPosterior`: the Gibbs posterior `prior(θ) · exp(−η · loss(θ))` of the problem's loss, sampled by sequential Monte Carlo from the priors to the posterior; it returns a `GibbsResult` with the `η` it ran with. `eta` is required: a number above 0, `InformationMatchingEta(block_length)` (the curvature of the sum of squares or of observation models against the variance of the scores of its terms summed over blocks, with a deterministic engine) or `BootstrapCoverageEta(replicates, block_length, confidence_level)` (any loss), joined in the union `Eta`. See [Sequential Monte Carlo](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/smc/#gibbs-posterior).
- `ABCSMC` and `ABCRejection`: approximate Bayesian computation on a required distance, `LossDistance()` or `SeriesDistance(metric)`. With a stochastic engine each distance reads one fresh replicate of its particle, so the problem's `replicates` and `replicate_summary` do not apply, and the result says so. See [ABC](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/smc/#abc).
- `SMCResult`: the sample, the level of each step, the log evidence, the value each particle keeps and the diagnostics of each step (`SMCDiagnostics`: effective size, resampling, acceptance rate and move count).
- Priors: `Uniform()`, `LogUniform()`, `Beta(a, b)`, `Normal(mean, sd)`, `LogNormal(mu, sigma)` and `Gamma(shape, rate)`, each truncated to the bounds of its parameter, and `Priors` (a mapping of parameter to distribution, or `Priors.uniform_on_bounds()`). Every sampling method takes `priors` with no default, and a prior whose bounds do not fit raises a `ValueError` that names the distributions that fit them. Their draws are the same on every platform. See [Priors](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/smc/#priors).
- `SampleIdentifiability(reference="prior", priors=...)`: the contraction of each parameter against its prior. See [Identifiability](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/identifiability/#a-sample).
- Conformal prediction intervals through `Calibrator.uncertainty`: intervals for observations with a coverage guarantee that needs no noise model, no prior and no correct model. `SplitConformal` scores held-out observations; `RollingConformal` gives intervals ahead of the data, one quantile per horizon (the `k`-th observation after an origin); `JackknifePlus` refits once per block left out, with the CV+ bound for blocks of more than one observation; `EnbPI` draws its own replicates of blocks for series with dependent errors; `AdaptiveConformal` walks a stream of new observations with a working level that moves with each miss. Each takes a required `score` (`"absolute"`, `"normalized"` or `"spread"`), `by` (`"series"` or `"all"`) and `level`, and returns a `ConformalResult` (`PredictionIntervals`, the scores and the guarantee). See [Conformal Prediction Intervals](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/conformal/index.md).
- `SimulationPlotter.plot_series(prediction_intervals=...)` draws the band of conformal intervals, and `simulation_report(..., prediction_intervals=...)` reports them.
- Observation models: `CalibrationProblem(observation_models={series: model})` takes one model per series label, `NormalObservations(sd)`, `LogNormalObservations(sigma, center)` (`center="mean"` or `"median"`, no default), `StudentTObservations(df, scale)`, `PoissonObservations()`, `NegativeBinomialObservations(overdispersion)` (variance `μ + φμ²`) or `BinomialObservations(trials)` (or the new `ObservedDataPoint.trials` of each observation), and the problem fits by maximum likelihood. A noise argument is a number or a calibration parameter of the new type `"noise"`, which never reaches the engine. Observed values outside a model's support raise a `ValueError` that names the observation. A stochastic engine and `normalize_observations` need a loss. See [Observation Models](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/observation-models/index.md).
- `BayesianPosterior`: the posterior of the observation models and its log evidence, on the sequential Monte Carlo sampler. `GibbsPosterior` on observation models is the fractional posterior `prior · L^η`.
- `DistributionNoise()`: prediction intervals that draw from the observation models; `commol.scores.log_score`, the log density of held-out observations under the predictive, which needs `DistributionNoise()`.
- `ParametricBootstrap(replicates)`: fits to data sets drawn from the observation models at the fit. `ResamplingDiagnostics.block_length` is `None` for it.
- A model can hold bins of different units, such as a count and a concentration: each bin starts at an amount in its own unit, a model whose bins all start at `0` builds and runs, and the `Calibrator` rejects an initial-condition remainder whose unit is not the unit of a calibrated amount. See [Bins of different units](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/building-models/#bins-of-different-units).
- Sensitivity analysis with no data: `SensitivityAnalysis(simulation, inputs, replicates=None, seed=None).run(method)`, the third entry point of the registry, with methods that subclass `SensitivityMethod[R]`. What varies is an `InputSpace` of calibration parameters (model parameters or initial conditions): independent distributions (`InputSpace.independent`, `InputSpace.uniform_on_bounds`) or a weighted sample (`InputSpace.from_sample`). Each run is reduced in Rust to quantities of interest: `ValueAt`, `Gain` (as an observation with a window), `Peak`, `PeakPosition` and `Trajectory`. With a stochastic engine `replicates` and `seed` are required; a point of a design holds the mean of its replicates on common seeds, and a propagation keeps every replicate. See [Sensitivity Analysis](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/sensitivity/index.md).
- `Propagation`: the draws of the inputs and the quantities of each run (`PropagationResult`, with `summary(confidence_level)`); its sample gives the bands of a `Predictive`, which runs the same replicates.
- `PRCC`: partial rank correlation coefficients and their p-values (`PRCCResult`), weighted for a sample, with Kish's effective size in the test.
- `Morris`: elementary effects, `mu`, `mu_star` and `sigma` (`MorrisResult`), on levels at the centres of strata of equal probability.
- `Sobol`: first-order and total indices on the design of Saltelli, with bootstrap intervals (`SobolResult`).
- `PolynomialChaos`: a Legendre expansion of `F(x)`, its leave-one-out error, its Sobol indices and `predict` as a surrogate (`ChaosResult`); the number of terms is checked before any run.
- `SimulationPlotter.plot_prcc`, `plot_morris` and `plot_sobol`.
- `ProfileLikelihood(parameters, threshold, max_steps)`: the profile of each parameter, refitted with the problem's own optimizer at values that step away from the fit by the adaptive step of Raue et al. (2009), its pointwise interval and its verdict (`identifiable`, `practically_non_identifiable`, `structurally_non_identifiable`), in a `ProfileResult`; `ProfileResult.report()` gives the verdicts as an `IdentifiabilityReport` with a `profile` section. A profile is read by resetting the other parameters to their fitted values (`ProfileResult.structure`), against the floor of two evaluations (`ProfileResult.evaluation_floor`): it gives the structural verdict `in_combination` or `non_identifiable`, and names the parameters that compensate it. A crossing made by the bound of another parameter counts as an open side (`Profile.box_crossings`), and `Profile.refit_error` measures the error of a refit at the fit. See [Profile Likelihood](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/profiles/index.md).
- `PredictionProfile(specs, threshold)`: the interval of each prediction (`PredictionSpec`), held at each value as an equality constraint by an augmented Lagrangian. See [Prediction profiles](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/profiles/#prediction-profiles).
- `Threshold.chi_square(level)` (observation models), `Threshold.beale(level)` (a sum of squares of independent Gaussian errors) and `Threshold.bootstrap_calibrated(bootstrap, level)` (any loss, calibrated by the replicates of a bootstrap).
- `SimulationPlotter.plot_profiles`.

### Changed

- Nelder-Mead with an infinite bound fails with the message `Nelder-Mead needs finite bounds`, instead of a rate that is not a number. The sine transform of the bounds and the root finder of the quantiles come from the argmin fork; calibrations, profiles, quantiles and draws give the same results.
- **Breaking:** `InformationMatchingEta(block_length)` takes a required `block_length`, an `int` or `"auto"`: the variance of the scores is summed over blocks of positions, as the meat of `Sandwich`, so it holds under dependence; `block_length=1` gives the independent version. It also takes a problem with observation models, where a correct model gives `η ≈ 1`.
- **Breaking:** `Predictive(source, sample, positions)` takes a `Calibrator` or a `SensitivityAnalysis` (any `PredictiveSource`), and its attribute `calibrator` is now `source`. `Predictive.at_observations` of an analysis takes only `NoNoise()`, and `scores.log_score` refuses its predictive.
- With a stochastic engine, every replicate of every draw of a `Predictive`, of `Predictive.at_observations` and of `scores.log_score` has a seed of its own, derived from the calibrator's seed; before, every draw ran the same replicates of the problem, so a predictive with few replicates showed the same few noise paths for every draw. The bands and scores of a stochastic predictive change; a seed still repeats them.
- **Breaking:** `ModelStructure.check_calibration_values(model, engine, parameters, remainder)` takes the values and the remainder instead of a calibration problem; a model kind that implements it changes its signature.
- A prior whose family does not fit its bounds is named "The distribution ... of" in its message, instead of "The prior ... of".
- The starts of `Calibrator.run(starts=n)` come from the Latin hypercube of `commol-random`; a seed gives the same starts as before.
- **Breaking:** an `Aggregate` states the initial amount of each bin in the unit of the bin, not fractions of one total. A structure that states `total`, `bin_fractions` or `compartment_fractions` is rejected with the fields to use.

| Before                                                        | Now                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"S": 0.99, "I": 0.01})` | `Aggregate(bin_amounts={"S": 990, "I": 10})`                                        |
| `compartment_fractions={"I_g1": 0.005}` (of the total)        | `compartment_amounts={"I_g1": 5}` (in the unit of its bin)                          |
| `model.structure.total`                                       | No declared total: `sum(model.structure.bin_amounts.values())` for bins of one unit |
| `update_bin_fractions({...})`, which kept the sum at 1        | `update_bin_amounts({...})`; the other bins keep their amounts                      |
| `update_compartment_fractions(process, {...})`                | `update_compartment_amounts(process, {...})`                                        |
| `stratification_fractions`                                    | Unchanged: the split of the amount of every bin a stratification applies to         |

- **Breaking:** a calibrated initial condition of a bin, a bin prefix or a compartment is an amount in the unit of its bin, not a fraction of the total; its bounds are amounts too. A category value is still a split. The remainder takes the sum of the amounts the model states less every other compartment, so a bin that no value covers keeps its amount; with a bin left `None`, the remainder holds the sum (`{"S": 1000, "I": None}`). Without a remainder no initial state is infeasible. A remainder below zero is measured as a share of the amounts the values set. The write-back updates the amount of a bin only when the values and the remainder set every compartment of it.
- **Breaking:** `applied_parameters_report` gives an aggregate model the sections `initial_amounts` (`amount`, `unit`, `calibrated`) and `category_splits` (`group`, a list of categories, `fraction`, `calibrated`) in place of `initial_conditions`, with no `total` row. A category split is reported as the fraction of its group, with no rescaling of its interval.
- **Breaking:** a stochastic engine needs a whole amount in each bin, not a whole total, and `largest_remainder` and `random` round within each bin, so a unit never moves to another bin.
- **Breaking:** the description of an aggregate model shows the bin amounts and their units, and the initial state with the unit of each compartment.
- **Breaking (Rust):** `InitialConditions` has `bin_amounts` and `compartment_amounts` in place of `total`, `bin_fractions` and `compartment_fractions`; `CompartmentalEngine::total` is the sum of the amounts the model states; `check_model_values` returns the plan it resolves, and `InitialConditionPlan::coverage` gives the compartments each value sets.
- **Breaking:** `CalibrationProblem.loss_function` has no default: a problem needs `loss_function` or `observation_models`, exactly one, and raises a `ValueError` with both or neither. Write `loss_function="sse"` where a problem relied on the default.
- **Breaking:** public class names write every letter of an acronym in capitals, as PEP 8 asks: `OdeSolver` is `ODESolver`. `EnbPI` keeps the spelling of its authors. See [Conventions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/conventions/#python).

### Fixed

- A `DifferentialEquations` run with `method="tsit45"` whose solution blows up returned NaN with no error. A step that leaves the state not finite now raises `RuntimeError` that names the last position the solver reached, with either method.
- The finite-difference step of a parameter with an infinite bound was infinite, so its sensitivities, identifiability and curvature failed: the width of its bounds now counts as 1 in the step.
- The quantile of a distribution hundreds of orders of magnitude below 1, such as `Beta(0.01, 1)` at `1e-3`, was far from it, so a prior or a draw of such a shape was wrong: when its Newton and halving steps run out, the quantile now bisects the floating-point numbers between the two ends.
- A particle swarm whose first particle had a NaN cost kept no best particle and returned its start point: a NaN cost now counts as the worst.
- A transition whose rate holds `$compartment` dropped `per_compartment`, `accumulators` and the `absolute` of its stratified rates: each transition it expands to now keeps them, so with `per_compartment=True` `$compartment` reads the compartment that flows, and its accumulators count the flow.
- A `Calibrator` on a `Simulation` that had run shared a calibrated bin, bin prefix or remainder across its compartments in the proportions of the last state of the run, so its fit, its uncertainty and its `Predictive` started from a wrong split: they now share it in the proportions of the initial state.
- `Model.update_parameters` wrote each value with no check, so a list of points for a series parameter left a model that `Simulation` could not read, with an error that named no parameter. It now takes a list of points for a series parameter and keeps its mode, or a `SeriesValue` (now in `commol`) with a new mode, and it runs the checks of a new model: a value it cannot take raises `ValueError` at the call, with the id of the parameter, and leaves the model unchanged.
- A `Predictive` at positions out of order failed inside a draw with a `RuntimeError` that named a parameter set: it now raises `ValueError` before any draw runs, with the first pair out of order, as it does for a position the engine rejects.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-10-19

This release replaces the ensemble calibration with uncertainty methods that have a stated meaning. `Calibrator.uncertainty` resamples the data (bootstraps and the jackknife) and returns a `ParameterSample`; a `Predictive` runs its draws, and `commol.scores` scores its bands. `Calibrator.identifiability` tells which parameters the model and the data determine, and `Calibrator.run(starts=n)` fits from several start points. Before you upgrade, read the **Breaking** entries: the ensemble calibration is removed (use `BayesianBootstrap` in its place), and every interval uses one quantile, so the intervals of `member_statistics` and `SimulationReplicates.quantiles` move slightly. See [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/index.md) and [Resampling](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/resampling/index.md).

### Added

- `Calibrator.run(starts=n)` runs the optimizer from `n` start points in parallel and returns the best: the initial guess, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds drawn from the problem's `seed`. `CalibrationResult.starts` lists every start (`StartSummary`: start, end, loss, converged); distinct ends with equal losses show that the data do not identify the parameters. See [Several starts](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/calibration-optimizers/#several-starts).
- `CalibrationResult.failed_runs`: why each failed start failed, also logged as a warning.
- `ParameterSample`: weighted draws of the parameters of a problem, with their invariants checked at construction and weighted statistics computed in Rust (`mean`, `covariance`, `correlation`, `quantiles`, `interval`, `effective_size`, `draws`, `resample`, `summary`). It saves to JSON and loads back equal.
- `Predictive(calibrator, sample, positions)`: the run of every draw, in parallel, its band (`band`, `series_band`) and every draw's value of a set of observations through the observation operator of the loss, with an observation noise that has no default (`at_observations(observed_data, noise)`: `NoNoise()` for a band of the model, `ResidualNoise(...)` for a prediction interval). `SimulationPlotter` and `simulation_report` take a predictive.
- `commol.scores`: empirical coverage, interval score, weighted interval score, the CRPS of a weighted sample and PIT values of a predictive, per observation and per series. Each takes the observation noise, so a band of the model is never scored as a prediction interval by accident.
- `Calibrator.uncertainty(method)`: one entry point for every uncertainty method. A method's configuration subclasses `UncertaintyMethod[R]` and registers its runner; the result type follows the configuration's type.
- `Calibrator.identifiability(method)`: which parameters the model and the data determine, and which combinations they determine in their place. `StructuralRank` (the rank of the sensitivities at random points, on the design of the observations or a dense one), `Collinearity` (Brun's indices at a fit or over a sample), `SampleIdentifiability` (contraction, correlations and modes of a sample) and `StartsIdentifiability` (starts of equal loss that end apart). Each returns an `IdentifiabilityReport` with a structural and a practical verdict per parameter; `merge` joins reports and `identifiability_report` gives one as plain data. See [Identifiability](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/identifiability/index.md).
- `InferenceMethod[R]`, the common base of `UncertaintyMethod[R]` and `IdentifiabilityMethod[R]`; each entry point refuses the other kind with a `TypeError`.
- `weighted_quantiles`, and a `weights` argument for `member_statistics`.
- `CalibrationHistory` and `CalibrationEvaluation`, returned by `Calibrator.run_with_history()`.
- The crate `commol-inference`: the parameter sample, the one quantile, the predictive and the scores. See [Uncertainty](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/index.md).
- Resampling methods with no noise model, through `Calibrator.uncertainty`: `BayesianBootstrap`, `ResidualBootstrap` and `WildBootstrap` return a `BootstrapResult` (the fit, one draw per replicate, diagnostics, and the Monte Carlo error of each interval bound, `interval_error`); `BlockJackknife` returns a `JackknifeResult` (estimate, bias, standard error, pseudo-values and the influence of each block). Blocks of consecutive positions span every series; `block_length` is an integer or `"auto"` (Politis and White). See [Resampling](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/uncertainty/resampling/index.md).
- `ResidualNoise`: observation noise made of blocks of residuals of a fit, which gives a prediction interval with no noise model; `NoNoise` gives a band of the model.
- `CalibrationProblem::with_data` (Rust): a copy of a problem with other observed values and weights.

### Changed

- The `latest` version of the documentation site is the documentation of the last release, published from its tag; the `dev` version follows `main`.
- **Breaking:** every interval uses one quantile: the weighted inverse of the empirical distribution between the midpoints of the cumulative weights, NumPy's `method="hazen"` with equal weights. `member_statistics` and `SimulationReplicates.quantiles` used NumPy's `linear`; their intervals move slightly.
- **Breaking:** `CalibrationResult.best_parameters` keeps the order of `CalibrationProblem.parameters`.
- **Breaking:** `Calibrator.run_with_history()` returns a `CalibrationHistory` instead of the extension's object.
- **Breaking:** `applied_parameters_report(..., sample=, confidence_level=)` reads the statistics of a `ParameterSample`; `parameter_statistics` is gone.
- **Breaking (Rust):** `CalibrationProblem` is split into layers (`ForwardModel`, `ObservationOperator`, `Feasibility`, `Discrepancy`, `OptimizationObjective`); `optimize` takes the problem by reference, and the optimizer configurations have no `verbose` field. `CalibrationEvaluation` has no `predictions`.
- A verbose optimizer writes its table to Python's `sys.stdout` only, and needs one start; the library never writes to the standard error.
- A rate, a formula parameter or a constraint that the expression compiler cannot compile, such as `typeof(k)`, is rejected when the model or the calibration problem is built, with the reason; it no longer fails when it is evaluated.
- The functions `erf`, `erfc`, `tgamma`, `lgamma`, `j0`, `j1`, `y0`, `y1`, `fdim` and `remainder` of a rate come from the `libm` crate, so they give the same values on every platform; the other functions still come from the system's math library.
- `AxisPattern` is abstract: `AxisPattern()` raises `TypeError`. Build a pattern with one of its class methods.
- Error messages that list ids (the stratifications of a transition, the missing and extra keys of the fractions of an `Aggregate`) list them in sorted order.

### Fixed

- Several starts of Nelder-Mead began at the same point: each start now comes from the run seed.
- A parameter value could land on another parameter when results were read by name from an unordered mapping.
- A failed run of a multi-start optimization was written to the standard error and dropped; it is now part of the result.
- An error of the model at a vertex of the initial Nelder-Mead simplex made the optimizer panic; it now stops the calibration with its message (the argmin fork returns the error).
- A `to` condition on a transition without a source was ignored by its flow but applied by its accumulators; `build` now rejects it, and a `category` condition chooses the compartment the flow enters.
- `Model.from_json` read a file in the encoding of the system; it now reads UTF-8, the encoding of JSON.
- `Model.check_unit_consistency` checked every flow of a category transition in the unit of the first bin of the model; each flow is now checked in the unit of its own bin. In a model of bins of different units, a rate that reads `total`, a subgroup total, a category or `neighbors` fails the check: these add amounts of different units.
- The LaTeX description wrote a part of a rate in parentheses, such as `(I / N)` or the argument of `sin(t / T)`, as upright text, and wrote a unit inside the name of another variable (`A_{g1(\text{item})}`); only units are text now, each after its variable. The expanded form merges `k * p` and `k * (1 - p)` also when a third term shares another factor, and a merged term keeps the place of its first term.
- `ModelBuilder` and `Simulation` logged to the root logger of the application; they log to the `commol` logger, as the rest of the library does, so `add_stderr_logger` shows their messages.
- `AxisPattern.combine(mode="max")` raised "Unknown combine mode": a mode may be given by its value.
- A quantile level outside `[0, 1]`, or NaN, gave the smallest or the largest value; `ParameterSample.quantiles` and `weighted_quantiles` now raise `ValueError`.
- `AxisPattern.from_formula` and `AxisPattern.combine` with a `config` that allows formulas longer than the default rejected them anyway; the configuration now applies.
- A rate of `StochasticSteps` that is not a number raised `InfeasibleStateError` and said that a rate cannot be negative; it now raises `RuntimeError`, as `StochasticEvents` does, and says that the rate is not a number.
- A rate that is not a number gave amounts that are not numbers in `DifferenceEquations` and `DifferentialEquations`, and a calibration only penalized the run; the run now stops with `RuntimeError` that names the flow and the position, as in the stochastic engines.
- A rate that read an id with digits, such as `e1`, `E2` or `c1star`, was rejected as a malformed number; and the exponent of a number such as `1e1` was read as the undefined variable `e1`. An identifier now starts only after a character that is not a letter, a digit or `_`, so the digits of an id belong to its name and an exponent belongs to its number.

### Removed

- `commol.api.model_loader.ModelLoader`: a copy of `Model.from_json` that no page documented and nothing called.
- **Breaking:** the ensemble calibration: `Calibrator.run_probabilistic`, `ProbabilisticCalibrator`, `CalibrationProblem.probabilistic_config`, `ProbabilisticCalibrationConfig`, `ProbabilisticCalibrationResult`, `EnsembleSolution`, `EnsembleSelectionSummary`, `ParameterSetStatistics` and their settings classes. Its intervals had no statistical meaning: its members were points the optimizer visited, and the selection maximized the coverage of the data it was fitted to. The closest replacement with no noise model is `Calibrator.uncertainty(BayesianBootstrap(replicates=..., block_length=...))`: the same parallel fits, each on randomly weighted data, with a stated meaning.
- The dependency on `scikit-learn`.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-16

### Added

- `Model.describe(layout="default")` returns a `ModelDescription`: the model as data, sections of tables, equations, state graphs and text, for every kind of model. `render(format)` gives text, Markdown (with the state graph as a Mermaid diagram), a LaTeX document, JSON or Graphviz DOT, and `save(path)` writes it in the format of the suffix (`.txt`, `.md`, `.tex`, `.json`, `.dot`). In a notebook it shows as Markdown. See [Describing a Model](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/describing-models/index.md).
- `layout="odd"`: the description follows the ODD protocol for describing individual- and agent-based models (Grimm et al. 2006, 2010, 2020), and marks what commol cannot fill "To be written by the modeller.".
- `EngineType.dynamics_form` and `EngineType.schedule`: how an engine advances (`difference_equation`, `differential_equation`, `stochastic_events`, `rules`), as a description shows it.
- The process of a model apart from its structure: `Model.process` (`Process`: bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is written once, and `Model.structure` lays it out. `Aggregate` is the structure of amounts per compartment, the kind `aggregate`.
- `neighbors_<bin>` and `neighbors` in a transition rate: the amount of a bin among the neighbors of a unit and their total. A rate that reads them and no compartment is proportional. `Aggregate(neighbors=Complete())` makes every unit a neighbor of every other; `Groups(stratification, weights)` makes units neighbors by the categories of a stratification. A rate that reads them needs `neighbors`, with no default.
- Variants of a structure: a subclass with the same kind, fields and engines, saved with its `variant` and loaded back as its own class.
- Seeds and replicates for stochastic engines: `Simulation.run(…, seed=)` and `run_at(…, seed=)` (`SimulationResults.seed` keeps the seed, drawn when none is given), `Simulation.replicates(n, seed=)` with `run` and `run_at` that return `SimulationReplicates` (runs in parallel, one seed each; `mean`, `quantiles`, `member_statistics`), `Simulation.is_stochastic`, and `EngineType.is_stochastic`. `SimulationPlotter` draws the mean and a band of replicates, and `simulation_report` takes them as `ensemble_runs`.
- `CalibrationProblem(replicates=…, replicate_summary=…)` calibrates a stochastic engine with common random numbers: `"mean"`, `"median"`, `Quantile(q)` or `"crps"` (the continuous ranked probability score). A stochastic engine needs them and a `seed`; there is no default summary.
- The crate `commol-random`: a portable generator (`Xoshiro256PlusPlus`), the derivation of replicate seeds, samplers and a sum tree of rates, for every stochastic engine.
- Two stochastic engines of an aggregate model, in the crate `commol-stochastic`, that run the process of any model as whole units moved at random, with no change to it: `"StochasticEvents"` (continuous time: Gillespie's direct method, exact also when a rate reads `t`, or `method="tau_leaping"`) and `"StochasticSteps"` (the chain binomial, with per-step probabilities). Their settings are `StochasticEventsSettings` and `StochasticStepsSettings`. A total must be whole, and initial amounts that are not whole need `rounding="largest_remainder"` or `"random"`, with no default. A per-step probability outside `[0, 1]`, or probabilities out of one compartment that sum to more than 1, raise `InfeasibleStateError`. See [Stochastic Simulation](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/stochastic/index.md).
- The `dynamics` section of a stochastic model is an event table: each flow, the change of one event and its propensity or its draw; the `schedule` section lists the settings of the engine.

### Changed

- **Breaking:** a model is built from a process and a structure. `ModelBuilder` writes the process, and `build(structure, engine, settings=None)` joins it with a structure; the model is a `Model` of the class of the structure.

| Before                                                                                                                                                                              | Now                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `builder.set_initial_conditions(total=…, bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9}, …], stratification_fractions=[…], compartment_fractions=[…])` then `builder.build(engine=…)` | `builder.build(Aggregate(total=…, bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, …}, stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, …}}, compartment_fractions={"A_g1": 0.0}), engine=…)` |
| `CompartmentalStructure`, `Model[CompartmentalStructure]`                                                                                                                           | `Aggregate`, `Model[Aggregate]`                                                                                                                                     |
| `model.structure.bins`, `stratifications`, `transitions`, `accumulators`                                                                                                            | `model.process.bins`, …                                                                                                                                             |
| `model.structure.initial_conditions.total`, `bin_fractions`, …                                                                                                                      | `model.structure.total`, `bin_fractions`, … (mappings by id)                                                                                                        |
| `model.structure.initial_state()`, `subgroup_total(…)`, `get_conditioning_categories(…)`, `update_compartment_fractions(…)`                                                         | The same methods, with the process first: `model.structure.initial_state(model.process)`, …                                                                         |
| `model.structure.update_initial_conditions(…)`                                                                                                                                      | `model.structure.update_bin_fractions(…)`                                                                                                                           |
| `model.structure.outputs_by_source()`, `series_label(id)`                                                                                                                           | `outputs_by_source(model)`, `series_label(model, id)`                                                                                                               |
| `CompartmentFraction`, `BinFraction`, `StratificationFraction(s)`                                                                                                                   | Mappings in `Aggregate`                                                                                                                                             |
| `CompartmentalEngineType`                                                                                                                                                           | `EngineName`                                                                                                                                                        |

- **Breaking:** the model file has `process` and `structure`, the structure has `kind: "aggregate"` and `variant`, and the fractions are objects keyed by id. A file of 0.3 does not load; rebuild the model and save it again.
- **Breaking:** an engine names a method, not a kind: `EngineType.kinds` replaces `EngineType.kind`, and the error of an engine that does not run a kind lists the engines of that kind.
- **Breaking:** `neighbors` and the names that start with `neighbors_` are reserved: no parameter, bin or accumulator may take them.
- `EngineType.equation_lhs` comes from the form of the dynamics of the engine (`DynamicsForm` in Rust), and returns `None` for an engine without equations.
- Python names follow PEP 8: ruff checks them (`N` rules).

### Fixed

- The unit check reads the flows the engine plans, so a proportional rate is checked as its flow, the rate times its source: `k2` in `1/day` from a bin in `item` passes as `item/day` instead of failing as `1/day`.

### Removed

- **Breaking:** `Model.print_equations`, `ModelStructure.print_equations` and `PrintEquationsOutputFormat`. `model.describe().render("text")` shows the same compact and expanded forms, and `render("latex")` writes them in LaTeX; a description with some units missing shows none instead of raising.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added

- An ODE engine: a model built with `engine="DifferentialEquations"` runs in continuous time, `dX/dt = Σ flows`, integrated by `diffsol` (`commol-differential`). It has the same flows, outputs, accumulators, calibration, ensembles, reports and plots as a difference model. On `[n, n + 1)` a rate sees `step = n` and the continuous `t`. The engine restarts its integration at each integer when a rate reads `step`, and where `t` reaches a value a rate compares it with (`t >= t_on`), so the solver cannot step over a jump.
- `OdeSolver` (`method` `"tsit45"` or `"bdf"`, `rtol`, `atol`), the settings of the `DifferentialEquations` engine, stored in the model as `Model.engine.settings` and set with `build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...)`.
- One list of engines in the Rust engine (`EngineType`): each entry names the model kind it runs, validates its settings, and says the form of its equations and what a rate means (`per_step` or `continuous`). Python asks it through `commol_rs.engine.EngineType` instead of branching on engine names.
- `Simulation.run_at(at)`: the outputs at the given sorted positions. A differential model takes any position, such as `0.5`.
- `SimulationResults`: what `Simulation.run` and `run_at` return. A `dict` from output name to values, as before, with the positions in `positions` and the rows in `rows()`.
- The window grid as module functions: `window_start`, `window_end`, `window_index` and `window_ends`, beside `windowed_totals`.
- A public Pydantic class rejects an unknown field and names it (`extra="forbid"` on every class of `commol.__all__`), so a misspelt or an old name is an error instead of being dropped.
- Impulses: `add_transition(..., impulse_at=[...])` or `impulse_every=(period, offset)` moves the rate (a fraction or an amount) at once at those steps, in both engines, before the flows of the step. `print_equations` lists impulses apart.
- `ModelBuilder(..., step_unit=...)` (`Model.step_unit`): the unit of one step for the unit check, of any single dimension: the axis is the independent variable of the model, which need not be time (for example `"meter"`). Without it, the step unit is `step`, the default increment of any axis.
- `AxisUnits(step_unit, engine)` and `Model.axis_units()`: `steps(value, unit)` converts a value in any unit of the step dimension to steps on `pint` (`3 day` with a step of `hour` is `72.0`; `2 km` with a step of `m` is `2000.0`), and raises, naming both units, for a unit of another dimension. `rate_from_mean_span(span, unit)` and `rate_from_probability(probability, period, unit)` ask the engine what a rate means: the per-step rate for `DifferenceEquations` (`1 - exp(-1/n)`, `1 - (1 - p)^(1/n)`) and the continuous rate for `DifferentialEquations` (`1/n`, `-ln(1 - p)/n`).
- `EngineType.rate_from_mean_span` and `rate_from_probability` in the engine's list (`RateMeaning` in Rust), which hold those formulas.
- The unit check reads `if(condition, a, b)`: both branches share a unit.
- One interface for every kind of model: `ModelStructure`, an abstract base class that the structure of each kind inherits. `Simulation`, `Calibrator`, `ProbabilisticCalibrator`, the reports and `SimulationPlotter` use only it, so another kind (for example an agent network) is a new subclass with its engines in the engine's list. `CompartmentalStructure` is the structure of a compartmental model. A subclass that misses a method cannot be made, and the error names the method.
- An engine runs one model kind, and a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine and both kinds.
- Each kind declares the values calibration may set besides `parameter` and `factor` (`ModelStructure.calibration_value_types`); a compartmental model accepts `initial_condition`. A type the kind does not accept raises an error that names the kind.

### Changed

- **Breaking:** a `DifferenceEquations` step that leaves a compartment below zero (by more than `10⁻¹²` of the total) raises `InfeasibleStateError`, a `ValueError`. The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows out of it. Before, the run went on with negative amounts. A calibration gives such a run a penalty and goes on; any other error of a run still stops it. See [Amounts below zero](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/transitions/#amounts-below-zero).
- **Breaking (Rust):** `SimulationEngine::run_at_positions_into_buffer`, `run_at`, `run` and `step` return `SimulationError` (`Infeasible` or `Failed`) instead of `String`.
- A position on the axis is a `float` everywhere, and the engine alone decides which positions its model type accepts: a difference model integer steps, a differential model any non-negative position. Its error names the observation, constraint, impulse transition or series parameter that holds a rejected position. The engine trait runs only at positions (`run_at_positions_into_buffer`); `run(n)` returns the grid it ran on.
- The engine of a model and its settings are one field, `Model.engine = {type, settings}` (`ModelEngine`), which replaces `Model.dynamics.typology`. The builder takes the engine where it builds, so one builder builds the model for each engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both. A model file saved before has `dynamics.typology` and does not load: move it to `"engine": {"type": …, "settings": null}`.

| Before                                                                                                   | Now                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `builder.build(typology="DifferenceEquations")`                                                          | `builder.build(engine="DifferenceEquations")`                |
| `model.dynamics.typology`                                                                                | `model.engine.type`                                          |
| `commol_rs.difference.DifferenceEquations(model)`, `commol_rs.differential.DifferentialEquations(model)` | `commol_rs.engine.Engine(model)`, the engine the model names |
| - A model is a header, an engine and a `structure`: `Model.structure`, tagged                            |                                                              |
| in JSON by `kind`, replaces `Model.population` and `Model.dynamics`, and the                             |                                                              |
| transitions are held once. `Model` is generic in its structure class:                                    |                                                              |
| `ModelBuilder.build` returns `Model[CompartmentalStructure]`, and                                        |                                                              |
| `Model.from_json` reads the class from the `kind`. The methods that only a                               |                                                              |
| compartmental model has moved to its structure. A model file saved before                                |                                                              |
| has `population` and `dynamics` and does not load: move the fields of                                    |                                                              |
| `population` and `dynamics.transitions` into                                                             |                                                              |
| `"structure": {"kind": "compartmental", …}`.                                                             |                                                              |

| Before                                                                                                        | Now                                                                                    |

| `commol_rs.model.initial_state(model)`, `expanded_outputs`, `transition_flows`                                | they take a `commol_rs.core.CompartmentalStructure`                                    |
| `commol_rs.calibration.check_initial_conditions`                                                              | `check_model_values`                                                                   |
| `commol_rs.calibration.calibrate(…, initial_population_size, …)` and the other calibration functions          | no `initial_population_size`: the engine knows it                                      |

- `applied_parameters_report` returns `parameters` and the sections of the kind of the model; a compartmental model adds `initial_conditions`, with the same keys as before.
- The Rust engine trait (`SimulationEngine`) is the same for every model kind: `compartments`, `state` (was `population`), `set_initial_condition` and `output_labels` moved to `CompartmentalEngine` (`commol-model`), and the engine resolves and writes the values of its kind (`plan_values`, `apply_values`). The initial-condition plan moved from `commol-calibration` to `commol-model`. The crates are not published.
- Names of positions, lengths and counts, and names with more than one meaning. No old name is kept; an old keyword raises an error that names it.

| Before                                                                                                    | Now                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ObservedDataPoint(step=…)`                                                                               | `ObservedDataPoint(at=…)`                              |
| `ObservedDataPoint(window_steps=…)`                                                                       | `ObservedDataPoint(window=…)`                          |
| `ObservedDataPoint(compartment="B")`                                                                      | `ObservedDataPoint(output="B")`                        |
| `ObservedDataPoint(compartment="label", compartments=[…])`                                                | `ObservedDataPoint(label="label", outputs=[…])`        |

| `CalibrationConstraint(time_steps=…)`                                                                     | `CalibrationConstraint(at=…)`                          |

| `windowed_totals(series, window_steps, at_steps)`                                                         | `windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at)`       |
| `window_end_steps(window_steps, num_steps)`                                                               | `window_ends(window, end)`                             |
